title: Christmas Is Good News for the Headline Weary
summary: There’s no better news than the gospel—the message that God sent his Son to die on a cross for our sins and open a way for us to be reconciled to him.
summary_zh: 没有比福音更好的消息了——上帝差遣祂的儿子上十字架为我们的罪而死，为我们开辟了一条与祂和好的道路。
title_zh: 对那些厌倦了头条新闻的人来说，圣诞节是个好消息
content: Read Go on up to a high mountain, O Zion, herald of good news; lift up your voice with strength, O Jerusalem, herald of good news; lift it up, fear not; say to the cities of Judah, “Behold your God!” (Isa. 40:9) Reflect When I first started writing for The Gospel Coalition, my editor told me we were going to report good news. We were going to tell stories of where Christians were helping and the kingdom was advancing. We were going to say, “Behold, church, how God is at work in the world!” Neither of us had a lot of confidence it’d work. We have education and experience in journalism, and we know there’s a reason joy, peace, and cooperation aren’t often featured in articles. Nobody reads those stories. There’s a reason joy, peace, and cooperation aren’t often featured in articles. Nobody reads those stories. That’s not because humans are insensitive monsters. It’s because when we read bad news, our bodies react with fight or flight instincts— studies show our hearts beat faster and our skin begins to perspire. We want to understand or process what’s going on, so we click on the link and read past the headline. When we read good news, on the other hand, we have no physiological response. Heart rates and perspiration levels stay the same. Researchers say it’s the same nonresponse we have when we look at a blank screen. For a long time, I was frustrated with God for creating us this way. Why didn’t he make us able to absorb bad news calmly and react to good news with wild, enthusiastic joy? Wouldn’t that be better? Wouldn’t that make Isaiah’s job easier? And John the Baptist’s? And Jesus’s? Wouldn’t that make the church’s job easier? “Behold your God!” we could say to the world. “Isn’t he amazing? Isn’t it wonderful what he has done for us?” And the secular world would shout back, “Hooray! Praise the Lord!” But that’s not how God did it. And only recently did I begin to spot the beauty in his way. First, it’s right that human bodies react with stress and anxiety to news of sin and brokenness in the world. That’s a sign we were made for another world, one that isn’t steeped in corruption and sadness. It’s a testimony that God himself, the One we image, doesn’t ignore evil. The tension we feel is a tiny shadow of God’s reaction when he sees depravity unfolding across space and time. Second, just because we stay relaxed when reading good reports or stories doesn’t mean we’re unaffected. Studies show that when we hear positive news, we’re not only happier but more likely to take action —to respond with compassion and energy to the world around us. There’s no better news than the gospel—the message that God sent his Son to die on a cross for our sins and open a way for us to be reconciled to him. Our good God offers us not only salvation from our past but purpose for our present and hope for our future. Our good God offers us not only salvation from our past but purpose for our present and hope for our future. This good news changed, and continues to change, the world. Out of grateful joy, Christians have become missionaries, started schools, and adopted children. They’ve moved to broken places, given away their time and money, and forgiven those who sinned against them. They’ve preached the gospel, made countercultural choices, and kept doggedly working long before they saw any fruit. Behold, our God! What marvelous things he has done in us, is doing through us, and has planned for us. Respond Consider your news diet. If good news energizes us, how can you limit your bad news intake or find more good news? How can you keep reminding yourself of the good news of the gospel?

author: Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra

title: The Church Needs to Know Its History
summary: Readers of this first volume of ‘Church History for Everyone’ won’t get a complete understanding of church history, but DeYoung provides a doorway through which ordinary Christians can learn to explore primary sources and more comprehensive surveys on their own.
summary_zh: 阅读《人人适用的教会史》第一卷的读者不会对教会史有全面的了解，但德永为普通基督徒提供了一条途径，让他们学会自行探索原始资料和更全面的综述。
title_zh: 教会需要了解自己的历史
content: Deep in the archives of my Facebook messages sits a note from a widow named Kathy. She thanked me for using church history in our weekly Bible studies. She loved learning about the early-church martyrs and the pilgrims. As a newly minted senior pastor pursuing a PhD in church history, this was the reassurance I needed. Our message thread ended with Kathy describing her chemo treatments. Like Faithful in John Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress (a story new to her that strengthened her fight with cancer), Kathy endured her trials and entered the Celestial City. I usually have to defend the benefits of history to other pastors and friends of mine—but rarely with church members. I mostly encounter excitement when I direct Christians to our family history. In Church History for Everyone: The Story of Christianity from the Fall of Jerusalem to the Dawn of the Reformation , Kevin DeYoung, pastor of Christ Covenant Church and associate professor of systematic theology at Reformed Theological Seminary (Charlotte), blends rich doctrine with a pastoral tone. It’s the first of two planned volumes. DeYoung writes, “I intend this book to be a popular history rather than professional history, which means I am writing to be understood by ordinary people who are eager to learn but are not experts” (3). He’s successful in that effort. I wish Kathy could have read this book; it’s a church history for the church. History for the Church How is church history for the church actually for the church ? Well, words on a page are costly. Just like a pastor needs to cut more of his preparation and study out of his sermons than he’d like, a church history book for everyday Christians needs to value the reader’s attention. This means accepting that not every believer has the bandwidth to process all the names and details from church history we might want him or her to. There’s so much to digest, and the practical value of these names, dates, and specialized terms often don’t stick in the minds of casual readers. It’s easy for the stay-at-home mom or busy mechanic to delve into a church history book and quickly lose steam. On the other hand, oversimplifying in an attempt to make a book more accessible can move an argument from truth and falsehood. The story of our past needs the proper names, dates, and details to lead readers to experience the fruit of good historical learning. DeYoung attempts a near-impossible task: to write an introduction to church history that’s true (factually sound), good (encourages the church), and beautiful (enjoyable to read). He checks those boxes. Biographical Emphasis The most compelling histories are told through people, not periods. That explains why, “instead of a chronological encyclopedia version of history,” DeYoung takes “a biographical approach” (6). We get stories about figures like Irenaeus, Perpetua and Felicity, Athanasius, and Jan Hus. We read of Hus, As a pastor, Hus was passionate and sometimes hotheaded. His sermons also displayed a witty sense of humor. . . . Compared to most men of his age, he was not poor, but neither did he amass any fortune or have family estates to retire to. Even later when his enemies charged him with many faults and crimes, they never charged him with the typical list of priestly sins: drunkenness, sexual immorality, laziness, or opulence. (351) This approach has downsides, of course. A lot of important information gets left out. However, DeYoung recognizes that “when the author tells a story, there is a better chance that the reader might keep reading” (8). The most compelling histories are told through people. The biographical approach reinforces the fact that history often isn’t just about information transfer. “The goal in telling church history has been—for most of church history—a deliberate attempt at inspiration,” DeYoung observes. 我的Facebook留言的档案里 藏着一个叫凯西的寡妇的遗言 她感谢我在我们的每周圣经研究中使用了教会历史. 她喜欢了解早期教会的烈士和朝圣者. 作为一位在教会历史中攻读博士学位的资深牧师,这是我需要的保证。 我们的信息线结束 凯西描述她的化疗。

就像忠实于约翰·邦扬的朝圣者进步(她的新故事加强了她与癌症的战斗)一样,凯西忍受了她的考验并进入了天城。 我通常不得不为其他牧师和朋友捍卫历史利益, 当我把基督徒引向家族历史时,我大多会遇到兴奋。

在《人人教会历史:从耶路撒冷沦陷到改革黎明的基督教故事》中,Kevin DeYoung,基督盟约教会牧师和改革神学院(夏洛特)系统神学副教授,将丰富的学说与牧歌融合在一起。 这是两卷计划书中的第一卷。

DeYoung写道:“我打算这本书是一部受欢迎的历史,而不是专业历史,这意味着我写作是为了让渴望学习但并非专家的普通人理解。” (3)。 他的努力是成功的。 我希望凯西能读到这本书, 教会的历史是怎样的 教会的历史实际上为教会?

嗯,一页上的字是昂贵的。 就像牧师需要从布道中切除更多准备和学习, 这意味着接受并非每个信徒都有带宽来处理我们可能希望他或她处理的教会历史中的所有名字和细节.

这些名称、日期和专门术语的实际价值往往不会停留在临时读者的脑海里。 家庭妈妈或繁忙的技工很容易深入研究教会历史, 另一方面,为了使一本书更容易获得而过分简化,可以使一个论点从真理和谎言中转移出来。

我们过去的故事需要适当的名字,日期,细节,以引导读者体验良好的历史学习成果. DeYoung试图完成一个近乎不可能的任务:写一个教会历史的介绍,这个介绍是真实的(实际上声音),好的(鼓励教会),和美丽的(阅读的乐趣). 他检查那些箱子。

传记重点 最有说服力的历史是通过人们而不是通过时间讲述的。 这解释了为什么“而不是历史的按时间顺序的百科全书版本”,DeYoung采取“一种传记方式”(6)。 我们得到有关伊雷纳厄斯、佩佩图亚和费利西蒂、阿塔纳修斯和扬·胡斯等人物的故事。 我们读到胡斯,作为一个牧师,胡斯是热情的,有时是热头.

他的布道也表现出幽默的幽默感.  . 与他这个年龄的大多数男人相比,他并不贫穷,但他也没有积累任何财富,也没有家庭庄园可以退休. 甚至在后来他的敌人指控他有许多过失和罪行时,他们从未指控他典型的祭司罪列表:醉酒,性不道德,懒惰,或奢侈.

(351) 当然,这种做法有缺点。 很多重要信息被忽略. 然而,DeYoung承认,“当作者讲述一个故事时,读者继续阅读的可能性更大。” (8)。 最有说服力的历史是通过人们讲述的。 历史往往不只是信息传递。

title: Leverage Church History for Ministry
summary: Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan discuss how pastors can use church history to strengthen their preaching, encourage their congregations, understand historic Christian beliefs, and learn from believers who have gone before us.
summary_zh: 马特·斯梅瑟斯特（Matt Smethurst）和利根·邓肯（Ligon Duncan）讨论了牧师如何利用教会历史来强化讲道、激励会众、理解历史上的基督教信仰，并向先辈信徒学习。
title_zh: 利用教会历史开展事工
content: Why should pastors care about church history, and how can they use it in everyday ministry? Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan discuss why church history is more than a subject for scholars. They share practical ways pastors can draw from Christian biographies, historical events, and the early church to strengthen their preaching and help their congregations grow in faith. 牧师为什么要关心教会的历史,他们怎么能在日常的部里使用? 马特·斯梅特赫斯特(英语:Matt Smethurst)和利贡·邓肯(英语:Ligon Duncan)讨论了为什么教会历史不仅仅是学者的课题. 他们分享了牧师从基督教传记,历史事件以及早期教会中汲取的实用方法,以加强他们的传教,帮助他们的会众在信仰中成长.

title: How to Preach to Workers
summary: The New Testament offers two paradigms for how preachers can consider workers in their teaching.
summary_zh: 新约提供了两种范式，说明传道人如何在教导中考虑到工人。
title_zh: 如何向工人传福音
content: I still remember the first time I heard a sermon on God’s design for work. Pastor Colin Smith was in a series working through the Ten Commandments, and he’d come to the fourth command about the Sabbath. I was expecting to hear challenging words about rest. So I was surprised when he spent the first half of his sermon talking about work. Because he’s a good exegetical preacher, Smith reminded us to pay attention to the part of the passage we might overlook: “Six days you shall labor, and do all your work . . .” (Ex. 20:9). For 16 minutes, Smith preached about God’s design for work. He explained how God modeled work in creation, crafting and making our world like a builder, engineer, and artist. And since humans were created in the likeness of this God, our labors are a significant part of what it means to represent him in the world. Then he started naming regular kinds of work—such as the school crossing guard who creates a zone of safety and protection for children. He shared example after example, even naming those who are were unemployed and looking for work as engaging in a form of dignified labor. They can please God as they trust him to provide and remain diligent to seek out what’s next. At the time, I was working a summer landscaping job between semesters at seminary. I took the job because it was necessary, not because I found it personally fulfilling or spiritually significant. I’d been subconsciously wanting to be done with mowing lawns and picking weeds so I could get back to the important work of studying Scripture. But God used Smith’s sermon to reorient my ordinary labor. Preaching with workers in mind is vital to shepherding a congregation. It reminds church members that work is a primary context for discipleship and helps them work out the implications of God’s Word where they spend a large portion of their time. The New Testament gives two paradigms for how preachers can consider workers in their teaching. Work as an Illustration of the Kingdom As the eternal, perfect Son of God, Jesus isn’t only Savior and Lord but also the most brilliant teacher the world has ever heard. Therefore, as preachers, we take his pedagogy seriously even as we learn his precepts and mimic his practices. Jesus often proclaims the good news by igniting people’s imaginations and explaining eternal truths in concrete realities, including the body (Matt. 6:22; 7:3–5; 24:7–8), nature (Matt. 6:28–29; Mark 11:23; Luke 17:6), and food (Matt. 13:33; John 6:35, 53–56). But Jesus’s most consistent metaphor for the truths of the kingdom is work and workers. Klaus Issler’s survey reveals that of the 37 parables in the Synoptic Gospels, 32 reference work or workers, representing 22 different work roles. In 25 of the parables, work is a main part of the storyline. Here are examples: The farmer sows the seed (Matt. 13). The faithful manager gives the servants of the household food at the proper time (Luke 12:42). Even an unjust judge will give a persistent widow justice (18:1–8). The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). A king going into battle should take counsel to see if he’s strong enough before he a ttacks (Luke 14:31). When Jesus describes what it meant to follow him and live in his kingdom, why does he use the ordinary language of work and workers? First, God’s self-disclosure is often wrapped in the language of work. For instance, he’s portrayed as a composer and performer (Deut. 31:19), a tentmaker (Job 9:8), a garment maker and dresser (29:14), a shepherd (Ps. 23:1–4), a builder (Prov. 8:27–31), a metalworker (Isa. 1:24–26), a potter (31:9), and a farmer (Hos. 10:11). If God is the original worker, it makes sense that the whole realm of work can teach us his ways. If God is the original worker, it makes sense that the whole realm of work can teach us his ways. 我还记得我第一次听到关于上帝设计工作的布道。 科林·史密斯牧师在"十诫"系列中工作, 我希望听到关于休息的富有挑战性的话。 他上半场讲道工作时 我感到惊讶

由于他是一个优秀的传教士,史密斯提醒我们注意我们可能忽略的那段话:"六天你必须努力,并做你所有的工作."(前20:9). 16分钟,史密斯宣扬上帝的工作设计. 他解释了上帝如何塑造我们的世界 像一个建筑师、工程师和艺术家

由于人类是在这个上帝的相似之处创造的, 我们的劳动是世界中代表他的意义的重要部分. 然后,他开始点名从事常规工作,例如学校越野警卫,为儿童创造一个安全和保护的地区。

他举了个例子,甚至将那些失业和寻找工作的人命名为从事一种有尊严的劳动。 他们可以取悦上帝, 因为他们相信上帝提供, 当时我在神学院的暑期园林设计工作

我接受这份工作是因为有必要,而不是因为我发现这份工作是个人的满足或精神意义。 我潜意识地想要完成割草和摘草, 但上帝用史密斯的布道来调整我的普通劳动。 向工人宣讲对牧羊人至关重要。

它提醒教会成员,工作是门徒活动的主要背景,帮助他们解决神话的影响,在那里他们花费了大量的时间. "新约"为传教士如何在教学中考虑工人给出了两种范式.

发挥王国的作用 耶稣不仅是救世主, 因此,作为传教士,我们在学习他的戒律和模仿他的做法时,也认真对待他的教学方法.

耶稣经常通过点燃人们的想象力和在具体现实中解释永恒的真理来宣告好消息,包括身体(Matt 6:22;7:3–5;24:7–8),自然(Matt 6:28–29;Mark 11:23;Luke 17:6)和食物(Matt 13:33;John 6:35,53–56). 但耶稣对王国真理最一致的比喻是工作和工人.

Klaus Issler的调查表明,在Synoptic福音书中的37个比喻中,有32个参考工作或工人,代表着22个不同的工作角色. 在25个比喻中,作品是故事情节的主要部分. 以下是例子:农民播种(Matt.13). 忠诚的经理在适当的时候给家庭食物的仆人(公爵12:42).

即使是不公正的法官也会给守寡者一个持久的公正(18:1-8)。 善牧者为羊舍命(约翰10:11). 一个参战的国王应该接受建议, 当耶稣描述追随他并生活在他的王国的意义时,他为什么使用普通的劳动和工人语言?

首先,上帝的自我披露常常用工作语言包扎。 例如,他被描绘成作曲家和表演者(德国31:19)、帐篷匠(约旦9:8)、制衣和梳妆师(29:14)、牧羊人(Ps.23:1-4)、建筑师(Prov.8:27-31)、金属工人(Isa:1:24-26)、锅工(31:9)和农民(Hos:10:11)。

如果上帝是最初的工人,那么整个工作领域可以教我们他的方法是有道理的. 如果上帝是最初的工人,那么整个工作领域可以教我们他的方法是有道理的. 第二,耶稣作为一名普通工人可能花费了近6倍于他在公共部委中花费的年头,可能是石匠,或者经营一个S.

title: In the Darkness, Christmas Shines a Light
summary: The general revelation of God’s created order—darkness and light, night and day—primes every created thing to know they need light, a salvation from outside themselves.
summary_zh: 神所创造的秩序——黑暗与光明、黑夜与白昼——的普遍启示，使每一受造物都认识到自己需要光明，需要来自自身之外的拯救。
title_zh: 在黑暗中，圣诞节照亮光明
content: Read For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but the LORD will arise upon you, and his glory will be seen upon you. And nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising. (Isa. 60:2–3) Reflect There’s something about a sunrise. It wakes the world. Unlike the jarring blare of an alarm clock, a sunrise quietly whispers “Wake, O sleeper” with the graceful love of a parent rubbing a sleeping child’s back. When the sun rises, the slumbering stir to life. We’ve just spent seven or eight hours dead to the world. Then the sunrise triggers in us what looks like a resurrection. We rise. Certain flowers—daisies, poppies, and the aptly named morning glories—open their blossoms at the sun’s rising. Little by little, empty streets fill and quiet houses stir. Drawn to the warmth and energy of the just-unveiled sun, we transition from rest to work, stillness to activity. Drawn to the warmth and energy of the just-unveiled sun, we transition from rest to work, stillness to activity. It’s not surprising that the sun is an oft-used metaphor for God. For he, too, resurrects the dead. He, too, is the Giver of life and growth. He, too, draws all things to himself—such as the trees, which by nature grow upward, toward the sun, their branches like arms raised in perpetual worship. This is the created order. All things were made to be drawn to and sustained by the sun. We were made to be alive insofar as we live, grow, and flourish by solar energy. So too with God. We’re in darkness and death without him. As he bestows his grace on us, we rise to new life. We’re able to grow. Like the sunflower blossom, which turns to follow the sun wherever it’s positioned in the sky, we’re created to look to the Lord, who “will arise upon [us], and his glory will be seen upon [us]” (Isa. 60:2). In a world of darkness, we ache for the light. We wait for the sunrise. All nations, all kings, all people share this in common. The horizon each of us looks to—the nature of the “new day” we await—may be different: A new job. A remodeled home. A regime change. But only the sunrise of Christ will eternally satisfy. His is “the true light, which gives light to everyone” (John 1:9). Isaiah’s prophecy was fulfilled in him. Only the sunrise of Christ will eternally satisfy. The general revelation of God’s created order—darkness and light, night and day—primes every created thing to know they need light, a salvation from outside themselves. The special revelation of Christ reveals a truer light than even the sun: the light that is our eternal life, the light the darkness will never overcome (v. 5), the light that will one day end night as we know it (Rev. 22:5). Respond How is God’s glory seen in your life? How are you reflecting his beauty? In contrast to those who dwell in darkness, how does your life reflect 1 Thessalonians 5:5: “You are all children of light, children of the day. We are not of the night or of the darkness”?
content_zh:
读取 看 哪 、 黑暗 必 遮蔽 大地 、 厚 厚 的 黑暗 、 民 的 黑暗 、 但 耶和華 必 降臨 你 們 、 他 的 荣耀 必 降臨 你 們 诸国将至汝光,诸王将至汝升华之光. (以60:2-3为单位) 日出时, 能唤醒世界.

日出与闹钟不同, 当太阳升起时,沉睡会激起生命. 我们刚刚花了七八个小时去世界。 然后日出触发了我们 看起来像复活。 我们升起。

某些花朵——日出、罂粟和有名的晨光, 空荡荡的街道 安静的房屋被搅动 我们从休息到工作 静静到活动 我们从休息到工作 静静到活动

太阳是上帝常用的比喻, 他也会复活死者 他也是生命和成长的源泉 他也将万物引到自己身上,如那些自然而然地向着太阳生长的树木,他们的枝条,犹如在永恒的崇拜中竖起的手臂一样。 这是创造出来的秩序。 万物皆为太阳所牵引及支撑.

我们被太阳能所制成活生生的 故与神为也. 我们身处黑暗和死亡之中, 当他赐予我们恩典时 我们走向新生活 我们有能力成长。

和向日葵花一样,它会随太阳而来,无论太阳位于何处,我们都是为了仰望主而创造的,主"将出现[我们],他的荣耀将出现[我们]"(Isa. 60:2)。 在一个黑暗的世界里,我们渴望光明。 我们等待日出。 所有国家,所有国王,所有人民都拥有这个共同点.

我们每个人期待的地平线——我们等待的 " 新日 " 的性质——可能不同:新的工作。 一座重修的故乡. 政权更迭. 但只有基督的日出才能永远满足. 他的作品是“真正的光,它为每个人带来光明”(约翰1:9)。 以赛亚的预言在他身上得到了实现. 只有基督的日出才能永远满足

真主所创造的秩序——黑暗和光明,昼夜——的启示,使每一个被创造的事物都明白,他们需要光明,这是外部的拯救。 基督的特别启示揭示出比太阳更真实的光芒:即我们永恒生命的光芒,黑暗永远不会战胜的光芒(v. 5),即我们所知道的一天末夜的光芒(Rev.22: 5).

响应 上帝的荣耀在你的生活中是如何显现的? 你怎么反映他的美丽? 与那些生活在黑暗中的人不同,你的生活如何反映一个塞萨洛尼亚人5:5:“你们都是光明的孩子,是白天的孩子。 我们不是在黑夜中,也不是在黑暗中。”

title_zh: 卡杜纳教堂绑架事件后，仍有9名基督徒被劫持
content: Nine Christians remain in captivity after gunmen abducted 12 worshippers during a Sunday church service in Kurmin Wali community, Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna state, according to church leaders. The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Kaduna state chapter, disclosed the abduction on Tuesday, Nov. 17, two days after the attack on Nov. 15. CAN State Chairman Rev. Caleb Bawa Ma’aji said armed men invaded the community while residents were attending a church service and took 12 worshippers. Three of the victims later escaped and returned to the community, while nine remain with their captors. Ma’aji also reported that five residents were abducted during another attack on Oct. 5. According to him, all five remain in captivity. The latest abduction brings the number of people reportedly still held by kidnappers from the two attacks to 14. Ma’aji criticized the Kaduna State Government’s response to security concerns in the community, saying commitments made by Governor Uba Sani after the October attack had not been fulfilled. He said the governor had promised to establish a security base, construct roads, build a school and provide medical facilities for residents. The CAN chairman called on the state government to take urgent action to secure the release of the 14 captives. He also urged security agencies to intensify rescue operations and ensure the victims return safely to their families. He said repeated attacks and kidnappings had created fear among residents who previously lived peacefully in the community. Kaduna State Police Command Spokesperson DSP Mansir Hassan could not be reached for comment. He did not respond to telephone calls seeking confirmation of the Nov. 15 attack or information about measures being taken to rescue the abducted worshippers. The two abductions occurred in Kurmin Wali within six weeks, according to CAN’s account. The association has called on the state government and security agencies to address the situation and secure the release of those still being held. To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post 9 Christians Remain Captive After Kaduna Church Abduction first appeared on International Christian Concern .

title_zh: 印度奥里萨邦教堂遭暴徒袭击后被拆除
content: A church in India’s eastern state of Odisha was demolished under the supervision of government authorities the day after its owner reported that villagers had vandalized the building, raising fresh concerns about the treatment of Christian minorities in the region. The Beersheba Church, located in Patraguda village in Koraput district, was damaged on Nov. 21 by a group of men who entered the property with pickaxes and hammers, pulled down a cross, and damaged part of a wall. Durjan Harijan, the local Christian who built the church, filed a police complaint naming seven alleged attackers. The next day, Nov. 22, police and local revenue officials demolished the remaining structure in public view. Harijan told The Indian Express that the church was built beside his home for his family, which he described as the only Christian household in the predominantly tribal village of about 900 residents. He said the land belonged to his father. The church served as a place of Sunday worship for his family and other Christians from nearby communities. Harijan also said that some villagers had begun attending services in recent months, prompting accusations that he was attempting to convert people to Christianity. He denied the allegations and said villagers verbally abused him and his family before the church was vandalized. Seeking Justice Police registered a First Information Report (FIR), the formal document initiating a criminal investigation in India, against seven individuals based on Harijan’s complaint. The charges reportedly include offenses related to property damage and acts committed with common intention. As of Nov. 25, police said the investigation remained underway and did not confirm any arrests. Pastor Franklin Josobonto said he joined about 40 other pastors in approaching the police station on Nov. 21 to seek action against those responsible for the vandalism. He told UCA News that villagers subsequently asked police not to pursue the complaint. Local officials offered a different account of the church’s demolition. Kotpad Tehsildar Parsuram Bhatra told The Indian Express that authorities visited the village after the vandalism report and held a peace meeting. During the meeting, villagers alleged that the church was built on government land. Officials then issued Harijan a show-cause notice asking why the structure should not be demolished. Bhatra said Harijan removed the building after receiving the notice. Kotpad police also stated that Harijan carried out the demolition. However, Harijan disputed that account, saying he was pressured to arrange the machinery and is seeking legal advice about taking the matter to court. The dispute over the land has not been independently resolved. Bhatra said a revenue official had been asked to submit a report on the property and demolished structure, with further action to follow. Christian leaders criticized the circumstances surrounding the demolition, particularly its timing so soon after the reported attack. Bishop Pallab Lima of the United Believers Council Network of India described the action as an alarming failure by local authorities to protect the Christian community. Ismail Patro, general secretary of the National Christian Front, visited Patraguda and said seven Christian families lived in the village. Three families had already left because of fear, intimidation, and persecution, he told UCA News. Patro said Christian representatives planned to approach the district’s senior administrator to request an official investigation and restoration of the church. Growing Hostility The incident comes amid longstanding concerns about anti-Christian hostility in Odisha. Christians account for approximately 2.77% of the state’s population of 42 million, according to figures cited by UCA News. The state has experienced some of India’s most serious episodes of anti-Christian violence. In 2008, coordinated attacks by extremist Hindu mobs in Kandhamal district killed more than 100 Chris
content_zh:
印度东部奥迪沙邦的一所教堂在政府当局的监督下被拆除,次日,该教堂的主人报告说,村民破坏该建筑,引起人们对该地区基督教少数民族待遇的新关切. 位于科拉普特区帕特拉古达村的比尔谢巴教堂于11月被损坏.

由一行人用取斧和锤子入地,取出十字架并损坏了一堵墙的一部分. 建造教堂的当地基督教徒Durjan Harijan向警方提出申诉,指控7名据称袭击者。 次日(11月22日),警方和地方税收官员在公众视野中拆除了所剩建筑.

哈里扬告诉"印度快报",这座教堂是在他的家旁边为他的家人而建的,他形容这家是以部落为主的约900名居民村中唯一的基督教家庭. 他说土地属于他父亲 教堂作为他的家人和附近社区的其他基督徒的礼拜场所.

哈里扬还说,近几个月来,一些村民开始参加礼拜会,引起他试图将人们皈依基督教的指控. 他否认这些指控,并说村民在教堂被破坏之前对他及其家人进行辱骂.

根据Harijan的控诉,寻求司法警察登记了第一份资料报告,这是在印度启动刑事调查的正式文件。 据报告,这些指控包括与财产损失有关的犯罪和出于共同意图实施的行为。 截至11月25日,警方称调查仍在进行,没有证实有任何逮捕。

Franklin Josobonto牧师说,他与其他大约40名牧师一起于11月21日接近警察局,寻求对破坏行为责任人采取行动. 他告诉UCA News,村民们后来要求警察不要追诉. 当地官员对教堂被拆除的情况提出了不同的说法.

Kotpad Tehsildar Parsuram Bhatra告诉"印度快报",当局在破坏报告后访问了该村并举行了一次和平会议. 会议期间,村民声称教堂是建在政府用地上. 官员随后向Harijan发了一张展会,因为通知询问为何该建筑不应被拆除. 巴特拉说,哈里扬收到通知后拆除了大楼.

克特帕德警方还称哈里扬进行了拆除. 然而,Harijan对该说法提出异议,说他受到压力,要安排机器,并正在寻求关于将此事提交法院的法律咨询。 土地纠纷尚未独立解决.

Bhatra说,已要求一名税务官员提交关于财产和被拆除建筑的报告,并随后采取进一步行动。 基督教领袖们批评了拆除的周围环境,特别是在报道的袭击发生后如此快的时间.

印度联合信徒理事会网络的Pallab Lima主教称,这一行动是地方当局在保护基督教社区方面的令人震惊的失败。 全国基督教阵线总书记伊斯梅尔·帕特罗(Ismail Patro)拜访了帕特拉古达并说有七个基督教家庭住在该村.

由于恐惧、恐吓和迫害,三个家庭已经离开。 Patro说,基督教代表计划与该区的高级行政人员接洽,要求正式调查和修复教堂。 日益严重的敌意 这一事件是在对奥迪沙反基督教敌意的长期关切中发生的。

基督教徒约占全州4200万人口的2.77%, 印度经历了一些最严重的反基督教暴力事件。 2008年,Kandhamal区的极端印度教暴徒协同袭击,杀害了100多名克里斯。

summary_zh:
11月15日星期日上午8时30分左右,位于南苏丹朱巴附近Gorom难民营的达尔富尔基督教会教堂的庭院成为突然发生暴力事件的场所. 当礼拜者聚集祈祷时,由Baqir Muhammad Saleh率领的一个团体发动了残酷的攻击。

有人扔石头,用棍子打人,有些... 南苏丹Gorom难民营发生暴力袭击后,
title_zh: 南苏丹戈罗姆难民营的礼拜者遭遇暴力袭击
content: Around 8:30 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 15, the courtyard of the Darfur Christian Council church in Gorom Refugee Camp near Juba, South Sudan, became a scene of sudden violence. As worshippers gathered for prayer, a group led by Baqir Muhammad Saleh launched a brutal attack. Stones were thrown, sticks were used to beat people, and some victims were bitten and strangled. “Pastor Daniel Hassan suffered severe injuries: a large part of his left ear was lost to a bite, and the tendon in his middle finger was damaged,” a local bishop who wished to remain anonymous said. “Pastor Samuel Omer received serious blows to the head that caused internal injuries. His wife was beaten in the abdominal area and sustained internal trauma. Brother Michael Yusuf was struck in the nose, while Brother Elias Ibrahim Mohammed was strangled and beaten on the stomach, resulting in minor injuries. Others, including Ahmed Khalid and Fatima Ahmed Khalid, were also exposed to the violence.” This was not the first time the church courtyard had been attacked. On April 17, 2025, Pastor Hassan was shot, sustaining injuries to his thigh and hand. The repeated nature of these assaults has left the congregation shaken and deeply concerned for their safety. “We continue to pray for peace and forgiveness, asking believers to restrain themselves and offer words of love, because the church is a place of holiness and prayer. As the Psalmist writes, ‘Turn from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it’ (Psalm 34:14). Christ teaches us to forgive and to be a blessing even in the face of hatred.” Hassan stated. The Darfur Christian Council serves believers who have already fled conflict and persecution in Sudan. For many, the refugee camp was meant to be a place of relative safety. Instead, the church has become a target. The latest attack has deepened fear among worshippers, many of whom now wonder whether they can gather freely to pray without risking further violence. “We demand that the authorities in the camp provide as much protection as possible to the worshippers,” another victim said. “We also demand that a proper investigation be carried out and that justice be done according to the law. The Lord is a God of justice; ‘He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples with equity’ (Psalm 98:9). We cry out for that justice to be seen here.” Despite the pain and injury, the leaders of the Darfur Christian Council have chosen the path of restraint and faith. They continue to call their people to respond with the love of Christ rather than retaliation, holding fast to the truth that the church must remain a place of peace and holiness even when surrounded by hostility. “Though the attack has wounded our bodies and our hearts, we refuse to abandon the way of the cross,” Pastor Hassan said. “‘The Lord is close to the broken-hearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit’ (Psalm 34:18). We trust him to heal our wounds, protect his people, and turn this suffering into a testimony of his grace.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . content_zh:
11月15日星期日上午8时30分左右,位于南苏丹朱巴附近Gorom难民营的达尔富尔基督教会教堂的庭院成为突然发生暴力事件的场所. 当礼拜者聚集祈祷时,由Baqir Muhammad Saleh率领的一个团体发动了残酷的攻击。 投掷石块,用棍棒打人,一些受害者被咬死并勒死.

当地一位希望匿名的主教说,“Daniel Hassan牧师受重伤:左耳大部被咬伤,中指的阴茎受损”。 “Samuel Omer神父头部受到严重打击,造成内伤。 他的妻子在腹部遭到殴打,并受到内伤。

Michael Yusuf兄弟被击中鼻子,而Elias Ibrahim Mohammed兄弟被勒死并殴打腹部,造成轻伤。 其他人,包括艾哈迈德·哈立德和法蒂玛·艾哈迈德·哈立德也遭到暴力。 这不是教堂庭院第一次遭到袭击。 2025年4月17日,哈桑牧师中弹,大腿和手受伤.

这些袭击一再发生,使教会感到动摇,并深为关切其安全。 “我们继续祈求和平和宽恕,要求信徒克制,献出爱语,因为教堂是神圣和祈祷的地方。 如"诗经"所记载:"从恶反善;求和而追之(诗经34:14).

基督教导我们,即使面对仇恨,也要宽恕和成为祝福。” 哈桑说。 达尔富尔基督教理事会为已经逃离苏丹冲突和迫害的信徒服务。 对许多人来说,难民营是相对安全的地方。 相反,教堂已经成为目标.

最近的一次袭击加深了礼拜者的恐惧,其中许多人现在怀疑他们是否可以自由聚集在一起祈祷,而不会面临进一步暴力的风险。 另一位受害者说,“我们要求难民营当局向礼拜者提供尽可能多的保护。” “我们还要求进行适当调查,并依法伸张正义。

主是正义的神; " 他将以正义和公平来评判世界和人民 " (第98:9段)。 我们要求在这里看到这种正义。” 尽管遭受了痛苦和伤害,但达尔富尔基督教理事会的领导人选择了克制和信仰的道路。

他们继续号召自己的人民以基督的爱而不是报复来回应,坚守真理,即即使周围充满敌意,教会也必须保持和平和神圣。 “尽管袭击伤害了我们的身体和心灵,但我们拒绝放弃十字架的道路,”哈桑牧师说。

" `主近于伤心者,救精神所压者'(34:18). 我们信任他医治我们的创伤,保护他的人民,并把这种痛苦变成他恩惠的见证。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

title_zh: 尼日利亚19岁基督徒农民在袭击中失去一只手
content: A 19-year-old Christian farmer, Jesse Monday, lost one of his hands after suspected Fulani herdsmen attacked three young men working on their farmland in Rewienku Village, Miango District, Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau state, on Monday, Nov. 23. The attack reportedly occurred around 3 p.m. when the three young men were working on their farm. Monday sustained multiple machete wounds, and his hand was completely severed during the assault. He is currently receiving medical treatment at an undisclosed hospital. The other two young men escaped without physical injuries, according to a statement issued by the Rewienku Youth Development Association (RYDA). Rewienku is a predominantly farming community in Miango District, part of the Irigwe-speaking area of Bassa LGA in Plateau state’s central region. Residents depend largely on agriculture for their livelihoods. In a statement signed by its general secretary, Comr. Vokwe Joshua Obadiah, RYDA called on the Plateau State Government, Bassa Local Government Council and security agencies to investigate the attack, identify those responsible and prosecute the perpetrators. The association also demanded increased security deployments in Rewienku and surrounding farmlands to protect residents from further attacks. It appealed to the government and humanitarian organizations to provide medical assistance and rehabilitation support for Monday. RYDA urged community leaders, the Rigwe Development Association and the Irigwe Youth Movement to work with security agencies to address threats to residents. The association also appealed to residents, particularly young people, to remain calm, avoid retaliation, and report credible information to security authorities. A Growing Problem According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. The network of militias is responsible for four times more civilian deaths than the two prominent Islamic terror organizations, Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), combined. The study’s findings challenge the commonly held belief that the two organized terror groups kill the larger number of Christians, highlighting the Fulani network’s expanded efforts to target Christians. title_zh: 印度一个有8口人的基督徒家庭被驱逐，无家可归
content: A Christian family of eight in the Sukma district of Chhattisgarh, India, was left homeless after Hindu nationalists ransacked and demolished their home on the morning of Nov. 16. During the eviction, the family’s essential household items — including food, clothing, bedding, kitchen utensils, and vital personal documents — were thrown out of their home. The house, belonging to Manglu Sodi and his wife, Hirmibai, was reportedly ransacked and demolished because of their Christian faith. Amid the destruction, 4,000 rupees (roughly $43), about five grams of gold, and a bicycle were stolen before the house was destroyed. Relief in Safe House Fleeing for their safety, the family traveled roughly 40 miles to reach the district headquarters of Sukma, where they were placed in a Safe House. Representatives of the Progressive Christian Alliance (PCA), a rights advocacy group working for the welfare of Christian minorities, coordinated with local pastor Harendra Madiya in Sukma to provide relief for the persecuted family. PCA State Coordinator Patras Balti visited the family to encourage and pray with them, urging them to remain steadfast in their faith despite the severe hardship. Although formal complaints have been submitted to the local police station, the Superintendent of Police (SP), and the district collector of Sukma, no formal inquiry or legal action has been initiated to date. Without their identification documents or savings, the family faces steep hurdles in rehabilitation and rebuilding their lives. Historic Church Building Razed Down In another development, up north of Sukma district, about 300 miles away, a historic church estimated by locals to be roughly 130 years old was demolished in Rajnandgaon district of Chhattisgarh in the past week. The structure was part of the campus of the Missionary Bands of the World Leprosy Hospital (also known as the Rajnandgaon Leprosy Hospital and Clinics), which stood on about 23 acres of government-leased land originally allotted for treating and rehabilitating leprosy patients. The Clearance Operation The demolition followed a lease-cancellation order issued on Nov. 6 by the Rajnandgaon district collector. The demolition drive razed not only the church, but also the old hospital wards, administrative offices, and residential quarters of the leprosy hospital. The administration said the reclaimed land will be used for public amenities, including a sports ground. However, Christian watchdogs are skeptical about the district collector’s action. Christian community leaders urged a clear distinction between the government’s right to recover land over alleged lease violations and the decision to destroy a heritage religious structure. 印度恰蒂斯加尔邦Sukma县一户由8人组成的基督教家庭在11月16日上午印度民族主义者洗劫并拆毁了他们的家后被无家可归. 在驱逐期间,家庭的基本家用物品 -- -- 包括食物、衣服、被褥、厨房用具和重要个人证件 -- -- 被赶出家门。

这所房子属于Manglu Sodi和他的妻子Hirmibai,据报因其基督教信仰被洗劫并被拆毁。 在被摧毁时,4 000卢比(约43美元),约5克黄金被偷走,还有一辆自行车被摧毁。

安全屋的救济为他们的安全而逃出,全家出行了大约40英里去到Sukma区总部,在那里他们被安置在安全屋.

进步基督教联盟(PCA)的代表,这是一个致力于基督教少数派福利的权利倡导团体,与苏克马的Harendra Madiya当地牧师协调,为受迫害的家庭提供救济. 常设仲裁法院州协调员Patras Balti访问了该家庭,鼓励他们和他们一起祈祷,敦促他们尽管遭遇了严重困难,但仍要坚定信念。

虽然已经向地方警察局、警察局长和Sukma地区收藏家提出正式申诉,但迄今尚未启动任何正式调查或法律行动。 没有身份证件或储蓄,家庭在恢复和重建生活方面面临严重障碍。

历史教堂建筑被刮倒 在位于相距约300英里外的Sukma区以北的另一项发展中,当地人估计大约有130年历史的一座历史教堂在过去一周被查蒂斯加尔的Rajnandgaon区拆除.

该建筑是世界麻风病医院(又名Rajnandgaon麻风病医院和诊所)传教团校园的一部分,该院占地约23英亩,最初分配给麻风病人治疗和康复。 清除行动 拆除是在11月签发的租约取消令之后进行的。

6由拉杰南德加翁区收藏家出品. 拆除运动不仅夷平了教堂,还夷平了麻风医院的旧医院病房,行政办公室和住宅区. 行政当局说,被开垦的土地将用于公共设施,包括体育场。 但基督教监督员对地区收藏家的行为持怀疑态度。

基督教社区领袖敦促明确区分政府收回土地的权利与摧毁传统宗教结构的决定。 更多新闻报导, 采访,请通过电子邮件。 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

summary_zh: 这可能令人感到意外，但圣诞节是伊拉克的国定假日——自2018年12月政府正式宣布以来一直如此。“这感觉像是为了显得不歧视而采取的象征性举措。”“彼得罗斯”说道。他是一名亚述基督徒，与一个伊拉克侨民家庭一起居住在美国。他补充说，这种“象征性”的庆祝……   这篇题为《圣诞节在伊拉克是一个喜忧参半的节日》的文章最初发表在“国际基督徒关注”网站上。
title_zh: 圣诞节是伊拉克一个喜忧参半的节日
content: This may come as a surprise, but Christmas is a national holiday in Iraq — ever since the government formally declared it so in December 2018. “It feels like a token move to appear non-discriminatory,” said “Petros,” an Assyrian Christian living in the U.S. with an Iraqi expat family. He added that this “token” celebration of Christmas “ignores the native traditions” of the region’s Christians and “instead opts for a European-style Christmas” with Santa Claus and various types of Christmas trees that don’t naturally grow in the area. Iraq, which was already celebrating the birth of Christ when most of Europe was still pagan, has among the world’s oldest Christian communities, with the faith arriving in the first century A.D. Petros feels that the Iraqi government’s acknowledgment of Christmas is more of a public relations strategy to deflect from the recent horrors faced by Iraq’s Christians. “Yonita,” an Assyrian woman who is Chaldean Catholic and lives in the U.S., believes the recent recognition of Christmas is financially motivated. “Iraq is trying to rebuild itself,” she said, adding that it might be “taking notes” from more successful countries in the region that have comparatively more religious freedom. Yonita suspects that celebrating Christmas could be an attempt at showing camaraderie with the West. It could also be a way to make the homeland seem more congenial to the many Iraqi Christians abroad. As she pointed out, the Christian Iraqi diaspora tends to be quite well-off financially. “There was a formal call inviting us back to Iraq [to] invest in the rebuilding of the cradle of civilization,” Yonita said. A Sad Reality Whatever the Iraqi government’s true motivation, one painful aspect is hard to deny: By the time Christmas became a national holiday, most Iraqi Christians had already been driven out of their homeland. Conditions were so difficult during the previous 15 years that the country had lost up to 90% of its Christian community. Iraq’s remaining Christians, most of whom belong either to the Chaldean Catholic Church or the Assyrian Church of the East, now comprise less than half of 1% of the country’s overall population. The Christian population had already seen considerable decline during the 24-year reign of former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein, a man of immense sadism. But, for all his homicidal flaws, Hussein — though Muslim by background — was no Islamic extremist. In fact, his longtime right-hand man, Deputy Prime Minister Tariq Aziz, was a Christian, at least technically. It would likely be an exaggeration to say that Hussein cared about the welfare of Iraqi Christians, but the bone-crushing force of his reputation rendered most Iraqis, regardless of their faith, too intimidated to indulge in sectarian hostilities. Petros said that his fellow Assyrian Christians “either liked Hussein for providing stability and jobs, or hated him for killing their family members.” Many of Iraq’s Christians wanted him to stay in power only because they had an acute sense of the mayhem that would erupt after their secular tyrant was deposed. “It’s like the saying goes,” Petros said. “Better to deal with the devil you know than the devil you don’t.” At this point, though, both “devils” have fully acquainted themselves with Iraq. The Rise of Extremism The ousting of Hussein from power in 2003 brought in an era of rising Islamic extremism, most notably with the Islamic State group (ISIS), formerly known as “al-Qaida in Iraq.” Some Iraqi Christians were even accused of collaborating with the U.S. military. As the atmosphere grew increasingly precarious in post-Hussein Iraq, most Christians fled the country, having decided the other options — violent death, forced conversion, or paying a religious tax — were unpalatable. Those who remained were often hunted. In June 2007, in the northern Iraqi city of Mosul, a priest and his assistants were killed right in front of his church. content_zh:
这也许是个惊喜, 但圣诞节是伊拉克的国庆节, “Petros”是一位居住在美国的亚述基督教徒,

他补充说,这种对该地区基督教徒的圣诞节 " 玷污当地传统 " 的 " 庆祝 " , " 而不是选择一个欧洲式的圣诞节 " ,圣诞老人和该地区自然不会生长的各类圣诞树。

伊拉克在庆祝基督诞生时,欧洲大部分地区仍然是异教徒,伊拉克是世界上最古老的基督教社区之一,公元一世纪时,信仰就已经降临。 彼得罗斯认为伊拉克政府承认圣诞节更是一种公共关系策略,旨在转移伊拉克基督徒最近面临的恐怖。

“Yonita”是一位信奉迦勒底天主教、居住在美国的亚述妇女, 她说,“伊拉克正在努力重建自己”,她补充说,它可能“注意到”该区域比较成功的宗教自由的国家。

Yonita怀疑庆祝圣诞节可能是试图与西方展示友情. 这也可以成为使祖国看起来对海外许多伊拉克基督徒更加融洽的方法. 正如她指出的那样,伊拉克的基督教散居国外者往往在财政上相当富裕。

Yonita说,“有人正式邀请我们回到伊拉克,投资重建文明的摇篮。” 一个悲哀的现实 无论伊拉克政府的真正动机如何,一个痛苦的方面很难否认: 到圣诞节成为国家节日时,大多数伊拉克基督徒已经被驱逐出家园.

在过去15年里,情况十分困难,以至于该国丧失了90%的基督教徒。 伊拉克其余的基督教徒,大多属于迦勒底天主教会或东方亚述教会,现在占该国总人口的不到1%。

伊拉克前总统萨达姆·侯赛因24年的统治期间,基督教徒人数已经大幅度减少,他是一位极度虐待的人。 但是,侯赛因尽管有穆斯林背景,但他的杀人缺陷并非伊斯兰极端主义分子。 事实上,他长期担任右手的副总理塔里克·阿齐兹是基督徒,至少在技术上是这样.

如果说侯赛因关心伊拉克基督徒的福利,那很可能是一种夸张的说法,但他的名声的骨折力量使大多数伊拉克人,无论其信仰如何,都过于恐吓,不敢陷入教派敌对行动。

Petros说,他的亚述基督徒同胞“要么喜欢侯赛因提供稳定和工作,要么恨他杀害家人”。 许多伊拉克基督徒希望他继续掌权,只是因为他们对世俗暴君被废黜后爆发的混乱有强烈的感受。 Petros说,

“最好对付你认识的恶魔, 然而,此时,这两个“恶魔”已完全熟悉伊拉克。

极端主义的兴起 2003年侯赛因被赶下台,带来了伊斯兰极端主义抬头的时代,其中最突出的是伊斯兰国集团(ISIS),它以前被称为“伊拉克基地组织”。 一些伊拉克基督徒甚至被指控与美国军方勾结.

title_zh: 为巴基斯坦基督徒的释放而进行的呼吁工作变得更加紧迫
content: Shahzad Masih has been praying for justice since 2017. He was just 16 years old when he was arrested on false charges, and has been waiting to be hanged since 2022. Nine years later, the American Center for Law and Justice (ACLJ), through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), is continuing to advocate for his release, Christian Daily International reported. In 2017, Masih was working as a janitor at a hospital when a Muslim coworker asked him about his belief in Jesus. As he explained his faith, he mentioned a comment made by a family friend that was spoken against the Prophet Muhammad, which offended the coworker and ended the conversation. The coworker belonged to Tehreek-e-Tahfuz-e-Islam, a conservative Islamic group in Pakistan. Members of the group heard about their conversation and confronted the Masih. Though he tried to clarify the situation, he was handed over to the police on July 13, 2017, and was questioned without legal representation before being imprisoned. In November 2022, according to Section 295C of the Pakistan Penal Code, he was sentenced to death for the “use of derogatory remarks, etc. in respect of the Holy Prophet.” Since then, he has been waiting to be hanged for his unjust sentence. The United Nations has called for his immediate release, stating that these decisions deny his right to “freedom of expression.” OLA has supported him and filed an appeal for his freedom four times, but the Lahore High Court has yet to hear his case. “Shahzad Masih was just 16 years old when he was arrested, and nine years later, he remains on death row for allegedly reporting someone else’s words,” said CeCe Heil, senior counsel and international legal director for the ACLJ. “We urge Pakistani authorities to uphold fundamental human rights, overturn this unjust conviction, and bring Shahzad Masih home to his family.” One of Many As more stories of Christians being imprisoned for false blasphemy accusations arise this year — including Amir Peter , who was tried before by a Lahore court in 2024 and died in custody in July — ACLJ is committed more than ever to fighting for the life of this young Christian. “This is the ultimate abominable human rights violation, and we’ll take this case all the way to Pakistan’s Supreme Court,” the advocacy group wrote . Open Doors ranks Pakistan as the eighth most dangerous place to be a Christian in the world. They are constantly subjected to persecution through discrimination, death threats, mob violence, imprisonment, and death, through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), continues. Story by Bella Agnello To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . title_zh: 越南在教会土地纠纷中拆除历史悠久的天主教建筑
content: Vietnamese authorities demolished a historic building belonging to the Redemptorist Catholic community in the central city of Huế on Tuesday, escalating a decades-long dispute over church property and raising renewed concerns about religious freedom in the communist-governed country. The demolition of the L’Accueil building followed the deployment of police by local authorities to block roads surrounding the Redemptorist monastery and Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church. Electricity to the area was also cut, preventing some parishioners from reaching the church to attend Mass or express solidarity with the religious community. According to the Redemptorists, heavy machinery began demolishing the structure while priests, religious brothers, and parishioners gathered nearby in prayer. The demolition continued through Nov. 18, leaving the property leveled and fenced off. The Redemptorist Provincial Chapter of Vietnam condemned the operation, arguing that authorities proceeded despite unresolved legal questions and repeated requests to review the property’s ownership. “Justice cannot be established through force, and the truth cannot be erased along with the structures that have been demolished,” the congregation said in a Nov. 17 statement as the demolition was proceeding. Communist Land Takeover The dispute centers on land that the Redemptorists purchased in 1930. According to historical documentation cited by the religious order, Huế municipal authorities formally recognized the congregation’s ownership in 1971. The L’Accueil complex was subsequently developed on the property between 1938 and 1943. It served as a center for educational, cultural, and community activities, housing a library, auditorium, and reading room. A sawmill was also established on the grounds in the 1950s, providing local employment. Following the communist takeover of South Vietnam in 1975, the government’s relationship with religious institutions changed significantly. Church properties throughout the country came under increasing state control, with religious communities frequently losing access to land and buildings they had previously owned. The Redemptorists maintain that they never voluntarily surrendered their rights to the L’Accueil property. They acknowledge that the congregation transferred assets associated with a sawmill to the state in 1978, but argue that the transfer did not include the land itself. Authorities subsequently assigned the property to government-controlled institutions. The remaining parcel, measuring about 2,550 square meters, is currently managed by a local sports vocational school. Recent Efforts The congregation has sought the property’s return since 1994. Its most recent formal complaint, submitted to the Huế People’s Committee on Oct. 24, requested recognition of its land-use rights and clarification of the property’s legal status. Authorities reportedly rejected the complaint in a Nov. 8 response, stating that it had no basis for consideration. A notice posted at the property in October announced plans to develop a public park and parking lot on the site. Local authorities have defended the project as serving public interests, including improving traffic conditions and providing additional green space in a densely populated area. Vietnamese law establishes that land is collectively owned by the people and administered by the state. Government authorities have also invoked a 2003 National Assembly resolution that generally prevents reconsideration of certain land and housing arrangements established before July 1, 1991. The Redemptorists, however, dispute the government’s interpretation of the property’s history and say authorities have not adequately explained the legal grounds for demolishing the building. They have asked officials to publicly disclose the documentation supporting their decision and review the historical records presented by the congregation. 在L ' Accueil大楼被拆除之前,地方当局部署了警察,封锁救赎会修道院和永生圣母助教周围的道路。 该地区的电力也被切断,使一些教区人士无法前往教堂参加弥撒或表示对宗教界的声援.

据救赎派说,重型机械开始拆除该建筑,而祭司,宗教兄弟,以及教区教徒聚集在附近祈祷. 拆除工作一直持续到11月18日,财产被夷为平地和围起来。

越南救赎主义省分会谴责了这次行动,认为当局不顾尚未解决的法律问题和一再要求审查该财产的所有权而继续行动. “正义不能通过武力建立,真理不能与被拆除的建筑物一起抹去。”

17份在拆除过程中的声明。 共产党夺地 争端集中在救赎者在1930年购买的土地上。 根据宗教秩序所引用的历史文献,胡瓦克市当局于1971年正式承认该教会的所有权. L ' Accueil建筑群后来于1938年至1943年间在地产上发展.

它作为教育、文化和社区活动中心、图书馆、礼堂和阅览室。 1950年代还在当地建立了锯木厂,提供当地就业。 1975年共产党接管南越后,政府与宗教机构的关系发生了重大变化.

全国各地的教会财产受到越来越多的国家控制,宗教社区往往失去获得其以前拥有的土地和建筑物的机会。 救赎者坚持认为,他们从未自愿放弃对L ' Accueil财产的权利。

他们承认教会在1978年将与锯木厂有关的资产转移到了国家,但辩称转让不包括土地本身. 当局随后将财产分配给政府控制的机构。 其余部分占地约2,550平方米,目前由当地体育职业学校管理.

最近的努力 自1994年以来,教会一直要求归还财产。 它最近于10月24日向胡瓦克人民委员会提出正式申诉,要求承认其土地使用权并澄清财产的法律地位。 据报告,当局在11月8日的答复中驳回了申诉,称申诉没有审议依据。

10月在该地产张贴了一份通知,宣布计划在该地开发一个公共公园和停车场. 地方当局捍卫该项目是为了公共利益,包括在人口稠密地区改善交通条件和提供更多的绿色空间。 越南法律规定,土地属于人民集体所有,由国家管理。

政府当局还援引了2003年国民议会的一项决议,该决议一般禁止重新审议1991年7月1日之前确定的某些土地和住房安排。 但救赎者质疑政府对该地产历史的解释,

他们要求官员公开公布支持其决定的文件,并审查教会提出的历史记录。 争议说明了宗教共产主义的困难

summary: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met Thursday in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented trilateral summit, projecting an image of cooperation among three of the world’s most powerful nations but offering few concrete agreements on the conflicts and international issues facing them. The roughly 80-minute meeting produced a…   The post  Trump, Xi, and Putin Meet Amid Deteriorating Religious Freedom Conditions   first appeared on  Intern
summary_zh:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普,中国国家主席习近平,俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京星期四在中国深圳举行前所未有的三边峰会,展现出世界三大强国之间合作的形象,但对面临的冲突和国际问题却很少提出具体协议.

大约80分钟的会议产生了一个. .
title_zh: 特朗普、习近平和普京在宗教自由状况恶化之际会晤
content: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met Thursday in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented trilateral summit, projecting an image of cooperation among three of the world’s most powerful nations but offering few concrete agreements on the conflicts and international issues facing them. The roughly 80-minute meeting produced a joint statement addressing United Nations reform, energy production, international legal authority, and nuclear risks. However, the statement offered no clear breakthroughs on the wars in Ukraine or Iran and made no public reference to religious freedom or the persecution of religious communities in China and Russia. The gathering underscored the importance of direct engagement among world leaders as they seek to manage competing interests, global conflicts, and questions about the future of international order. The summit also offered an opportunity to address concerns affecting millions of people who face persecution for their faith, particularly in countries governed by authoritarian regimes. A Summit Focused on Global Stability The three leaders presented themselves as sharing responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. Their joint statement called for United Nations reform, increased production and supply of petroleum products, and further dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The leaders also emphasized state sovereignty and the immunity of government officials, declaring that the International Criminal Court and similar bodies should not abuse their authority. The language reflects a shared interest among the three governments in limiting the reach of international institutions, although their respective political, economic, and security priorities remain distinct. Concerningly, this language is similar to that used by China in pushing back on American calls to respect human rights and ensure citizens can freely practice religion. Claiming that these are internal affairs, China rejects what it considers to be overly zealous policing by the U.S. and continues on its path of persecution. Putin described the summit as a new chapter in diplomatic history and praised the opportunity for direct engagement with Trump and Xi. The Russian president also invoked the 1945 Yalta Conference, which helped shape the postwar European order, arguing that international conflicts eventually require countries to recognize realities on the ground. While the leaders expressed interest in dialogue and international stability, their meeting did not produce publicly announced agreements to resolve major conflicts or address underlying tensions between their governments. Religious Freedom Remains a Global Concern For religious freedom advocates, high-level diplomatic meetings represent an important opportunity to raise the plight of prisoners of conscience and religious communities facing government persecution. China, in particular, continues to impose severe restrictions on religious practice. Christians in unregistered churches face surveillance, detention, church closures, and pressure to submit to government oversight. The Chinese Communist Party’s campaign to bring religious institutions under its control has affected Protestant house churches, Catholic communities, Tibetan Buddhists, Uyghur Muslims, and other religious minorities. In recent months, international advocates have urged the Trump administration to raise the cases of imprisoned religious leaders with Xi. Earlier this year, Trump raised the case of Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri, founder of Beijing’s Zion Church, during a meeting with Xi. Chinese authorities subsequently released Jin, who later relocated to the United States. However, other Zion Church leaders arrested during the same crackdown remain detained, and no such direct advocacy seems to have occurred at this most recent meeting. The case demonstrated how direct presidential engagement can potentially influence the circumstances
content_zh:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普,中国国家主席习近平,俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京星期四在中国深圳举行前所未有的三边峰会,展现出世界三大强国之间合作的形象,但很少就它们面临的冲突和国际问题达成具体协议.

大约80分钟的会议产生了关于联合国改革、能源生产、国际法律权威和核风险的联合声明。 然而,该声明对于乌克兰或伊朗的战争没有提出明确的突破,也没有公开提及中国和俄罗斯的宗教自由或对宗教团体的迫害.

会议强调了世界领导人直接参与的重要性,因为他们寻求管理相互竞争的利益、全球冲突和有关国际秩序未来的问题。 首脑会议还提供了一个机会,解决影响到数百万因信仰而面临迫害的人的关切,特别是在专制政权统治的国家。

以全球稳定为重点的首脑会议 三位领导人自称分担维护国际和平与安全的责任。 他们的联合声明呼吁联合国改革、增加石油产品的生产和供应,以及就减少核风险进一步进行对话。

各国领导人还强调国家主权和政府官员的豁免权,宣布国际刑事法院和类似机构不应滥用其权力。 其措辞反映了三国政府对限制国际机构的影响力的共同利益,尽管它们各自的政治、经济和安全优先事项仍然不同。

关于这一点,这种语言类似于中国在抵制美国尊重人权和确保公民可以自由信奉宗教的呼声时所使用的语言。 中国声称这是内政,反对美国过于狂热地维持治安,继续走迫害的道路。

普京将峰会描述为外交史上的新篇章,并称赞与特朗普和习近平直接接触的机会. 俄罗斯总统还援引了1945年雅尔塔会议,会议帮助塑造了战后的欧洲秩序,认为国际冲突最终需要各国承认当地的实际情况.

虽然领导人对对话和国际稳定表示兴趣,但他们的会议没有达成公开宣布的协议,以解决重大冲突或解决政府之间的紧张关系。

宗教自由仍然是全球关注的问题 对于宗教自由倡导者来说,高级别外交会议是一个重要的机会,可以提高良心犯和宗教界面临政府迫害的困境。 特别是中国继续严格限制宗教活动.

在未登记的教堂的基督徒面临监视,拘留,教堂关闭,以及服从政府监督的压力. 中国共产党将宗教机构置于其控制之下的运动影响了新教住宅教堂,天主教社区,藏传佛教,维吾尔穆斯林等宗教少数派.

最近几个月,国际倡导者敦促特朗普政府向习近平提出被囚禁宗教领袖的案件. 今年早些时候,特朗普在北京锡安教会创始人伊兹拉·金明里牧师会见习近平时提出这个案例. 中国当局随后释放了后来移居美国的金.

然而,在同一次镇压中被捕的其他锡安教会领导人仍然被拘留,在最近的这次会议上似乎没有进行这种直接的宣传。 该案表明,总统直接参与会如何影响局势

title_zh: 女性可以成为执事吗？
content: ABSTRACT: Whether or not women can serve as deacons is a live question for many Christians, especially with more churches shifting from a deacon-led to an elder-led polity. The nature of the role, the example of Phoebe, and the qualifications for deacons in 1 Timothy 3 may allow room for deaconesses, but each of these arguments faces compelling counterarguments. In the absence of clear biblical evidence for women holding this formal office, wisdom leads Christians to approach the question with both conviction and charity. For our ongoing series of feature articles for pastors and Christian leaders, we asked Benjamin Merkle (PhD, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary), Research Professor of New Testament and Greek at Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary, to examine the biblical evidence for women serving as deacons. By asking the question “Can women serve as deacons?” we are not simply asking whether women can serve the church. Scripture obviously permits and commends women serving the church. The question is whether the New Testament permits women to hold the formal office of deacon. Many churches are asking this question, for at least two reasons. First, women should not be restricted from serving in places where the Bible does not restrict them. If the Bible permits women to be deacons, then a church’s tradition does not offer sufficient grounds to prohibit them from holding the office. Women are essential to the health and vitality of the church, and we certainly don’t want to limit the church’s effectiveness over an unbiblical practice. Second, many churches either have moved or are moving to a plural-eldership model of church leadership. Historically, many Baptist, baptistic, or nondenominational churches were governed by a board of deacons. These deacons held leadership authority in a way that many believe is inappropriate for the office of deacon. For complementarians, it would not be wise for women to be deacons in such a context since it would violate 1 Timothy 2:12 (“I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man”). Under complementarianism, the relevant question is not whether an office possesses any authority whatsoever, but whether an office’s authority constitutes the kind of teaching or governing authority restricted to men. If a deacon holds elder-like authority, then, regardless of the title used, it would be wrong for a woman to hold the position because she would have authority over a man. If, however, a church has male elders who have authority to lead the church, then some are asking if it would be permissible to allow women to be deacons since a deacon is a position with little to no authority. With hundreds of churches shifting from a deacon-led to an elder-led polity, the question of whether women can be deacons becomes relevant. This essay unfolds as follows. I present the three best views for allowing women to be deacons. 1 (I assume a complementarian framework. The egalitarian-versus-complementarian debate is important, but I will not address it here.) After presenting each argument in favor of women deacons, I provide counterarguments. Although there are reasonable arguments for allowing women to serve as deacons, this essay argues that the New Testament provides no clear text that permits women to hold the office of deacon. I conclude the essay with three principles to keep in mind when dealing with this issue in the local church. Argument 1: The Nature of the Office The first argument for allowing women to hold the office of deacon concerns the nature of the office itself: Deacons are servants and not leaders. 2 As servants, deacons do not possess authority but serve the church in low-key (though important) ways. Consequently, nothing in Scripture would prohibit women from holding this office. The elders (also called “overseers” or “pastors”) are given the task of teaching and leading the church. ABSTRACT:妇女是否可以担任执事是许多基督徒的活生生的问题,特别是更多的教会从执事转向长者领导的政体。 角色的性质,菲比的例子,以及1 Timothy 3中的执事资格,可能为执事留有余地,但这些论点都面临着令人信服的反驳.

在没有明确的圣经证据证明妇女担任这一正式职务的情况下,智慧促使基督教徒以信念和慈善的态度对待这个问题。

对于我们目前为牧师和基督教领袖发表的一系列专题文章,我们请本杰明·梅尔克勒(PhD, The Southern Baptist Theocational Seminary),新约研究教授和东南浸信会神学院的希腊人,为担任执事的妇女审查圣经证据.

通过问“妇女能否担任执事?” 我们不仅仅是问妇女是否能够为教会服务。 圣经显然允许和赞扬为教会服务的妇女。 问题是新约是否允许妇女担任正式执事职务. 许多教会提出这个问题,至少有两个原因。

第一,不应限制妇女在圣经没有限制的地方服务。 如果《圣经》允许妇女担任执事,那么教会的传统就不足以禁止她们担任公职。 女性对教会的健康与活力至关重要,

第二,许多教堂要么已经搬迁,要么正在转向教会领导的多元-老年模式。 历史上,许多浸信会,洗礼会,或非宗派教会都由执事委员会管理. 这些执事以许多人认为不适合执事办公室的方式掌握领导权.

对于辅助者来说,在这样的背景下由妇女担任执事是不明智的,因为这将违反1 Timothy 2:12(“我不允许妇女教授或对男子行使权力”)。

在补充主义下,相关问题不是办公室是否拥有任何权威,而是办公室的权威是否构成仅限于男性的教学或管理权威。 如果执事拥有长者般的权威,那么,不管使用的头衔如何,女性担任这一职务是错误的,因为她将对男性拥有权威.

但是,如果一个教会有男性长者有权领导教会,那么有些人会问是否允许妇女担任执事,因为执事是一个几乎没有权力或没有权力的职位。 随着数百个教堂从执事转向长者领导的政体,妇女是否可以担任执事的问题变得重要. 这篇散文展开如下.

我提出三种最佳观点,允许妇女担任执事。 1(我假设是一个补充框架。) 平等与互补的辩论很重要,但我不想在这里谈论。 ) 在提出每一个有利于女性执事的论据后,我提出反驳.

虽然有合理的理由允许女性担任执事,但是这篇文章认为,新约没有给出允许女性担任执事的明确文本. 最后,我提出三项原则,以便在当地教会处理这一问题时铭记这些原则。

论点1:办公室的性质 允许妇女担任执事职位的第一个论点涉及办公室本身的性质:执事是仆人而不是领导者。 2个 作为仆人,执事并不拥有权威,而是以低调(虽然重要)的方式为教会服务. 因此,《圣经》中没有任何内容禁止妇女担任这一职务。

content: Audio Transcript Welcome back to the podcast on this Thanksgiving week. Yesterday, we read about Jesus washing the feet of his disciples in John 13. Jesus worked his basin of water from disciple to disciple on the floor. When he reached Peter, Peter instinctively pulled his feet back and said, “You shall never wash my feet.” Then “Jesus answered him, ‘If I do not wash you, you have no share with me.’ Simon Peter said to him, ‘Lord, not my feet only but also my hands and my head!’” Dump the basin on my head. Give me a shower! And then “Jesus said to him, ‘The one who has bathed does not need to wash, except for his feet, but is completely clean. And you are clean’” (John 13:8–10). Peter is clean. He was chosen, and he was redeemed. Christ’s future work has already applied to him. Now he only needs his feet washed. Confessing sin is a part of daily cleansing (1 John 1:9), and that practice is never inconsistent with being “completely clean.” Peter is a living metaphor for justification and sanctification. And it tells me we can miss what Christ has done for us because we have dirt on our feet. We fixate on washing off the dust every day. We obsess over daily sanctification and forget that Christ washed us clean. Today on Ask Pastor John: how to beat scrupulosity. Today’s question is from a middle-aged man named Dave. “Pastor John, thank you for taking my question. I have struggled for many years with scrupulosity. That’s the word I learned last week while watching YouTube videos. When I looked up that word, scrupulosity, I wept for joy. My obsessive fears have destroyed my peace for many years. And I think I have discovered the root of most of my spiritual challenges and struggle with anxiety. So, now I want to ask you, Pastor John, what advice would you give to a man who has for years been paralyzed by scrupulosity?” There is a similarity between ordinary spiritual attacks that every believer endures, on the one hand, and more sustained obsessions that some believers endure, on the other hand. There’s a similarity. There’s an overlap. In other words, I don’t think we should overstate or understate the peculiar seriousness of what it is to deal with scrupulosity, or what is sometimes called obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Let me try to illustrate what I mean by the overlap between (1) the normal threat of a thought or an image or a behavior becoming an obsession that all of us experience and (2) the more persistent thoughts or images or behaviors that keep returning and returning, and won’t let a person have any rest, like a tick that bites you on the leg and sinks into your skin, and you try to pull it off, but it just grabs on deeper and harder. All of us deal with this danger. I’ve dealt with it personally and written about it, mostly in relation to sexual threats. For example, you inadvertently see some sexually riveting situation — say, a couple having sex on the ground behind your garage. Immediately, that image lodges itself in your consciousness with tremendous force. It threatens to take over. It wants to stay there and be developed in living color by your imagination. You can adapt this situation, this sexual temptation, to whatever your temptation is, whatever the threat of repetition is. You know the kind of thing I’m talking about. What do you do? Here’s my strategy. I’ll just sum it up quickly and then show how it might apply to this issue of scrupulosity. ANTHEM is my technique for handling a situation of threatening preoccupation with thoughts that ought not to be in my head. A: Avoid what triggers the thought or the image. If it’s inadvertent, don’t look back. If you can avoid the trigger in the first place, avoid it. N: Say no out loud to Satan, to your own mind. No — a strong, decisive no. “You will not have dominion over me (Romans 6:14)!” No to that thought, image, or memory. T: Turn your mind to another compelling reality. It might be the bloody body of Jesus hanging on the cross to make you pure. It m
content_zh:
这个感恩节周 欢迎回到播客现场 昨天,我们读到耶稣洗脚 他的门徒在约翰13。 耶稣在地板上从门徒到门徒都用他的水盆工作.

当他到达彼得时,彼得本能地拉回他的脚,说:“你永远不能洗我的脚。” 耶穌回答说:如果我不洗涤你们,那末,你们与我毫无关系。 西门·彼得对他说:我的主啊!我的脚不只是我的,我的手和头也一样。 把盆子扔到我头上 给我洗澡!

然后,耶稣对他说:洗过澡的人,除脚部外,不必洗,但洗得干净。 而你是清白的”(John 13:8-10)。 彼佛清净. 他被选中,被赎回。 基督的未来工作已经适用于他。 现在他只需要洗脚

承认罪恶是日常清洗的一部分(1 John 1:9 ) , 这种做法绝不与“完全干净”相矛盾。 彼是生生比喻说理及圣化. 它告诉我,我们可以错过 基督为我们做了什么,因为我们有 污垢在我们的脚。 我们每天都在洗尘

我们沉迷于日常的圣化 并忘记基督为我们洗净。 今天在"问约翰牧师"上:如何战胜粗心. 今天的问题来自一位中年男子, “约翰神父,谢谢你接受我的问题。 多年来我一直很努力地努力着 上星期我在观看YouTube视频时学到这个词。

当我抬头看那句话,粗心,我为欢乐而哭泣。 我执着的恐惧毁了我多年的和平 我想我已经发现了我大部分精神挑战的根源,与焦虑作斗争.

所以,现在我想问你,约翰牧师,你会给一个多年来因粗心而瘫痪的人什么建议?” 每个信仰者所忍受的普通精神攻击与某些信仰者所忍受的更持久的痴迷之间有相似之处。 也有相似之处。 也有重叠之处。

换句话说,我认为我们不应该夸大或低估处理心烦意乱或有时被称为强迫症(OCD)的特殊严肃性。

让我来解释一下,我所说的重叠是:(1) 一个想法、一个形象或一个行为 成为我们所有人所经历的痴迷的正常威胁;(2) 持续回归和回归的更顽固的思想或图像或行为, 并且不会让一个人得到任何休息, 就像一只咬住你的腿和沉入你的皮肤的虱子,

只是抓住更深,更难。 我们所有人都面对这种危险。 我亲自处理此事, 例如,你无意中看到一些性刺激的情况——比如,一对夫妇在你的车库后面的地面上发生性关系. 即刻,这种形象会以巨大的力量在你的意识中产生。 它威胁要接管。

它想停留在那里,被你的想象所发展成活的颜色. 你可以适应这种情况, 这种性诱惑, 不管你的诱惑是什么, 无论重复的威胁是什么。 你知道我在说什么。 你们做什么的? 以下是我的策略。 我将很快总结一下,

ANTHEM是我的技巧 处理一个威胁 关注的状态 与不应该在我的脑海中的想法。 答:避免引发思想或图像的东西. 如果这是无意的, 若能先避触发者,避之. N:对撒旦大声地说不,对你自己的心灵说不. 不,一个强烈,决定性的不。

你们不能支配我, 没有那种想法,图像,或者记忆。 T:把心转向另一个令人信服的现实。 可能是耶稣挂在十字架上的血腥尸体 让你变得纯洁 这...

title_zh: 您就不能做点新东西吗？
content: How often does church-leadership content online reveal a lightly veiled obsession with new ? The experts today might not come out and say it, but the assumption often seems to be: Surely after two thousand years and all of our light-year advances in technology, the church needs a serious upgrade. Capturing this sentiment, one article insists, “Church leaders face two options. Either battle the marketplace currents and strive to convince enough people to pay for sermon-centric Sunday gatherings, or rethink that model to better fit the realities of making disciples in the twenty-first century.” Someone recently shared a clip with me that illustrates one such updated model. The video features a popular preacher who begins his Sunday sermon by driving a Rolls-Royce onto a stage. Twenty-two screens surround him, and hundreds of light bulbs hang overhead. The “preacher” steps out of the half-a-million-dollar car and takes critics like me head-on: There are some of you who are saying, “Oh man, I can’t believe you drove a Rolls-Royce into church. Man, that’s gimmicky.” No, it’s not; it’s godly. “Oh, that’s trite. That’s flippant.” No, it’s from Christ’s playbook. If you ever go to church and you find yourself bored, blame the communicator, the pastor. Don’t blame God. Yeah, for some reason we go to church and expect boredom. Just the opposite should be true. We are — and this is going to mess you up — we are in the entertainment business. I agree that no one should be bored in church — and I certainly agree that God is not to blame for any boredom in the pews. This preacher’s gimmick implies, however, that the same old formula for church — prayer, singing, fellowship, preaching — can’t possibly keep the attention of modern people like you. Mere sermons won’t cut it. God needs us to spice things up. God is not surprised by our state-of-the-art technology or shriveling attention spans, and he has told us, from the beginning, what captures souls when we gather for worship. He’s told us how to do church, and his counsel hasn’t expired. A Church Anyone Would Want Do you want to hear about a church that was emphatically not bored? They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers. And awe came upon every soul , and many wonders and signs were being done through the apostles. And all who believed were together and had all things in common. And they were selling their possessions and belongings and distributing the proceeds to all, as any had need. And day by day, attending the temple together and breaking bread in their homes, they received their food with glad and generous hearts, praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved. (Acts 2:42–47) Don’t you want to be a part of a church like that? Don’t you want your local church to taste the camaraderie, sacrifice, growth, and joy these people experienced when they gathered? The God-authored recipe is remarkably simple and durable: “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” What did this church do when it grew so wildly and unexpectedly? They gathered. They ate. They gave. They prayed. They preached. And because they devoted themselves to God’s inspired Sunday-service plan, they rejoiced and their numbers multiplied. It’s dumbfounding that we see this kind of church thrive for literally millennia and still conclude it’s time to shake things up. “Sunday sermons got us this far,” we say, “but we’ll take it from here.” What if God knew everything we know — artificial intelligence, fiber-optic internet, driverless cars, those new robot vacuums that can clean stairs — and deliberately told churches to pray, sing, eat, drink, and preach the word anyway? Preaching to Itching Ears God knew exactly what changes and pressures our churches would face in the twenty-first century, and so he warned us t
content_zh:

要么与市场相抗衡,并努力说服足够的人为以布道为中心的星期日集会付出代价,要么重新考虑这一模式,以更好地适应二十一世纪的门徒现实。” 最近有人和我分享了一段片段 展示了这样一个更新的模型

影片的主角是一位受欢迎的传教士, 22个屏幕包围着他 数百个灯泡挂在上方 “掠夺者”走出50万美元的汽车, 你们中有些人说,“哦,我不敢相信你们把劳斯莱斯开进教堂。

这真是令人头痛。 不,它不是;它是上帝的。 “哦,这太老套了。 这简直是一团糟。 不,这是基督的剧本。 如果你去教堂觉得无聊, 责备通讯员,牧师。 别怪上帝。 是啊,出于某种原因,我们去教堂 期待无聊。 正好相反。 我们是在娱乐圈里,这会让你很不爽。

我同意,任何人都不应在教堂感到无聊——我当然也同意,上帝不应为在教堂里发生的任何无聊而责备. 但是,这个传教士的花言巧语意味着,同样的教会老式——祷告、唱歌、研究金、传道——不可能保持像你这样的现代人的注意力。 仅仅布道是不会减少的。 上帝需要我们调味料

上帝对我们最先进的技术并不感到惊讶,或者把注意力伸展在一旁,他从一开始就告诉我们,当我们聚集起来进行礼拜时,什么会捕获灵魂. 他告诉我们如何做礼拜, 教会,任何人都会想要 你想听一个教堂 强烈的不无聊?

他们专心致志于使徒的教诲和善功,敬业和拜功。 敬畏降临每个人,许多奇事和迹象,都是通过使者们实现的。 所有相信的人都在一起 拥有一切共同点 他们正在出售他们的财产和物品, 并按需要向所有人分配收益。

日以同入庙会,并自家断饼取出,以欢喜慷慨之心取取取所取之食,以相赞之,取取所取之恩. 世尊于一日再加所救之众. (第2:42-47号法) 你难道不想加入这样的教会吗?

难道你不想让当地的教会尝到友情、牺牲、成长和欢乐吗? 真主所赐的秘方非常简单而持久: " 他们致力于使徒的教诲和奖学金,致力于断面包和祈祷。 当教堂变得如此疯狂和出人意料时,它做了什么? 他们聚集了起来。 他们吃了。

他们给了。 他们祈祷。 他们传道。 因为他们全心全意地奉真主所启示的礼拜计划,所以他们欢喜而喜,他们的人数倍增。 我们发现这种教堂在几千年里蓬勃发展,

“星期日的布道让我们走得这么远,”我们说,“但我们要从这里走。 ” 如果上帝知道我们所知道的一切—— 人工智能,光纤互联网,无驾驶的汽车,那些能清理楼梯的新机器人真空—— 并故意告诉教会祈祷,唱歌,吃,喝, 以及宣扬这个词呢?

上帝知道21世纪我们的教会会面临什么样的变化和压力 所以他警告我们

title_zh: 对南亚的IMB事工合作伙伴来说，这“只是一个开始”
content: IMB missionary Derrick Waters spent many days in areas like this market, learning his mission field. He made a breakthrough when he met Siraj, who now confidently shares the gospel. IMB Photo The conversation began on a dusty road in rural South Asia. Siraj, a Christian, told Derrick Waters about his desire to share the gospel with Muslims. How could he begin discussions about Christ with his neighbors? After months of training and encouragement, Siraj said, “I will soon share the gospel with 100 Muslims. I know that at least a few will believe.” Waters and his wife, Rosemary, are International Mission Board missionaries who serve in South Asia. His connection with Siraj is a breakthrough in sharing the gospel in this strongly Muslim region. When he first arrived on the mission field, Waters spent his early days getting acclimated to his new community by riding on the back of a motorcycle with a national partner, traveling around and making contacts. “My partner was trying to convince me not to buy a helmet because he said he was a safe driver,” Waters said, though he chose to wear the headgear. “It’s a good thing I wore the helmet because he drove into the back of a truck with a metal bar hanging out that smacked my head.” Surviving the motorcycle ride led to the relational network that eventually allowed Waters to meet Siraj. After they connected, Siraj introduced Waters to Muslim friends and watched him share the gospel. “At first, that’s how it was with Siraj,” Waters said. “But what I really wanted was for him to get involved in the work himself.” A few months later, Waters and local ministry partners traveled to Siraj’s village to lead evangelism training. They discussed God’s love for all people, learned key vocabulary and practiced a straightforward way to share personal testimonies and the story of Jesus. Then came the hard part. Waters began asking Siraj to lead conversations. Siraj stumbled through explanations and searched for the right words. He sprinkled in newly learned terms and nervously worked through the gospel message. Slowly, confidence replaced fear. After another season of ministry together, Siraj told Waters something he would never forget. “Before you came, I didn’t know how to share the gospel with Muslims,” Siraj said. “I wanted to, but I didn’t know how. Now I feel like I can do it.” The transformation became visible during a gathering arranged by a local teacher. Dozens of parents assembled to listen. Siraj stood before them, visibly nervous. His first few sentences faltered. He started, stopped and restarted. Then, something changed. Finding his rhythm, he shared what he had learned, speaking clearly and naturally. He used the vocabulary he had practiced and explained the message of Jesus with growing confidence. By the end of the meeting, the listeners invited the believers to pray for sick family members. They served snacks and chai, thanked them for coming and invited them back. For Waters, it was a glimpse of what God could do through one willing believer. Today, Siraj continues learning and sharing. He studies from a Bible in the local language that helps him engage more effectively with Muslim friends. He distributes Bibles, shares the gospel with coworkers and regularly speaks with people in the villages. This house is part of the village where Siraj lives with his wife, three daughters and his mother. He supports them on the equivalent of US$4 a day, while also farming his land and studying to earn his Ph.D. IMB Photo His enthusiasm is especially remarkable considering his circumstances. Siraj supports his wife, three daughters and his mother on the equivalent of US$4 a day. He farms a small plot of land and studies for exams in hopes of pursuing a Ph.D.  Despite these responsibilities, he continues making time to tell others about Christ. Currently, Siraj is excited about pursuing his goal of sharing the gospel with 100 Muslims. Whether the number is reached quickly or slowly is not the p
content_zh:
IMB的传教士德里克·沃特斯(Derrick Waters)在这样的市场中度过了许多天,学习了他的任务领域. 他在遇到现在充满信心地分享福音的西拉杰时取得了突破. IMB 图片 对话开始于南亚农村的一条尘埃漫漫的道路. 基督教徒西拉杰告诉德里克·沃特斯,他渴望与穆斯林分享福音.

他怎么能开始和邻居讨论基督? 在经过几个月的培训和鼓励之后,Siraj说:“我很快将与100名穆斯林分享福音。 我知道至少少数人会相信。” 沃特斯和他的妻子罗斯玛丽是国际传教委员会传教士,在南亚服务.

他与Siraj的联系是在这个强烈的穆斯林地区分享福音的一个突破。 当他第一次到达任务领域时,沃特斯花了早期时间,通过骑着一辆摩托车背着国家伙伴,四处旅行和进行接触,来适应他的新社区.

“我的搭档试图说服我不要买头盔,因为他说他是安全的司机,”沃特斯说,尽管他选择戴头盔。 “幸好我戴着头盔, 幸存的摩托车骑行导致关系网最终允许沃特斯与Siraj会面.

在他们建立联系后,西拉杰将沃特斯介绍给穆斯林朋友,看着他分享福音. " 沃特斯说, “但我真正想要的是他自己参与这项工作。” 几个月后,Waters和地方部委合作伙伴前往Siraj村,领导福音派培训。

他们讨论了上帝对所有人的爱,学习了关键词汇,并实践了一种直截了当的方法来分享个人证词和耶稣的故事. 然后是困难的部分。 沃特斯开始要求Siraj领导对话. Siraj偶然通过解释,寻找正确的词句。 他用新学的词汇撒水 紧张地工作 通过福音的信息。

慢慢地,信心取代了恐惧。 经过另一季的部会合作,西拉杰告诉沃特斯一些他永远不会忘记的事情. Siraj说:“在你来之前,我不知道如何与穆斯林分享福音。 “我想, 现在,我觉得我可以做到这一点。” 在当地教师安排的一次集会上,转变变得明显。 数十个家长聚集起来听.

Siraj站在他们面前,明显紧张。 他的最初几句话动摇了。 他开始,停止和重启。 然后,事情变了。 在寻找他的节奏时,他分享了他学到的,清晰而自然地说话. 他使用他所练习的词汇,并以越来越大的信心来解释耶稣的旨意.

会议结束前,听众邀请信徒为生病的家属祈祷. 他们为小吃和小柴服务,感谢他们前来邀请他们回来. 对沃特斯来说,这是上帝通过一个愿意的信徒所能做的一瞥。 今天,Siraj继续学习和分享。

他学习当地语言的圣经,帮助他更有效地与穆斯林朋友接触。 他分发圣经,与同事分享福音,并经常与村里的人交谈. 这所房子是Siraj与妻子,三个女儿和母亲住在一起的村庄的一部分.

他支持他们,相当于每天4美元,同时他还耕种自己的土地,并研究获得博士学位的IMB照片。 考虑到他的情况,他的热情特别引人注目。 Siraj每天以相当于4美元的金额支持他的妻子、三个女儿和母亲。 他种了一小块土地 和学习考试 希望追求博士学位。

尽管承担了这些责任,他继续腾出时间告诉别人基督. 目前,Siraj对追求与100名穆斯林分享福音的目标感到兴奋。 数字是快速还是缓慢的不是p
