title: When God’s Word Becomes Personal
source: Wycliffe Bible Translators · 译经故事
summary: Today on the Faithly Podcast, Alicia Lee welcomes Melissa Paredes, Senior Director of Content Marketing at Wycliffe Bible Translators USA, for a meaningful conversation about Bible translation, motherhood, and the life-changing power of Scripture.   The post  When God’s Word Becomes Personal  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
summary_zh: 今天，在Faithly播客上， Alicia Lee欢迎Wycliffe Bible Translators USA内容营销高级总监Melissa Paredes就圣经翻译、母性以及圣经改变生活的力量进行有意义的对话。当上帝的话语成为个人时，这篇文章首先出现在威克里夫。
title_zh: 当神的话变成个人的
content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now
content_zh:

title: Lucky Te Koha: The Gang Member Police Officers Prayed For
summary: 🇳🇿Kaikōura· 2017 (gave his life to Christ)
summary_zh: 🇳🇿凯库拉·2017年（将生命献给基督）
title_zh: Lucky Te Koha：警察为之祈祷的帮派成员
content: A Life in Gangs Lucky Te Koha, a South Islander, was raised by New Zealand's state care system. As a child he was made to stay at Cherry Farm, a state-run mental hospital for adults, a place he remembers plainly: "The abuse in that place was next level." He later found a home in the gang system. Drugs and drink, he says, led to "crime, court cases, police battles, boys' homes, youth prison, prison and rehabs." He moved into an organised crime group, and for 40 years he hated the police. His Third Sunday at Church He began going to Kaikōura New Life Church on New Zealand's South Island. On only his third visit he recognised a police officer who had recently arrested him. During the service Lucky felt intense chest pain. The officer came over and asked if he could pray for him. Four men gathered around him and prayed, and Lucky remembers the chest pain leaving. "I sensed God saying, 'I softened you, giving you a new heart. From here on, you'll feel for others.'" Afterwards he found out that all four men were police officers. His hatred of the police fell away. "I know God delivered me. I sensed that in this house, these were my brothers." Three months from turning 50, he had only ever felt he belonged in gangs, foster homes or prison. "It's a moment only God could've orchestrated." Taking Christ Into Gang Culture Lucky gave his life to Christ in 2017. Under the mentoring of Brian O'Connor, senior pastor of Kaikōura New Life Church, he was ordained in 2019, and in 2021 he founded Kingdom Ministries to take the gospel into gang culture. "Broken people raise broken kids. Hurt people hurt people, but healed people can heal people." God spoke this promise through the prophet Ezekiel: "I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh" (Ezekiel 36:26). In a small church in Kaikōura, with four police officers praying around him, Lucky Te Koha heard God say it to him.
content_zh:
南岛人Gangs Lucky Te Koha的生活由新西兰国家护理系统抚养。 他小时候被逼住到国营成人精神病院樱桃农场(Cherry Farm),他清楚地记得这个地方:"那个地方的虐待是下一个层次". 他后来在帮派系统中找到了一个家.

他说,毒品和饮料导致了"犯罪,法庭案件,警察战斗,男孩之家,青年监狱,监狱和康复". 他搬进一个有组织犯罪集团,40年来他讨厌警察. 他开始去新西兰南岛的新生活教堂。 在第三次访问中,他认出了一名最近逮捕他的警官。

在服役期间,Lucky感受到了强烈的胸痛. 该军官过来问他能否为他祈祷. 四人聚集在他周围祈祷,幸运儿记得胸痛离开. "我感觉到上帝说:"我软化了你,给你一个新的心. "从现在开始,你会为别人着想" 后来,他发现这四人都是警察。 他对警察的仇恨逐渐消失。

"我知道上帝救了我" 我感觉到,在这个房子里, 这些是我的兄弟。" 50岁后三个月,他只觉得自己属于帮派、寄养家庭或监狱。 "这是只有上帝能安排的时刻" 2017年将基督带入江湖文化幸运将生命献给基督.

在凯凯乌拉新生活教会高级牧师布赖恩·奥康纳(英语:Brian O'Connor)的辅导下,他于2019年被授职,2021年他成立了王国各部,将福音带入帮派文化. "破碎的人抚养破碎的孩子。 伤害人伤害人,但治愈的人可以治愈人". 神通过先知以西结说过这个诺言:"我将给你一个新的心,在你心中注入新的精神;

我将清除你的石心,给你肉心"(Ezekiel 36:26). 在凯科乌拉的一座小教堂里,有四名警察在他周围祷告,幸运德·科哈听到了上帝对他说的话.

title: Juan Alberto: A Security Guard Set Free at His Post
summary: 🇦🇷Buenos Aires· 7 to 8 November 2025 (came to faith); 7 June 2026 (baptised)
summary_zh: 🇦🇷布宜诺斯艾利斯·2025年11月7日至8日（归信）；2026年6月7日（受洗）
title_zh: 胡安·阿尔贝托：在岗位上获得自由的保安
content: Twenty-Five Years of Spirit Worship Juan Alberto, 64, lives in Guernica on the outskirts of Buenos Aires, Argentina. For 25 years he practised Quimbanda, an Afro-Brazilian form of spirit worship built around spirit possession and ceremonies that promise success and protection. Tears at the Stadium In November 2025 he was working security at Vélez Sarsfield Stadium for the Esperanza Buenos Aires Festival with Franklin Graham. On the first day, the musicians rehearsing on stage were praising Jesus and singing of His love. Juan Alberto had never heard anything like it. As he listened, the Holy Spirit touched his heart, and he began to weep and could not stop. Soon he felt sick, asked his supervisor if he could go home, and told no one what had happened. The next day his niece Melany, a Christian serving as a prayer volunteer, came to say hello. She told him the Lord had prepared that night for him to feel His love. When Franklin Graham invited people to come forward and receive Jesus, Juan Alberto could not leave his post, so he prayed silently right where he stood. Later that night Melany asked if he had prayed. He said yes, with wet eyes, and told her everything. "He told me he knew and understood that God loved him and forgave him," she said. Idols Burned at His Baptism In the months after the festival he lost his job and his rental home. He kept going to church with Melany at Iglesia Conexión con Dios and joined a small group. On 7 June 2026 he was baptised, and he burned all the idols, garments and spirit-worship objects he had used in Quimbanda. Since then, God has restored his relationships. "I always used to say I was the lost sheep. I never imagined that God would take notice of me," he says. Jesus told of the shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine "and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it" (Luke 15:4). He found Juan Alberto at a security post, in the middle of his shift. "Something extraordinary happened to me. I had an encounter with God, and it was the most beautiful experience of my life."
content_zh:
二十五年精神 宗教 Juan Alberto,64岁,住在阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯郊区的Guernica. 25年来,他一直信奉昆班达教,这是一种非洲裔巴西人的精神崇拜形式,它以拥有精神和仪式为基础,保证成功和保护。

2025年11月,他在Vélez Sarsfield体育场与富兰克林·格雷厄姆一起为Esperanza布宜诺斯艾利斯音乐节工作。 第一天,在舞台上排练的音乐人称赞耶稣并唱出他的爱. 胡安·阿尔贝托从未听过这样的话 他听了,圣灵感动了他的心,他开始哭泣,无法停止.

不久他觉得病了,问他的主管他能否回家,没有告诉任何人发生了什么事. 次日,他的侄女梅拉尼(英语:Melany)作为祈祷志愿者的基督教徒前来打招呼. 她告诉他当晚上帝已经准备让他感受到他的爱

当富兰克林·格雷厄姆邀请人们站出来接受耶稣时,胡安·阿尔贝托无法离开他的岗位,所以他默默地祈祷就站在原地. 当晚晚些时候,梅拉尼问他是否有祷告. 他同意了,用湿眼睛, 告诉她一切。 "他告诉我他知道并理解上帝爱他并原谅了他,"她说.

被洗礼烧伤的偶像 在节日结束后的几个月里,他失去了工作和租房. 他继续和梅拉尼一起在Iglesia Conexión con Dios教堂教堂,并加入了一个小团体. 2026年6月7日,他接受了洗礼,他烧掉了他在昆邦达使用的所有偶像,服装和精神败坏的物品. 此后,上帝恢复了关系.

"我常说我是迷路的羊. 我从未想到上帝会注意到我, 耶稣讲述了牧羊人离开九十九人"追寻失落者,直到他找到"(公爵15:4). 他发现胡安·阿尔贝托在一个保安哨所,在值班中间. "某事非同寻常发生在我身上.

我和上帝相遇过,这是我一生中最美丽的经历".

title: Rakthai Sophia Loibl: Sold as a Child, Brought Back to Life by Jesus
summary: 🇹🇭Bangkok· Over many years before 2025 (published March 2025)
summary_zh: 🇹🇭曼谷·2025 年之前的许多年（2025 年 3 月发布）
title_zh: Rakthai Sophia Loibl：被卖掉的童年，因耶稣而重获新生
content: A Child Sold in Bangkok Rakthai Sophia Loibl's earliest memory is of crying inside a locked supply room in Thailand. When she was 3, her mother was selling her for a few days at a time as a child labourer. When she was around 4, her mother took her to a home in Bangkok, where a man paid 2,000 baht. Her mother never came back. The man was the imam of the local Muslim community, and Rakthai grew up as his slave labourer. Twice she gave birth to his daughters, and twice the baby was taken from her at once. A Gentle Voice At 25, pregnant for the second time, she began to hear a gentle whisper: It's okay. Just stay alive. "I didn't know who or what this voice was, but it comforted me; it was powerful yet gentle." One night, not long after the second birth, the voice woke her at three in the morning and told her to escape through the window. She did. Later she followed a man to Chicago, where for six and a half years he abused her. She tested positive for HIV and developed tuberculosis. Sent back to Bangkok, she lay in hospital for three months, paralysed, unable to see or to remember her own name. In her heart she cried out to Jesus: If you are with me, come save me. The doctors told her relatives to prepare for a funeral. Afraid she was contagious, they put her in a small house far from their homes in the village to wait for her to die. For six weeks she had only water. Then the voice spoke again: Live. "In that little house, I understood that it had been Jesus' voice all along," she says. "My wounds healed and my spirits lifted." One day she stumbled out of the wooden house, and her family, the villagers and the doctors were shocked. A pastor who had visited her in hospital brought her to a ministry called The Well, and there she gave her life to Jesus. Bread for the Imam God called her back to the community she had escaped, to forgive them and to love them. About eight years later the imam, dying of cancer, phoned and asked to see her. "I sat next to him as he lay bedridden, and he asked me to forgive him." Then he asked for bread and coffee. She remembered Jesus' command to love her enemies, handed him the bread, and felt the chains in her heart break. Before he died, the imam asked if she wanted her daughters back. Both now live with her. Rakthai founded Walk with Love, a Bangkok ministry to people in desperate situations across Thailand. "I am living proof that God is working in the darkness."
content_zh:
曼谷的Rakthai Sophia Loibl最早的记忆是, 3岁时,她的母亲一次以童工身份出卖她几天. 在她4岁左右的时候,她的母亲带她到曼谷的一家家庭,一个男人在那里支付了2000铢. 她妈妈再也没有回来

此人是当地穆斯林社区的伊玛目,拉克泰作为奴隶劳工长大. 她两次生下他的女儿,两次一次把孩子从她身边带走。 一个温柔的声音在25岁, 怀孕了第二次, 她开始听到一个温柔的低语: 没事的 只要活着。 "我不知道是谁或是什么声音,但它安慰了我;

它强大而温柔" 一天晚上,在第二次出生不久后,声音在凌晨三点叫醒她,叫她从窗户逃走. 没错 后来她跟随一个男人去了芝加哥,在那里他虐待了她六年半的时间. 她检测出艾滋病毒呈阳性,并患上了肺结核。

她被送回曼谷,在医院里躺了三个月,瘫痪,无法看到或想起自己的名字。 在她的心中,她向耶稣喊叫: 如果你和我一起,来救我。 医生让她的亲戚准备葬礼 他们把她关在离他们家很远的小房子里,等着她死。 六周来她只有水

然后声音又说:生活。 "在那个小房子里,我明白这一直是耶稣的声音,"她说. "我的伤口痊愈,我的精神被解除" 一天,她从木屋中滑出,她的家人,村民和医生都感到震惊. 一位牧师曾到医院探望她,把她带到一个名为The Well的部里,在那里她把生命献给了耶稣.

为伊玛目神的面包把她召回了她已经逃离的社区,以宽恕和爱他们. 大约8年后,伊玛目死于癌症,打电话要求见她。 "我坐在他旁边,他躺在床上, 他要求我原谅他。" 然后他问面包和咖啡。

她记得耶稣命令要爱她的敌人,将面包交给他,并感觉到她心中的锁链断裂. 临死前,伊玛目问她是否想要女儿们回来. 现在都和她住在一起 Rakthai为泰国各地的绝望人士成立了曼谷部, "我活在证明上帝在黑暗中工作"

title: Maxym Abramov: From Occupied Sloviansk to Army Chaplain
summary: 🇺🇦Sloviansk· 2014 (came to faith); 5 May 2022 (wounded)
summary_zh: 🇺🇦斯洛维扬斯克·2014年（归信）；2022年5月5日（受伤）
title_zh: 马克西姆·阿布拉莫夫：从被占领的斯洛维扬斯克到军队牧师
content: A City Struck In 2014 Maxym Abramov was a 16-year-old schoolboy in Sloviansk, in eastern Ukraine, getting ready to finish school. On 12 April that year Russia first struck his hometown, and the city was occupied. The occupation shattered the way he saw life. Depression closed in, and it drove him to the edge of suicide. That was when he found Christ. "My material world simply collapsed like a house of cards," he says. Two Metres Away Before he joined the army, Maxym volunteered at a rehabilitation centre for people struggling with addiction. Later he signed a contract with the army. On 5 May 2022, in the third month of the full-scale war, his unit held a stretch of front line under a barrage that lasted more than 12 hours. A fellow soldier sitting two metres behind him was hit in the neck by shrapnel and died instantly. Maxym was wounded in the arm. He was ordered to reach the evacuation point about a kilometre away, and he ran, fell, got up and ran again under fire. At the hospital in Bakhmut the doctors looked at his arm and said things looked grim. "The damage was so severe, I still don't know how God saved it. But He did." A Chaplain Who Listens In December 2024 Maxym became a certified military chaplain. He studies at Kremenchuk Seminary and the Ostroh Academy, and he cares for soldiers, veterans and the families of the fallen, the captured and the missing. "I've earned the right to speak to them about hope," he says. "But more often, my job is simply to listen." God met a teenager at the edge of his life in an occupied city. Eight years later, in a hospital in Bakhmut, He saved the arm the doctors said looked grim. "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4).
content_zh:
A City Struck 2014 Maxym Abramov是乌克兰东部斯洛维安斯克的16岁在校生,准备完成学业. 当年4月12日,俄罗斯首次袭击他的家乡,该城被占领. 占领摧毁了他对生活的看法。 抑郁症收缩了,使他陷入了自杀的边缘. 那时他发现了基督。

他说:“我的物质世界就像一栋牌屋一样崩溃了。” 在他入伍前,两个梅特雷斯·阿威(英语:Two Metres Away)志愿在一个康复中心为那些为瘾君子挣扎的人服务. 后来他与军队签订了合同. 2022年5月5日,在全面战争的第三个月中,他的部队在长达12小时以上的炮火下保持了前线的伸展.

一名坐在他身后两米的士兵被弹片击中颈部,当场死亡。 Maxym手臂受伤。 他被命令到达约一公里外的疏散点,他跑,倒,起来,又在火力下跑. 在Bakhmut的医院,医生看着他的手臂,说事情看起来很惨淡。 "损失如此严重,我仍然不知道上帝是如何挽救的.

但是,他做到了。" 2024年12月,马克西姆成为一名经认证的军事牧师。 他在克勒门丘克神学院和奥斯特罗学院学习,他关心士兵,退伍军人和阵亡者家属,俘虏和失踪者. "我赢得了跟他们谈论希望的权利,"他说.

"但更常见的是,我的工作只是倾听。" 上帝在被占领城市遇到一个少年 八年后,在Bakhmut的一家医院里,他救了医生说看起来很惨的手臂。 "即使我走过死亡之阴谷,我也不会害怕邪恶,因为你与我同在"(第23:4段)。

title: Telemachus: The Monk Who Stepped Into the Arena
summary: 🇮🇹Rome· c. AD 404 (traditional date; Theodoret gives none)
summary_zh: 🇮🇹罗马·约公元404年（传统日期；Theodoret未提供日期）
title_zh: 特勒马科斯：踏入竞技场的僧侣
content: A Monk From the East Theodoret, a bishop of Cyrrhus in Syria who wrote a history of the Church in the fifth century, recorded this account. A man named Telemachus had "embraced the ascetic life": he was a monk. He left the East and travelled to Rome. Into the Arena In Rome the gladiatorial games still went on. Gladiators fought before crowds for entertainment, and a fight could end in death. From the time of Constantine, imperial laws had put limits on the games, and the fights continued. On a day when the games were on, Telemachus went into the stadium. He stepped down into the arena and tried to stop the men who were fighting each other with their weapons. The crowd was furious. In Theodoret's words, they "stoned the peacemaker to death." What Theodoret Says the Emperor Did When the emperor Honorius heard what had happened, Theodoret writes, he "numbered Telemachus in the array of victorious martyrs, and put an end to that impious spectacle." What Historians Say Theodoret gives no date. Tradition places the event around AD 404, and the Church remembers Telemachus on 1 January. Historians still debate the account. An older list of martyrs records a Roman martyr called Almachius on 1 January, and some scholars think Theodoret's story grew from that record. Others treat the two men as different martyrs. Recent studies also question whether Honorius issued a ban on the games in 404. Remembered Because Someone Wrote It Down Jesus said, "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God" (Matthew 5:9). In Theodoret's account, Telemachus has that same name: the peacemaker. Theodoret kept this story, and more than sixteen hundred years after its traditional date, Christians still tell it. It shows what peacemaking can cost: one man saw people kill each other for a crowd's entertainment, and he stepped in to stop it.
content_zh:
一个来自东西奥多的僧人,叙利亚的西尔胡斯主教,他写了5世纪的教会历史,记录了这一说法. 一个叫Telemachus的人曾"拥抱了乙酸盐的生活":他是一个僧侣. 他离开东方,前往罗马. 进入罗马的竞技场 角斗士游戏仍在继续 角斗士在人群前为娱乐而战,一场战斗可能会以死亡结束.

从君士坦丁时代起,帝国法律就对游戏设置了限制,战斗仍在继续. 在比赛开始的一天,Telemachus进入了体育场. 他下台进入竞技场,试图阻止那些用武器互相战斗的人. 大众大怒.

用西奥多的话说,他们"把和平缔造者砸死". 狄奥多莱特说,当皇帝霍诺利乌斯听到发生的事情时, 他写道,“在胜利的烈士阵营中,他把Telemachus数起来,并结束那场无礼的景象。” 历史学家说狄奥多莱特没有约会

传统将活动放在AD 404周围,教会在1月1日记得Telemachus. 历史学家仍然争论这个账户. 一份较古老的烈士名单记载了1月1日一位名叫阿尔马奇乌斯的罗马烈士,一些学者认为西奥多特的故事从该记录中发展起来. 其他人则视两人为不同的烈士. 最近的研究也质疑Honorius在404年是否发布禁赛令.

记得因为有人写下耶稣说:"和平缔造者有福,因为他们将被称为上帝的儿子"(Matthew 5:9). 在西奥多特的叙述中,Telemachus也有这个名字:和平缔造者. 西奥多保留了这个故事,在它的传统日期之后的1600多年里,基督徒们仍然告诉它.

它显示了建立和平的代价:一个人看到人们为了群众的娱乐而互相残杀,他介入阻止.

title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
summary_zh: 🇪🇷厄立特里亚·21世纪10年代
title_zh: 他在自己工作的医院被捕，并将监狱变成了讲坛。
content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.
content_zh:
Berhane博士是耶稣的新信徒,在厄立特里亚的一家医院工作,当时秘密警察来找他。 他的罪行是他的信仰。 他们把他关进监狱11个月,在地球上最严酷的系统之一,一个旨在使基督徒消失和安静的地方. 他做的恰恰相反。

"每天我拍手,"他说:"囚犯会站出来,我分享福音". 一个刚认识耶稣的人决定 他的牢房只是下一个介绍他的地方 三个圣经和一个死亡之谷 当局拿走了他的圣经。 他又偷渡进来了 他们也拿走了那个 他走私了三分之一

他极力倚靠"诗经",当狱友被带出处死时,关于走过死亡阴影谷的老台词不再是诗歌,成为了扶他站直的东西. 11个月没有打倒他。 这让他成了传教士。 守卫们打算让新基督徒安静下来,反而给了他一个无处可去的会众.

无论他们把你放在哪里,耶稣都跟着你,他不受墙壁的恐吓. Berhane博士在厄立特里亚的一所监狱发现了这一点。 你可以相信它 无论你在哪里。

title: A construction engineer in Madagascar became convinced the Bible was true
summary: 🇲🇬Madagascar· 2013
summary_zh: 🇲🇬马达加斯加·2013年
title_zh: 一位在马达加斯加的建筑工程师确信圣经是真的
content: Melias was building things for a living in Madagascar, a construction engineer with a steady trade and, by his own account, no particular expectation that God would interrupt him. In 2013, at twenty-one, God did. It was not dramatic thunder. It was quieter and harder to argue with. "The Holy Spirit convinced my heart that the Bible is true," Melias said. "I found new joy and excitement learning about Jesus through the Scriptures." The book he might have dismissed became the most alive thing in his life. From building houses to building the church He could have kept his new faith as a private comfort and gone on with engineering. Instead he gave it everything. In 2015 he trained for six months as a missionary, and since then he has planted churches and discipled new believers among the Tanala people in Ikongo and the Sakalava in Nosy Be, some of the least reached corners of the island. Now he is training three more Malagasy missionaries to do the same. Madagascar is not a footnote in what God is doing. He is raising up local people like Melias, engineers and tradesmen and ordinary workers, and sending them to their own unreached neighbours. When the Holy Spirit convinces your heart that this is all true, it does not stay a hobby. It becomes the thing you build your life around. He is ready to convince yours.
content_zh:
梅利亚斯在马达加斯加为生计而建东西,他是一位稳定的建筑工程师,据他自己说,他并不特别期望上帝会打断他。 2013年,21时,上帝做到了. 这不是戏剧性的雷声。 更安静,更难争论 "圣灵使我的心相信圣经是真的,"梅利亚斯说.

"我发现新的快乐和兴奋 通过圣经学习耶稣。" 他可能放弃的书 成为他一生中最活的 从建房到建教堂 他本可以保持他作为私人慰藉的新信仰,继续从事工程工作. 相反,他给了它一切。

2015年,他作为传教士接受了半年的训练,此后他在伊孔戈的塔纳拉人和诺西贝的萨卡拉瓦人中种植了教堂和门徒新信徒,其中部分到达的岛角最少. 现在他正在训练另外三名马达加斯加传教士, 马达加斯加不是上帝所作所为的一个脚注。

他正在培养梅利亚斯,工程师和商人以及普通工人等当地人,并将他们送到他们自己无法接触到的邻居那里. 当圣灵说服你的心脏 这一切都是真的, 它不仍然是爱好。 它成为你围绕你生活的东西。 他准备说服你

title: A New Testament sat in his welding workshop until a teenager finally read it
summary: 🇳🇪Agadez· 2000s
summary_zh: 🇳🇪阿加德兹·21世纪初
title_zh: 一本新约圣经一直放在他的焊接车间里，直到一位少年终于读了它。
content: Someone left a New Testament in Pierre's welding workshop in Niger, and for a while it just sat there. He was a teenager, and eventually he picked it up. What he read did not match what he had been told about Christians. It was full of tenderness, of nearness to the poorest, exactly the kind of world his young heart had been quietly hoping was real. Years later he moved to Agadez, out toward the desert, and there he found the thing the book had described. A church family drawn from Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, France, and Niger, living out what he had only read about. No regret, not for a single day Pierre became a lay missionary, and he does not hedge when he talks about it. "I have never regretted converting to the Christian faith," he says, "not even for a single day." That is a bold thing to say in Niger, where jihadist groups make following Jesus dangerous and his own children have stayed Muslim, something he carries with love and without pressure. Still, no regret. Not one day. He read about a God who is tender toward the poor, and he found that God to be exactly as advertised. Whatever you have heard about Jesus secondhand, He holds up when you finally meet Him yourself. Pierre would tell you to open the book and see.
content_zh:
有人在尼日尔的皮埃尔焊接车间留下了一份新约, 他少年时期,最终他捡到了. 他所读的内容与他被告知的基督徒的情况不符。 它充满了温柔,与最贫穷的人的亲近, 正是他年轻时所希望的世界是真实的。

多年后,他搬到阿加德兹, 向着沙漠, 在那里他发现了书上描述的东西。 一个来自贝宁、多哥、布基纳法索、法国和尼日尔的教会家庭,靠他只读过的东西生活。 没有遗憾,没有一天,皮埃尔成为了一名非专业的传教士,他谈论这件事时不设套.

"我从未后悔过皈依基督教信仰",他说:"即使是一天也没有". 在尼日尔,这是一件大胆的事,在那里,圣战团体追随耶稣,而他自己的孩子则留在穆斯林手中,他带着爱,没有压力。 不过,没有遗憾。 一日不见.

他曾诵读了真主--对于贫民是温和的--他发现真主确是彻知的。 无论你听到什么关于耶稣的二手消息 当你们终于亲眼见到他时 他都挺过来了 Pierre会告诉你打开书看看

title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
title_zh: 他被教导说基督徒不祷告。然后，他看到叔叔在饭前祷告。
content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.
content_zh:
查尔斯·亚巴加·迪亚拉(Charles Yabaga Diarra)在马里勒尔一个严格的穆斯林家庭长大,在那里基督徒受到嘲笑和误解. 他的父亲是一名校长和政治家,他像学校一样管理着房子. 童年时,查尔斯逃离了大约一百五十英里,与一个叔叔住在一起,在那里,他直接遇到了他被告知的东西并不存在.

他的叔叔,一位基督教牧师,低头祷告,在饭前祷告. 查尔斯被惊呆了 "因为我们是基督徒,我们吃饭前祈祷",叔叔解释道. 查尔斯被告知基督徒根本不祷告 用他自己的语言祈祷,他不会离开。

只要告诉我他父亲把他拉回来的方式 强迫他进入古兰经学校 但种子是种的 多年之后,与他的叔叔一起回来,疲惫和寻找,查尔斯终于自己祈祷. "主啊,我真的厌倦了寻找真相. "给我带路" 他在一所假期圣经学校听到的一首诗回到了他身边,1981年11月他把生命献给了耶稣.

代价是真实的。 查尔斯现在是一名传教士,因马里的冲突而流离失所,每天都面临压力。 但他没有一个人去。 他的十四个兄弟姐妹中,大多数现在都跟随耶稣,大约一百名基督徒聚集在他的大家庭活动中. 一个叔叔为晚餐祷告 整个家庭都向耶稣倾斜 你安静的,普通的忠诚 可能是种更多 比你知道。

title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
summary: Laos· 2022
title_zh: 一位寡妇从一位推销员那里听到了好消息，从此念念不忘。
content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.
content_zh:
裴 was在老挝是一位52岁的寡妇,养大了整个村庄的养殖方式,在政府推崇无神论的地方崇拜祖先和地方灵灵,邻居警告说,追随外国人神会冒犯家乡神灵. 然后一个推销员走过来,在出售他的商品之间,告诉她耶稣的事. 救世是礼物,不是报酬

裴 believed信之. 她放弃了她毕生怀念的祖先的崇拜,悄悄地跟随耶稣. 在她自己的前门付出的代价 她被秘密地关了四个月, 变得足够强大,可以说话。 她告诉的第一个人是她的女儿和女婿,她们碰巧是一名警察。 他们没有庆祝。

他威胁她,说如果她不停止相信耶稣,他们会告发她,监禁她,或者把她赶出去. 6月,他们在上面做得很好,把她的衣服扔到院子里,并告诉她去和给她这个耶稣的人一起生活. 她去了 她去了吗? 她没有回去。 一个什么都没有的寡妇选择了耶稣 而不是一个屋顶, 因为她已经发现了一些没人能从她的心脏里赶走的东西。

追随耶稣并不总是安全的,但总是值得的. 裴氏发现的比付出的代价更值钱,也是献给你的.

title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
summary_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦和塔吉克斯坦·2020年代
title_zh: 女儿被杀后，他祈祷能拥有一本无人能夺走的圣经
content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.
content_zh:
拉希德·卡迪罗夫(Rashid Kadirov)是中亚穆斯林,当时最糟糕的事情发生了. 他的六岁女儿Azizza被驾拖拉机喝醉的邻居杀死. 在悲痛中,他去寻找可以安息的东西,他去了可兰经. 在那里,他读到了一行,在苏拉5:70中,指向福音书作为圣经. 所以他祈祷了一个奇怪的,具体的祈祷.

他向上帝祈求"印吉尔","新约". 他的朋友给他带来了一个。 是一辆被偷来的吉迪恩圣经 从被破坏的汽车上拍下来的 它没有持续。 当朋友们收回它时,拉希德再次祈祷,这次要一本圣经,没有人能夺走他. 留下来的书 之后一对夫妇从塔吉克斯坦赶来,他们是由自己来到基督的前同学派来的.

他们携带了圣经和JESUS电影的拷贝. 拉希德和他的妻子阿莱卡观看了,正如好消息被解释的那样,他们每个人都在不告诉对方的情况下悄悄地祈祷要接受耶稣. 阿莱卡根本不懂这些

"她对福音几乎没有什么了解,"后来她说,"然而和平却淹没了她的心. 他们在塔吉克斯坦接受洗礼,拉希德开始告诉其他人他发现了什么. 一个悲伤的父亲要求一本书,上帝给了他一个人. 和平拉希德无法在耶稣到达的时候制造。 他与心碎者密不可分,他与你们密不可分。

title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
summary_zh: 北中央省
title_zh: 35位神父都无法帮助她。在教堂里，她看到耶稣粉碎了正在扼住她喉咙的东西。
content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.
content_zh:
钱德拉住在斯里兰卡中北部省的一个乡村,她慢慢地分崩离析. 痛苦,软弱,一个无缘无故的心脏 医生无法命名 她和她的家人是印度教徒,所以他们做了他们知道的事。 他们跟随牧师去了牧师那里. 三十五门. 什么都没有改变。 2021年7月,他们走进了一座教堂。

当人们为她祈祷时,钱德拉看到了一些东西. 恶魔试图掐死她,然后耶稣基督介入并盖在他们身上. 她感到痛苦和疾病 排出她的身体 当他们被打败。 在视觉中,耶稣说圣经 超过她,从Psalm 34。 他说:他们崇拜他,而且赞颂他超绝万物。他说:她也超绝万物,如果她信任他。

一个父亲祈祷她的丈夫迪尼什(Dinesh),一个白天的劳工,看着他的妻子复活,并给上帝一个承诺. "上帝,如果你能治愈我的妻子, 我将奉献我的女儿为你服务。" 几乎听不到耶稣之名的全家都为他献出了生命.

他们的女儿特努沙告诉了班上所发生的事情,她的母亲是自由的,耶稣宽恕了罪人,使他们成为新人. 他们没有保守秘密。 一所房屋教堂在他们家中开始,共有4人. 时已四十六. 耶稣仍然比任何 扼杀你生命的东西更强大 他走进来,他把它印下来,他叫你光辉。

title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
summary_zh: 🇸🇩哈萨希萨·2022年
title_zh: 他为母亲感染的腿祈祷。然后，他的穆斯林邻居开始前来
content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.
content_zh:
Abdalla Haron Sulieman牧师在苏丹El Hasahisa聚集了他的小教堂,为其母亲祈祷。 艾莎·亚当六十岁 腿部感染使她疲惫不堪 他们祈祷,她恢复了。 看起来像一个私人家庭的怜悯 并没有长期保持私人。 关于治愈的传言传遍了大部分是穆斯林的城镇。 人们开始出现在教堂。 不为辩才.

问治愈艾莎的神能否治愈他们 当治愈变成一扇门 这正是那种让人害怕的东西。 当地的极端分子逼迫警察逮捕苏利曼,他们确实如此,根据旧法指控他自称巫医,仿佛对耶稣的爱是一种巫术.

苏丹各地的信徒都认同他的名字,要求释放他。 "这是对苏丹基督徒的严重侵犯",一位名叫弗朗西斯·伊斯梅尔的福音者说. 但请注意恐惧无法消除 一个母亲很好 一个穆斯林城镇看到了耶稣的名字做一些真实的事情,从未进入教堂的邻居走进教堂寻找他.

上帝仍然痊愈,他仍然使用一个普通的应答祷告来打开一个没人能关闭的门. 他可以打开一个你的地方。

title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
summary_zh: 拉基拉基·1990年代
title_zh: 因果报应说他必须修功德才能上天堂。17岁时，他听说自己可以得到宽恕。
content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.
content_zh:
西蒙·古德出生于斐济一个严格的印度教家庭. 他的曾祖父在1874年英国人攻占群岛后,作为合同工从印度被运走,全家定居在维提莱武北部的一个小村庄. 西蒙在一个有明确规则的系统中长大. "作为一个印度教徒,我们相信因果报应,"他说. "若作善因缘即得上天.

若作恶报果报果报果. " 这是他无法平衡的分类账 他对自己的错误太了解了 结账的那一晚 17岁时,一位朋友邀请他到另一个城镇的一次基督教青年会议. 在那里,他听到一些不符合他所教过的东西。 耶稣基督可以宽恕罪过

不抵消它们, 也不平均出一生。 原谅他们 西蒙感受到了自己失败的轻重,并首次提出摆脱这些失败. "当晚我把生命交给耶稣,"他说. 起初他瞒着父母 当他们发现, 他们不高兴。 但回家的儿子变了 并没有停下来。

时他带领全家来到基督身边,他继续栽培一个对别人同样怀有宽恕的部. 卡玛一直有追踪器 你永远无法清除 耶稣撕开标签。 无论你今晚携带什么 他现在仍然要马上原谅这一切

title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
title_zh: 一名本应死于战斗的士兵走进了恶魔的神殿
content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.
content_zh:
牧师达诺在担任牧师之前是一名军人. 他毫无理由地活着走出战场,从未动摇过为什么的感官. "我相信上帝为了某种目的在战场上拯救了我的生命". 宗旨现于一佛村中欲与他无相. 副宰相的儿子被折磨,妖魔吞噬,无人能助.

达诺斋戒祈祷三天. 然后,近午夜,他去了男孩所在的神殿,做了他唯一知道该做的事. "我呼唤天主之名,"他说:"妖魔离开了少年. 夜神社失声村民说 每一个邪恶的灵魂 立刻离开村庄

达诺从神社到神社,祈祷反抗历代统治这个地方的黑暗. 副局长的家族,他为愤怒而坚韧不拔,却找到了恩典。 他们把生命献给了耶稣,还有四个家庭随行. 曾经反对他的人现在遵循他的路线。 今天村里有一座教堂 曾经有神社

耶稣的名字仍然比每件令你害怕的黑暗事物更强大. 一个信徒在午夜祈祷 足以让整个村庄自由

title_zh: 美国长老会（PCUSA）——一位被按立的牧师声称上帝是非二元性别和跨性别者，错误地引用了希腊语词汇

content: Antes de escribir la biografía de Jorge Bergoglio, que llamó El gran Reformador, Austen Ivereigh ya era un experto en la historia de la Iglesia argentina. “Mi tesis de doctorado [en Oxford], que terminé en el 92, fue sobre catolicismo y política en la Argentina”. Y hay más: “Debo mi fe a la Iglesia Argentina, leyendo artículos de monseñor (Gustavo) Franceschi, volví a la fe”, dice. Ese conocimiento de nuestro país y de su fe mayoritaria representó una ventaja a la hora de escribir sobre Bergoglio, ya que cada etapa de la trayectoria del futuro Papa está debidamente contextualizada en la época que atravesaba el país. Desde aquel marzo de 2013, cuando la novedad de un pontífice argentino y jesuita impactó al mundo entero, Ivereihg siempre pensó que vendría cuando Francisco visitara la Argentina, viaje que finalmente no se concretó. “Ahora vengo con León”, comenta. En efecto, este escritor, historiador, periodista y analista de asuntos religiosos y políticos estará en nuestro país contemporáneamente con la visita del papa León XIV, invitado por la Universidad del Salvador (USAL), donde dictó, el pasado viernes 6, una clase magistral sobre “El giro latinoamericano Francisco-León: la Iglesia misionera sinodal y el cambio de época”. Ivereigh también es co-autor de Let Us Dream (Soñemos Juntos, 2020), un libro escrito en colaboración con Francisco. Su trabajo más reciente es First Belong to God: On Retreat with Pope Francis (Lo primero es pertenecer a Dios: Un retiro con el Papa Francisco, 2024), basado en los escritos y charlas de Bergoglio como director espiritual de un retiro ignaciano de 8 días. De 2004 a 2006, Ivereigh fue colaborador del entonces arzobispo de Westminster, cardenal Cormac Murphy-O’Connor, uno de los más activos promotores de la candidatura de Jorge Mario Bergoglio al papado. Ivereigh considera que el papado de Francisco inició un giro latinoamericano hacia una iglesia misionera y sinodal, cuyo primer paso fue la exhortación apostólica Evangelii Gaudium (noviembre de 2013), sobre “el anuncio del Evangelio en el mundo actual”, con la cual, dice, “Francisco inaugura una hoja de ruta de su Papado que también es la del pontificado de León”. Pero esa hoja de ruta tenía una génesis anterior: el ya famoso documento de Aparecida, la V Conferencia General del Episcopado Latinoamericano y del Caribe (Celam), redactado por Bergoglio. De esta manera, “América Latina pasó a ser la iglesia fuente”, señala, porque “siempre hay una parte de la Iglesia de la cual brota un dinamismo teológico”. Antes, ese rol lo cumplía Europa, pero a partir del Concilio Vaticano II eso cambia porque es en América Latina donde mejor se lo pone en práctica. Aclara que “fuente” no quiere decir centro; de hecho, “Francisco quería una Iglesia multipolar”. — ¿Hasta qué punto Aparecida refleja a Bergoglio como individualidad y hasta dónde es la Iglesia latinoamericana, que usted define como “fuente”? — El proceso de preparación de esa conferencia general, fue muy sinodal, de mucha consulta, y el papel de Bergoglio en esa conferencia general es muy conocido. Creo que influyó la recepción del Concilio Vaticano II en el Río de La Plata, que tuvo un matiz distinto al resto de América Latina. Tal vez, cuando llegó a Aparecida esa visión sobre la religiosidad popular estaba ya madura. Es decir, una teología de espiritualidad latinoamericana, distinta a anteriores teologías latinoamericanas. Bergoglio tenía muchas cosas que eran de él. Pero también llevaba en su forma de ser y de pensar muchos aportes de la iglesia argentina, la influencia de Lucio Gera y de Rafael Tello y toda esa tradición. — ¿Cómo vio el impacto de su papado en la Argentina? — Creo que una de las razones por las que no vino, sobre todo al principio, fue que tenía horror del triunfalismo. Y sabía que tal vez los argentinos tenían —todos los países lo tienen— una cierta tentación de decir: “El Papa es argentino”. Y si le tenía tanto rechazo al triunfalismo, era porque éste pone a uno en el ce

content: Happy Thanksgiving to my American friends and family. I pray you have a restful and thankful day. As you feast, I’ll be prepping a roundup of Black Friday deals that are of interest to Christians, so be sure to check in tomorrow for that. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include the repackaged edition of J.I. Packer’s classic A Quest for Godliness , Tim Chester’s Isaiah for You , Brant Hansen’s Blessed Are the Misfits , and more. Recommended Reading Evangelicalism and ‘High’ Culture. Michael Jensen writes about the lack of Evangelical influence in high culture. “There’s good reasons for this absence. The instinct of true Christianity is thoroughly egalitarian, in recognition of the significance of every human individual and the universal appeal of the gospel. Elitism is abhorrent to true Christianity and especially to missionary Christianity. As Davison Hunter says, ‘elitism for believers is despicable and utterly anathema to the gospel they cherish’.” Reflection on a Public Memorial Service. Kraig Keck tells movingly about his experience at a public memorial service for two police officers who were killed in the line of duty. “Each element of the memorial service evoked powerful emotions in me. As I sat there I was struck by the dignity and honor of it all, and I wondered how a committed atheist evolutionist would understand this. I’m sure he would try to find some evolutionary purpose for it all, but it seemed to me that it would be ultimately unexplainable by his worldview. Why the ceremony, the quiet, the traditions, the dignity, and the honor of it all?” The Pilgrims Did Not Invent Thanksgiving. Allen C. Guelzo reminds American readers that the Pilgrims were not the ones who invented Thanksgiving. “To be sure, the Massachusetts Pilgrims probably did host a harvest dinner in 1621 to mark their survival through their first year in America. But the Thanksgiving we celebrate annually in November had its real origins much closer to the present, and its real designer not in William Bradford or William Brewster, but in the sixteenth president of the United States, Abraham Lincoln.” Quarters and Contentment. Marie Garreau explains how she has sometimes found it easier to be content during times of extreme distress than during “normal” difficulties. “The Lord gave me contentment in that season of extreme need, while in times of lesser need I have found it easier to slip from the confidence of his provision. Perhaps I lose sight of the fact that it is not just in extreme times of need that the circumstances of our lives are completely out of our own hands.” Are We Asking Too Much of Our Kids? Beth Barthelemy asks a question a lot of Christian parents wonder about, and perhaps especially those in missions or other forms of ministry: Are we asking too much of our kids? “As full-time ministry workers, my husband and I have anticipated and accepted all kinds of sacrifices on behalf of working for the kingdom. For our years overseas, those sacrifices looked like family, a sense of security, and cultural familiarity, among others. In pastoral ministry now, these sacrifices are financial, relational, and of our time. We are still discovering others.” Do We Have a Spirit of Entitlement or a Spirit of Gratitude? Randy Alcorn: “Ingratitude is not just wrong thinking—it’s the source of endless wrong thinking. An ungrateful person not only offends God, but is also the source of his own misery, and a cancer to others, spreading his misery. Ungrateful people are not only ungrateful to God but to their families and friends and co-workers and neighbors. They’re ungrateful to their church leaders, and quick to judge and condemn everyone for falling short of their standards.” Flashback Proven Faith Is More Precious than Gold. It can be difficult to make sense of our trials as we endure them. But the Bible always assures us that our difficulties are never purposeless but always in some way purposeful. God is always using them to accomplish somethin

Kraig Keck 感动地讲述了他在公开追悼仪式上为两名在执勤中丧生的警官的经历. “追悼会的每一个内容都激起了我强烈的情绪。 当我坐在那里时,我对这一切的尊严和荣誉深感震惊,我想知道一个执着的无神论进化主义者会如何理解这一点.

但在我看来, 他的世界观是无法解释的。 为什么仪式,安静,传统,尊严,以及一切荣誉?” 朝圣者没有发明感恩节 艾伦·C·盖尔佐提醒美国读者,朝圣者并非发明感恩节的人.

“当然,马萨诸塞朝圣者们很可能在1621年举办了丰收晚宴,以纪念他们在美国度过第一年的生存。

但我们每年11月庆祝的感恩节,其真正的起源远近于现在,其真正的设计者并非威廉·布拉德福德或威廉·布鲁斯特,而是美国第十六任总统亚伯拉罕·林肯". 四方与内容.

Marie Garreau解释了她如何有时发现在极端困难时期比“正常”困难时期更容易满足。 “在那个极为需要的季节,上帝给予我满足,而在不太需要的时候,我发现更容易从他所提供的信任中溜走。

或许我忽视了这样一个事实,即我们的生活环境不仅在极端需要的时候,而且完全不能靠自己。” 我们问太多我们的孩子了吗? Beth Barthelemy向许多基督教家长提出一个问题, 我们要求太多孩子了吗?

“作为专职的部委工作人员,我和我丈夫期望并接受为王国工作的各种牺牲。 在我们海外的岁月中,这些牺牲看起来像家庭、安全感和文化熟悉等。 在现在的牧业部,这些牺牲是财政、关系和我们时代的牺牲。

我们还在发现其他人。” 难道我们有应享的精神和恩惠的精神吗? Randy Alcorn:“忘恩负义不仅仅是错误的想法, 一个忘恩负义的人不仅冒犯了上帝,而且也是他自己痛苦的根源,也是对他人的癌症,分散了他的痛苦.

忘恩负义的人不仅对上帝不感恩,而且对家人和朋友以及同事和邻居也不感恩。 他们对教会领袖忘恩负义, 闪回证明信仰比黄金更珍贵 在我们忍受这些考验时,可能很难理解我们的审判。

但是,圣经总是向我们保证,我们的困难永远不是无目的的,而是以某种方式有目的的。 上帝总是利用他们来完成一些事情
author: Tim Challies

title_zh: 如果家庭游戏之夜能让您的孩子谈论圣经，会怎么样？
content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Doxa Games . This post is written by Marco Bartholomae, founder of Doxa Games and creator of the Bible-based board and card games Trials & Triumphs , Bible Clash , and Hurry! Fleeing Disciples . A couple of years ago, I was playing cards with my kids when a question hit me. What would it take to make a Bible game they’d ask to play again? I grew up in Germany with four brothers. We played cards on long car rides and spent hours on our bedroom floor with a board game spread out between us. I still remember how easy it was to lose track of time when we played together. Now I live in California with my wife and our four children, and we still love a good game night. The screens go away, somebody wants a rematch, and we get to enjoy being together. That question from the card table stayed with me. I started imagining games that could give other families that same experience and get them talking about Scripture along the way, games a child could sit down to, learn the rules, and enjoy right away, even if they were new to the Bible. Then maybe a name on a card or something that happened on the board would make them curious enough to ask a question. That’s how Doxa Games started. The Conversations That Start Around the Table In Deuteronomy 6, God tells his people to speak about his commandments with their children as they go about ordinary life, including when they sit at home. A game night gives us another chance to do that. Our games don’t replace family devotions, but they do open conversations about God’s Word. Your child might pick up a card and ask who Thaddaeus was. A race to a house church might get them wondering why the early Christians gathered in homes. Those are questions you can follow right back to Scripture. That’s also why I chose the name Doxa . It’s the Greek word for glory . In 1 Corinthians 10:31, Paul reminds us to do everything to the glory of God, even in ordinary things like eating and drinking. That conviction shapes what we make and how we think about time around the table. Three Games to Play With Your Family Bible Clash: Gospels (ages 8+) is a fast-paced, head-to-head card game. Play characters from the four Gospels and try to outscore your opponent. Trials & Triumphs (ages 5+) sends players down a winding path where one turn can move you forward, and the next can set you back. It gives younger kids a way to talk about trusting Christ through trials. Hurry! Fleeing Disciples (ages 8+) takes you into the world of Acts. Choose your route, evade Roman guards, and race to reach a house church. From Our Family Table to the Mission Field As Doxa grows, we hope to translate these games and put them in the hands of missionaries, church planters, and ministry training centers in places like Colombia, the Philippines, and East Africa. I’d love for a family in Malawi to pull out one of these games, play it in their own language, and have the same kinds of conversations we have around our table. If your family is getting together this Christmas, pick a game, clear a spot at the table, and let the kids make the first move. See all three games at DoxaGames.com . 교회언론회는 “문제는 다음 세대이다. 각 종교별 1-39세 종교인구는 기독교 289만 2,400명이고, 천주교가 91만 3,819명이며, 불교는 85만 1,349명이다. 그런데 기독교의 경우 10년 전보다 10-18% 이상 젊은 세대에서 빠져나갔다”며 “이제 다음 세대를 위해 한국교회가 ‘올인’할 때가 됐다”고 전했다.

이들은 “이것은 한 교회나 교단만의 문제가 아니라, 한국교회 전체가 참여하고 협력해 청년 세대의 고민과 갈등, 그들의 내면을 치유하고 삶의 의미에 답을 줄 수 있는 체계를 만들어 가야 한다”며 “앞으로 사회학, 인구통계학, 기술 발전 관점에서 탈종교화는 여전히 가속될 것이다. 그러나 영적 존재나 초월적 존재를 믿는 현상(Spirituality)에 대한 요구는 더해질 것”이라고 전망했다.

또 “미래 세대는 아무리 과학과 기술과 복지 제도가 발전한다 해도, 인간의 근본적이고 종교적 질문인 ‘Why(왜)’에 대한 영역은 오히려 또렷해질 것”이라며 “우리 기독교는 여기에 해답을 제시할 수 있어야 하고, 이를 철저하게 준비해야 한다”고 제언했다. 다음은 논평 전문.

2025년 인구주택총조사에서 종교인구 밝혀져 모든 종교에서 ‘탈종교화’가 뚜렷히 드러났다 한국교회는 다음 세대에게 영적 답을 주어야

정부가 지난해 ‘2025년 인구주택총조사’를 한 것이 밝혀졌다. 우리나라 전체 인구는 4,934만 9,707명인데, 그중에 종교를 가진 사람은 1,715만 6,360명이었고(34.8%) 종교가 없는 사람은 3,219만 3,347명이었다(65.2%) 종교가 있는 사람보다 종교가 없다는 사람이 약 2배 가까이 된다. 이는 인구조사를 할 때마다 종교 인구수가 줄어드는 현상이 뚜렷하다.

그 중에 주요 종교를 살펴보면, 기독교인은 843만 9,000명으로 종교인구 가운데 17.1%를 차지한다. 다음으로는 불교로 518만 4,000명으로 10.5%를 차지한다. 그리고 천주교는 330만 4,000명으로 6.7%를 차지한다. 그런데 세 종교 모두 숫자가 크게 줄어들었다.

기독교는 지난 10년간 123만 명이 줄어들었고, 불교는 243만 명이 줄어들었다. 천주교도 58만 명이 줄어든 것으로 나타났다(나머지 종교인구는 원불교 84,373명, 유교 24,655명, 천도교 19,132명, 대순진리회 34,446명, 대종교 1,792명, 기타 64,463명이다)

기독교가 강세 지역은 서울(20.5%) 인천(19.7%) 경기(19.6%) 강원(15.8%) 충남(17.7%) 충북(13.9%) 세종(18.0%) 대전(18.2%) 전북(22.8%) 광주(16.9%) 전남(19.5%) 지역이다. 반면에 불교세가 강한 지역은 경북(18.0%) 대구(16.6%) 울산(20.5%) 부산(20.6%) 경남(21.3%) 제주(14.5%) 지역이다.

문제는 다음 세대이다. 각 종교별 1-39세까지 종교인구는 기독교 2,892,400명이고, 천주교가 913,819명이며, 불교는 851,349명이다. 그런데 기독교의 경우, 10년 전보다 10~18% 이상이 젊은 세대에서 빠져나간 것으로 나타난다. 이제는 다음 세대를 위하여 한국교회가 ‘올인’할 때가 되었다.

이것은 한 교회나 한 교단만의 문제가 아니라, 한국교회 전체가 참여하고 협력하여 청년 세대의 고민과 갈등, 그들의 내면을 치유하고 삶의 의미에 답을 줄 수 있는 체계를 만들어 가야 한다. 앞으로 사회학, 인구통계학, 기술 발전의 관점에서 탈종교화는 여전히 가속될 것이다. 그러나 영적인 존재나 초월적 존재를 믿는 현상(Spirituality)에 대한 요구는 더해질 것으로 전망한다.

미래세대는 아무리 과학과 기술과 복지 제도가 발전한다고 하여도, 인간의 근본적이고 종교적 질문인 ‘Why’에 대한 영역은 오히려 또렷해질 것으로 예견된다. 여기에 우리 기독교는 해답을 제시할 수 있어야 하고, 이에 대하여 철저하게 준비해야 한다.
content_zh:
韩国教会媒体协会（会长沈河甫牧师）于11月27日就2025年人口普查结果的发布发表了评论。教会媒体协会表示：“问题在于下一代。在1-39岁的宗教人口中，基督教信徒为289.24万人，天主教信徒为91.3819万人，佛教信徒为85.1349万人。然而，就基督教而言，与10年前相比，年轻一代的信徒流失了10-18%以上。”他表示：“现在是韩国教会为下一代‘全力以赴’的时候了。” 他们表示：“这不是一个教会或一个教派的问题，而是整个韩国教会都应参与并合作，建立一个能够治愈年轻一代的烦恼与冲突、抚慰他们内心并为生命的意义提供答案的体系。”“未来，从社会学、人口统计学和技术发展的角度来看，去宗教化仍将加速。”

但他预测：“然而，对相信灵性存在或超然存在这种现象（灵性）的需求将会增加。” 他还建议道：“无论科学、技术和福利制度如何发展，对于未来世代来说，人类的根本性宗教问题‘为什么’的领域反而会变得更加清晰。”“我们基督教徒应该能够对此给出答案，并为此做好充分的准备。” 以下是评论全文。2025年人口普查显示，所有宗教的“去宗教化”趋势都非常明显。韩国教会必须为下一代提供精神层面的答案。

据透露，政府去年进行了“2025年人口和住房普查”。

我国总人口为49,349,707人，其中有宗教信仰的人数为17,156,360人（34.8%），无宗教信仰的人数为32,193,347人（65.2%）。无宗教信仰的人数几乎是信仰宗教的人数的两倍。这表明，每次进行人口普查时，有宗教信仰的人口数量都在明显减少。其中，就主要宗教而言，基督徒有843.9万人，占有宗教信仰人口的17.1%。其次是佛教，信众人数为518.4万人，占10.5%。天主教徒有330.4万人，占6.7%。然而，这三种宗教的人数都大幅减少。在过去十年中，基督教信徒减少了123万人，佛教信徒减少了243万人。

天主教徒人数也减少了58万人（其他宗教信徒人数分别为：圆佛教84,373人、儒教24,655人、天道教19,132人、大巡真理会34,446人、大宗教1,792人、其他64,463人）。

基督教信众较多的地区有：首尔（20.5%）、仁川（19.7%）、京畿（19.6%）、江原（15.8%）、忠南（17.7%）、忠北（13.9%）、世宗（18.0%）、大田（18.2%）、全北（22.8%）、光州（16.9%）、全南（19.5%）。另一方面，佛教势力较强的地区有庆尚北道（18.0%）、大邱（16.6%）、蔚山（20.5%）、釜山（20.6%）、庆尚南道（21.3%）和济州（14.5%）。问题在于下一代。

按宗教划分，1-39岁的宗教人口中，基督教为2,892,400人，天主教为913,819人，佛教为851,349人。然而，就基督教而言，与10年前相比，年轻一代中离开基督教的人数增加了10%至18%以上。现在是时候让韩国教会为下一代“全力以赴”了。这不是一个教会或一个教派的问题，而是整个韩国教会都应参与和合作，建立一个能够治愈年轻一代的烦恼和困惑、治愈他们的心灵并为生命的意义提供答案的体系。从社会学、人口统计学和技术发展的角度来看，未来去宗教化仍将加速。然而，预计对相信灵性存在或超然存在这种现象（灵性）的需求将会增加。

可以预见，无论科学、技术和福利制度如何发展，对于人类的根本性、宗教性问题“为什么”的关注，在未来世代反而会变得更加清晰。在这方面，我们基督徒应当能够提供答案，并为此做好充分的准备。

title_zh: [裴本哲专栏] 耶稣名号的能力
content:
복음이 거북스럽고 부담스럽게 느껴지는 분들이 있다. 현실적인 안주와 자기 중심적이며 세상적인 욕구에 매여 살아가는 이들에게는 복음이 그렇게 느껴질 것이다. 왜냐하면 신구약 성경 전체의 정신이나 예수 그리스도의 가르침과 명령 그 자체가 우리의 느슨하고 안일한 정신으로서는 도저히 이해되지도 않고 또 실천하기도 힘든 말씀이기 때문이다.

그래서 구약의 믿음의 백성들로부터 오늘의 깨어 있는 그리스도인에 이르기까지, 오직 철저한 헌신과 순종을 각오하며 주님을 따르는 자들만이 복음의 진리와 능력을 경험하게 되는 것이다. 어쩔 수 없다. 우리가 세상의 죄악과 자기중심적 삶을 택하든, 아니면 자신을 부정해 버리고 예수 중심적인 십자가의 삶을 택하든, 이것은 우리가 어떤 삶의 가치를 붙잡고 살아가느냐의 문제로서 양단간에 결국 우리의 진지한 선택을 요구한다.

기왕에 우리가 주님의 제자로서의 길을 따르기로 각오한 그리스도인이라면, 오늘날 우리에게는 오직 믿음의 길을 선택하며 살아갔던 수많은 믿음의 선배들의 발자취를 따를 수 있다. 그 중에서도 오늘 우리가 다룰 본문의 내용은 초대교회때 사도들이 어떠한 자세로 주님을 섬겼으며, 또 그러한 그들이 얼마나 복음을 자랑스럽게 전했는지에 대한 기가 막히게 멋진 또 하나의 장면을 보게 된다. 그 장면 속으로 들어가 보자.

오늘 사건의 배경은 초대교회 때 사도들이 복음을 전하다가 붙잡혀 있다가 기적적으로 하나님께서 보내신 천사를 통해 옥으로부터 풀려나온 후의 일이다. 그 소식을 듣고 대제사장의 무리들이 다시 사도들을 붙잡아 공회 앞에 끌고 나오게 된다. 그때 공회에서 대제사장으로부터 심문을 받는 과정에서 베드로와 사도들이 답변하는 장면이다.

행5:27 그들을 끌어다가 공회 앞에 세우니 대제사장이 물어

이 산헤드린 공의회(27)는 종교 문제뿐 아니라 유대 민족의 일반 통치권이나 재판권까지도 다 관장할 수 있었다. 이 공의회에는 대제사장뿐 아니라 이스라엘의 일반 통치권자들도 포함되어 있는 막강한 권력 기구였다. 따라서 이 공의회에서 정죄를 받는다는 것은 곧 일신상의 큰 위기가 초래된다는 것은 당연했다.

마침내 대제사장은 사도들에게 화가 나서 따지듯이 말한다; 5:28 이르되 우리가 이 이름으로 사람을 가르치지 말라고 엄금하였으되 너희가 너희 가르침을 예루살렘에 가득하게 하니 이 사람의 피를 우리에게로 돌리고자 함이로다

대제사장의 사도들에게 다구치는 내용은 다음과 같은 세 가지다; (1) 예수에 대해서는 두 번 다시 가르치지 말라고 엄하게 일러두지 않았냐? (2) 그런데 너희들은 온 예루살렘에 그의 가르침을 퍼뜨리고 있지 않나? (3) 게다가 예수를 죽인 책임까지 우리한테 있다고 뒤집어 씌우려 하고 있단 말이다.

그들은 예수를 죽인 책임에 대한 두려움에, 도둑이 제 발 저린 듯이 저렇게 말하면서 완강히 책임 회피를 하려 한다. 과연 그들은 바로 얼마 전에 빌라도가 ‘예수의 피를 우리와 우리 자손에게 돌려라’고 했던 말을 잊었던 것일까? (마 27:25)

‘이 이름으로’(28): 대제사장과 그 무리들은 그 이름 부르기를 꺼려했던 것을 본다. 이들은 계속해서 사도들에게 이 이름을 부르며 전하지 말라고 엄히 단속하고자 했다. 그러나 예수의 제자들은 예수의 이름으로 복음을 전하고 많은 기사와 이적을 행한 것과는 얼마나 대조적인가! 예수의 이름에 큰 능력이 있기에 사도들은 핍박 받고 매를 맞으면서도 예수의 이름을 부르며 복음을 전했고, 대제사장의 무리들은 예수의 이름에 무언가 저항할 수 없는 큰 힘이 있다고 보고 이를 두려워 하며 그 이름 부르는 것을 저지하려 했던 것이다.
content_zh:
有些人觉得福音令人尴尬和有负担。对于那些安于现状、以自我为中心、受世俗欲望束缚的人来说，福音会给他们这样的感觉。因为新旧约圣经的整体精神，以及耶稣基督的教导和诫命本身，对于我们松懈安逸的心灵来说，是根本无法理解，也很难付诸实践的话语。因此，从旧约中信心的子民到今天警醒的基督徒，只有那些做好彻底委身和顺服的准备、跟随主的人，才能经历福音的真理和能力。这是无可奈何的。

无论我们是选择世界的罪恶和以自我为中心的生活，还是否定自我，选择以耶稣为中心的十字架生活，这都是一个我们秉持何种人生价值观的问题，最终要求我们在两者之间做出严肃的选择。既然我们是已经下定决心要走上主门徒之路的基督徒，那么今天我们唯有追随那些选择走上信心之路并以此度过一生的大量信心前辈的足迹。其中，今天我们要学习的这段经文的内容，让我们看到另一个令人惊叹的精彩场景，那就是使徒们在初代教会时以怎样的态度侍奉主，以及他们是如何自豪地传扬福音的。让我们走进这一幕。

今天这段经文的背景是，在初代教会时期，使徒们在传福音时被抓，后来在神所差遣的天使的奇妙带领下从监狱中被释放出来之后发生的事情。听到这个消息后，大祭司的党羽再次将使徒们抓起来，带到公会面前。这是彼得和众使徒在公会中接受大祭司审问时回答的场景。使徒行传5:27 于是将他们带去，叫站在公会前。大祭司问他们说：

这个公会（27）不仅可以处理宗教事务，还可以掌管犹太民族的一般统治权和司法权。这个公会是一个强大的权力机构，不仅包括大祭司，还包括以色列的一般统治者。因此，在这个公会中被定罪，自然意味着个人将面临巨大的危机。

大祭司终于对使徒们发怒，像质问般地说道；5:28说：“我们曾严严地嘱咐你们，不可奉这名教训人；你们倒把你们的教训充满耶路撒冷，想要叫这人的血归到我们身上！”

大祭司对使徒的斥责有以下三点：（1）难道我没有严厉地告诫你们不要再传讲耶稣了吗？(2) 但是你们不是正在整个耶路撒冷传播他的教导吗？（3）而且你们还想把杀害耶稣的责任推到我们身上。他们出于对杀害耶稣的责任的恐惧，像贼心虚一样那样说话，试图顽固地推卸责任。

难道他们真的忘记了不久前彼拉多说的话吗？他说：“叫他的血归到我们和我们的子孙身上。”（太27:25）

“奉这名”（28）：我们看到大祭司和他的党羽不愿意称呼这个名。他们不断严厉地告诫使徒们不要呼喊这个名，也不要传扬这个名。但是，这与耶稣的门徒奉耶稣的名传福音并行许多神迹奇事形成了多么鲜明的对比！因为耶稣的名里有极大的能力，所以使徒们即使受到迫害和鞭打，也呼喊耶稣的名并传扬福音；而大祭司的党羽们则认为耶稣的名里有一种不可抗拒的巨大力量，他们害怕这种力量，并试图阻止人们呼喊这个名。

title_zh: 沙佩科恩斯，这些因信仰而团结在一起的足球运动员，直至死亡。
content: Le 28 novembre 2016, l’avion embarquant l’équipe de football de première ligue brésilienne Chapecoense, volant vers la Colombie pour la finale de Copa Sudamericana (équivalent de la Ligue Europa, ndlr) s’écrasait dans les montagnes, tuant 71 des 77 passagers, dont 19 joueurs, l’entraîneur, 23 membres du staff dont le président, 21 journalistes et invités. Ce crash et le sauvetage vécu en direct a bouleversé, bien au-delà du club, l’ensemble du monde du football. Les reportages, dont les portraits des joueurs par chaque veuve publiés dans Marca, reflètent une équipe pleine de joie et camaraderie, à l’ambiance remarquablement familiale, mais aussi portée par une piété exceptionnelle même dans un contexte latino-américain, loin des scandales ou d’une frivolité de jeunesse. Tous ces footballeurs, sans exception, s’inscrivaient dans une foi chrétienne, catholique ou évangélique – dans laquelle leurs proches puisent encore le soutien. Comme s’ils étaient sans le savoir déjà prêts pour le Ciel. Dix ans après la tragédie, leur héritage reste puissant, Tout lire… The post Chapecoense, ces footballeurs unis par la foi jusque dans la mort appeared first on Aleteia .
content_zh:
2016年11月28日，载有巴西甲级联赛球队沙佩科恩斯全队的飞机在飞往哥伦比亚参加南美杯（相当于欧罗巴联赛）决赛的途中坠毁于山区，机上77人中有71人遇难，其中包括19名球员、教练、23名工作人员（包括俱乐部主席）、21名记者和嘉宾。

这场坠机事故和现场直播的救援行动不仅震撼了俱乐部，也震撼了整个足球界。

《马卡报》刊登的报道，包括每位寡妇对球员的描述，展现了一支充满欢乐和友谊的球队，氛围格外温馨，甚至在拉丁美洲的背景下也显得格外虔诚，远离丑闻或年轻人的轻浮。

所有这些足球运动员无一例外地信仰基督教、天主教或福音派教义，他们的亲属至今仍从中汲取力量。仿佛他们不知不觉中已经为升入天堂做好了准备。悲剧发生十年后，他们的精神遗产依然强大。阅读全文……这篇文章《沙佩科恩斯：这些足球运动员因信仰而团结，直至死亡》最初发表于 Aleteia。

content: Star de Broadway puis figure incontournable du cinéma hollywoodien, Rosalind Russell, dont ce 28 novembre marque les cinquante ans de sa disparition, avait tout d’une grande dame du septième art. Mais derrière ses rôles de femmes indépendantes et pleines d’esprit se cachait aussi une catholique fervente, dont la foi a marqué la vie personnelle et les relations. Née le 4 juin 1907 à Waterbury, dans le Connecticut, Rosalind Russell rêvait déjà de devenir actrice lorsqu’elle était enfant. Mais il lui fallut du temps avant d’oser avouer sa véritable vocation à ses parents catholiques irlandais qui estimaient que le métier d’actrice n’avait pas bonne réputation. À l’époque, le monde du spectacle était volontiers associé à une vie dissolue, à l’alcool et aux excès. Ses parents, soucieux de son avenir, ne voyaient donc pas d’un bon œil cette carrière. D’autant plus que son éducation a été marquée par la présence et l’enseignement des religieuses dans les établissements scolaires qu’elle fréquentait comme la Tout lire… The post Rosalind Russell, cette star d’Hollywood qui a conduit des âmes vers Dieu appeared first on Aleteia .
content_zh:
罗莎琳德·拉塞尔（Rosalind Russell）是百老汇明星，后来成为好莱坞电影的标志性人物。11月28日是她逝世五十周年纪念日。她具备一位银幕巨星的一切特质。然而，在她所饰演的独立而机智的女性角色背后，隐藏着一位虔诚的天主教徒，她的信仰深刻影响了她的个人生活和人际关系。

罗莎琳德·拉塞尔于1907年6月4日出生于康涅狄格州沃特伯里，从小就梦想成为一名演员。但她花了很长时间才敢向她的爱尔兰天主教父母坦白自己的真正志向，因为他们认为女演员的职业名声不佳。

当时，娱乐圈往往与放荡的生活、酗酒和放纵行为联系在一起。她的父母担心她的未来，因此对她的演艺事业持反对态度。

尤其是在她就读的学校中，修女们的陪伴和教导对她的教育产生了深远影响。阅读全文……这篇文章《罗莎琳德·拉塞尔：引领灵魂归向天主的这位好莱坞明星》最初发表于Aleteia。

title_zh: 利奥十四世踏上追寻“神奇奖章”的旅程
content: La basilique Sant’Andrea delle Fratte doit accueillir ce vendredi 27 novembre un hôte de marque à l’occasion de la fête de la médaille miraculeuse. Léon XIV doit se rendre dans cette basilique du centre historique de Rome pour la première fois de son pontificat. L’histoire de cet édifice qui abrite le sanctuaire de la Madonna del Miracolo est étroitement liée à celle de la chapelle de la médaille miraculeuse, située rue du Bac, à Paris. En 1830, au cœur de la capitale française, la Vierge apparaît à trois reprises à une jeune religieuse des Filles de la charité de Saint-Vincent-de-Paul, Catherine Labouré. Lors de ces rencontres, la mère de Jésus demande à la jeune femme de frapper et diffuser une médaille en son honneur. La médaille miraculeuse naît alors et est rapidement diffusée à des centaines de milliers d’exemplaires à travers le monde. Douze ans après ces apparitions, un Alsacien d’origine juive, profondément athée, arrive à Rome : Alphonse Ratisbonne. Tout lire… The post Léon XIV part sur les traces de la médaille miraculeuse appeared first on Aleteia .
content_zh:
值此奇迹奖章节之际，圣安德肋·德莱·弗拉特圣殿（Basilique Sant’Andrea delle Fratte）将于11月27日（周五）迎来一位尊贵的客人。这是利奥十四世在就任教宗后首次前往这座位于罗马历史中心的圣殿。

这座建筑内设有奇迹圣母圣殿，其历史与位于巴黎巴克街（rue du Bac）的奇迹奖章小堂的历史密切相关。1830 年，在法国首都的中心地带，圣母三次向圣文生·德·保禄慈善修女会的年轻修女加大利辣·拉布勒（Catherine Labouré）显现。

在这些显现中，耶稣的母亲要求这位年轻女子铸造并传播一枚以她为尊的圣牌。于是，奇迹奖牌就此诞生，并迅速在全球范围内传播，发行量达到数十万枚。在这些显现发生十二年后，一位犹太裔的阿尔萨斯人抵达罗马，他名叫阿方斯·拉蒂斯邦（Alphonse Ratisbonne），是一位坚定的无神论者。

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位前流行明星兼模特谈到了她对耶稣的爱，尽管她从小就被带去犹太会堂。前Pussycat Dolls成员卡雅·琼斯（Kaya Jones）的父母都是犹太人，她说：“我想去犹太会堂，我也想有耶稣！” 即使在孩提时代（成长过程中……）这篇文章《前Pussycat Dolls成员是犹太人，但热爱耶稣》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 前Pussycat Dolls成员是犹太人，热爱耶稣
content: By Charles Gardner — A former pop star and model has spoken of her love for Jesus despite being brought up to attend synagogue. One-time Pussycat Dolls member Kaya Jones, whose parents are both Jewish, said: “I wanted to be in the synagogue, and I wanted to have Jesus!” Even as a kid (growing up in America), she felt the two sides – church and synagogue – were part of the same family and needed to be reconciled, quoting the words of Jesus, “I and my Father are one.” (John 10:30) In an interview with Stephen Briggs for his Israel Matters podcast, she said: “I read my Bible and knew that Jesus was my Mashiach (Messiah).” After getting baptised and committing her life to Jesus, she studied at a Hebraic Bible College (which included the New Testament) and has since travelled to Israel to show her support for the beleaguered nation. (photo: KayaJones.com) “The media narrative of Israel is really horrible,” she said. “It’s truly wicked that Israel is having to defend its right to exist.” Referring to the Hamas terrorists as “a death cult”, she echoes the words of her Saviour by saying: “The enemy has come to steal, kill and destroy. But God came to give us life.” (see John 10:10) As for the land, if it is not protected from ongoing threats to wipe out God’s ancient people, will Jesus return there? “God is sending Yeshua (Jesus) back to the exact place [where he ministered on earth],” she said (see Acts 1:11, Zechariah 14:4). “If there is such no place, his arrival will be delayed.” Urging Christians to visit Israel because it turns Bible locations from black and white into technicolour, she said: “It’s not just a storybook or fairytale.” She added that the biggest misconception about Israel is that they are committing genocide, suggesting that this was emphatically not the case. “But there is a war. And if we are going to live in peace, we must listen to what God says in the Torah (the Bible’s section on Law).” The post Former Pussycat Dolls member is Jewish, loves Jesus first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
由查尔斯·加德纳(Charles Gardner)——一位前流行明星和模特儿,尽管被抚养到参加犹太会堂,但还是谈到她对耶稣的热爱.

有一次,猫猫娃娃成员Kaya Jones的父母都是犹太人,他说:“我想在犹太会堂里,我想有耶稣!” 即便小时候(在美国长大),她还是觉得双方——教会和犹太会堂——是同一个家庭的一部分,需要和解,引用耶稣的话,“我和我父亲是一体的 ” (John 10:30) 史蒂芬・布里格斯的采访中

她说:「我读了我的圣经, 在接受洗礼,并将生命献给耶稣之后,她就读于一所希伯来圣经学院(包括新约),此后前往以色列,表明她支持被困民族. (图片:KayaJones.com). 她说,“媒体对以色列的描述确实可怕。”

“以色列必须捍卫其生存权,这真是邪恶的。 她把哈马斯恐怖分子称为“死亡邪教”,她重复了救世主的话:“敌人是来偷盗、杀人和破坏的。 但上帝来给我们生命。” 至于土地,如果不保护它不受不断的威胁,消灭上帝的古老人民,耶稣会返回那里吗?

她说,“真主要将耶和华派回他所管理的地方。”

“如果没有这种地方,他的到来将推迟。” 她敦促基督徒访问以色列,因为它把圣经地点从黑白变成技术品味。 她说 : “ 这不仅仅是一本故事书或童话。 ” 她补充说,对以色列最大的误解是他们正在犯下种族灭绝罪行,这表明情况显然并非如此。 “但战争仍然存在。

如果我们要和平地生活,我们就必须听取上帝在《图拉》中所说的话。 前猫猫娃娃成员是犹太人,

title_zh: 年度图书：《金色的西奥》（Theo of Golden）
content: By John Pearson — Oh, my. No words, really. JUST READ IT! You must read this extraordinary book, Theo of Golden, a Novel by Allen Levi. This is not a review. No spoiler alerts. Just my obnoxious pleading and begging: you must read this extraordinary book. I know. It’s still November—and I’m announcing my 2026 Book-of-the-Year. (My apologies to the authors of the other 44 books I’ve reviewed so far in 2026, but you’d have to agree with me.) This first-time author, Allen Levi, self-published Theo of Golden in 2023. Word-of-mouth created a publishing sensation and, eventually, a division of Simon & Schuster picked it up. It’s now a New York Times bestseller with more than four million copies sold! If you promise to order the book and read it—you can stop reading my “non-review” right here and move on with your day. If you still need my cajoling…read on. Five notes: #1.  A Gazillion Recommendations Ignored! My apologies to my sister-in-law, Polly Pearson, and dozen of other friends who urged me to read this book. My wife, Joanne, ordered the book last year and she urged (insisted/commanded) that I put aside “all those management books” and read something for fun once in a while. (Finally…mission accomplished. I’m grateful .) #2. Superb Writing. A friend, who is also an author, told me this week he was only eight chapters into the book (60 short chapters, 400 pages)—and he’s given up writing forever! Allen Levi’s wordcrafting…simply superb. #3. I Cheated! Because I borrowed Joanne’s book, with strict instructions not to underline or highlight anything, or make notes in the book, or circle ingenious word combinations ( you know—all the things thoughtful readers do ), I thought, “OK. I’ll just enjoy reading this. I won’t make notes. I won’t read it. I won’t review it.” Oops! I cheated. I couldn’t resist. I made 53 notes on my iPad. I could have made hundreds. I’m not alone. As of this week, Theo of Golden has over 214,000 reviews on Amazon and almost 750,000 ratings on Goodreads. ( It’s #2 on Amazon this week .) #4. He Got Teary-eyed! A pastor texted me—just one-third of the way through the audiobook: “Incredible! Some of the most beautiful writing I’ve ever heard.” While listening on his walk, he got “choked up.” ( Ditto .) #5. Audio, Kindle, or Book? I’m a book guy, but another friend said he was encouraged to listen to the book, while also reading along. I might try that. ( Listen to a three-minute sample here .) The audiobook runs 13 hours and 12 minutes. ( You’ll wish it were longer. Honest .) Allen Levi (YouTube) “Pearson—what’s the book about? I don’t get it. Why won’t you tell me about it?” OK, OK. Here’s the Amazon blurb: “One spring morning, a stranger named Theo arrives in the small Southern city of Golden. He doesn’t explain much about where he came from or why he’s there—but when he visits the local coffeehouse, where pencil portraits of the people of Golden hang on the walls, he begins purchasing them, one at a time, and giving each portrait to the person depicted. In exchange, he asks only for the person’s story. And so portrait by portrait, person by person, secrets are revealed, regrets are shared, and ordinary lives are profoundly altered.” From the back cover: “A story of giving and receiving, of seeing and being seen, Theo of Golden is a beautifully crafted novel about the power of creative generosity, the importance of wonder to a purposeful life, and the invisible threads of kindness that bind us to one another.” “Allen Levi—attorney, judge, singer/songwriter, author—lives on and cares for family acreage near a small town in middle Georgia.” This is his first novel. He’s 70. Here’s the link to the author’s summary on YouTube: Did I mention? Extraordinary. Book-of-the-Year. Grabs you by the heart. Can’t stop talking about it. You’ll want to quiet your Thanksgiving crowd and read them a short chapter. Also: your Christmas shopping is done. Order 20 copies today! (You’re welcome.) TO ORDER FROM AMAZON, click on the

title_zh: 父母的分居和姐姐的去世使他远离了上帝，而“认识基督教”课程为他带来了改变
content: By Charles Gardner — Andy Gibson (photo: Gardner) Getting through life with all its many challenges was particularly tough for Andy Gibson as he was growing up. This was especially the case when his parents separated, and his sister was killed in a car crash. He even prayed and asked God why these things were happening, but heard no answers – until much more recently, when a growing relationship with Jesus transformed his life. Now 33, the Doncaster-based railway operations planner has his journey firmly back on track. Having attended a Church of England primary school and subsequently made only occasional visits to church, following Jesus is now the focus of his days. Looking back, he recalls: “I was lost and, moving into my teens, was full of anger, ego and arrogance. I got heavily involved with underage drinking around town and yet, strangely, I’d always pray before going out. “Time moved on and I found myself coasting through life in my twenties – meeting Beth, now my wife, working, saving for a house and having our first child Arlo. “Then in 2019, as the Covid pandemic approached, I was listening to odd things relating to Christianity on YouTube, as a result of which I went to a local church and completed an Alpha course (an introduction to the Christian faith). “In all honesty, it didn’t really interest me. But I gave it a bit of time, feeling that I still wanted to know about Jesus, God and the Bible as a whole. So I went on Google and found BEC (Bessacarr Evangelical Church) which was not far from where we lived. “I remember saying to Beth, ‘I’m going to go there!’ So I went one Sunday evening and was just blown away. The preaching was different to anything I had experienced, and I was finally understanding the Bible. “I couldn’t wait for the following Sunday to find out more. It was like waiting for another episode of a Netflix documentary to come out because we’d be following a specific section of the Bible, studying each chapter in depth as part of a series over several weeks. So I’d be looking forward to an explanation of the next verses the following week. And in due course I publicly declared my faith in Jesus by getting baptised. “Until I started going to church, learning more about the Bible and developing a relationship with Jesus, I never felt fulfilment and love. I never felt I fitted in anywhere until I found Jesus. “I didn’t have answers in my youth. But now I realise it’s not something you can work out all on your own. I can just turn to God’s Word and, through prayer, have a relationship with Jesus. “I can honestly say it’s completely changed every aspect of my life, and I am so grateful that I can’t even put it into words.” Andy and Beth now have a second child, named Red, and are members at BEC, a growing church in a Doncaster suburb. If you want to know more about a personal relationship with God, go here The post Parents’ separation and sisters death turned him from God, Alpha course brought change first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
由查尔斯·加德纳(英语:Charles Gardner)——安迪·吉布森(英语:Andy Gibson)(摄影:Gardner)执导. 在安迪·吉布森长大的时候 面对众多挑战 生活特别艰难 父母分居,妹妹在车祸中丧生时尤其如此.

他甚至祈祷并问上帝为什么发生这些事情,但是没有听到答案——直到最近,与耶稣的日益密切的关系改变了他的生活. 现在33号 以唐卡斯特为基地的铁路运营规划师 他的旅程已牢牢地回到轨道上

曾就读于一所英格兰教会小学,后来只偶尔访问教堂,跟随耶稣成为他时代的焦点. 回顾过去,他回顾道:“我迷失了,进入十几岁时,充满了愤怒、自我和傲慢。 但奇怪的是,我总是在外出前祈祷。

“时光在流逝,我发现自己在20多岁时踏上了生命的旅程,结识了现在的妻子贝丝(Beth),在工作、为房子储蓄和生下第一个孩子阿罗。 “随后,在2019年,随着科维德大流行的临近,我在YouTube上听到一些与基督教有关的怪事,结果我去了当地的教堂,完成了阿尔法课程(基督教信仰介绍).

“老实说, 但我给了它一点时间,感觉我仍然想知道耶稣,上帝和整个圣经. 于是我继续谷歌,找到了BEC(Bessacarr福音教会),它离我们住的地方不远. " 我记得对贝丝说:‘我要去那里! 所以我去了一个星期天晚上 被吹走。

传教与我经历过的一切不同,我终于明白圣经. 我迫不及待地等待下一个星期日再了解更多情况。 这就像等待Netflix纪录片的另一集出来, 因为我们将遵循圣经的特定部分,

因此,我期待着下周对下一首诗进行解释。 在适当的时候,我通过接受洗礼公开宣布我对耶稣的信仰. “直到我开始去教堂,更多地了解圣经,发展与耶稣的关系,我从未感到满足和爱。 在找到耶稣之前,我从未感觉到自己身处任何地方 我年轻时没有答案。

但现在我意识到这不是你能自己解决的事情。 我可以转而引用上帝的话,并通过祈祷与耶稣建立关系。 “我可以坦率地说,这完全改变了我生活的方方面面,我非常感激,我甚至不能用言语表达。 安迪和贝丝现在有一个第二个孩子,名叫瑞德(Red),是BEC的成员,BEC是顿卡斯特郊区正在成长的教堂.

Nixon has another creative life—one that spans more than three decades of songwriting, recording, and musical exploration. Nixon is perhaps best known for his academic work at Veritas International University, his books, and his journalism for God Reports, ASSIST News Service, and other media […]  The post  From Post-Punk to German Techno—A Musical Journey  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh:
由马克·埃利斯(Mark Ellis)出名于他的奖学金,新闻,和声,布莱恩·C·尼克松(Brian C.

尼克松在维里塔斯国际大学的学术工作,他的著作,以及他为"上帝报道","ASSIST新闻服务"(ASSIST News Service),以及其他媒体[.]而出名的也许是他. 从后朋克到德意志科技-音乐之旅的文章首次出现在"上帝报告"上.
title_zh: 从后朋克到德国 техно——一段音乐之旅
content: By Mark Ellis — Known for his scholarship, journalism, and voice, Brian C. Nixon has another creative life—one that spans more than three decades of songwriting, recording, and musical exploration. Brian Nixon Nixon is perhaps best known for his academic work at Veritas International University , his books, and his journalism for God Reports , ASSIST News Service , and other media outlets. His voice has also reached listeners across the country through his former involvement with the radio program To Every Man an Answer (later known as Pastors’ Perspective ) and, more recently, Paratus , a program devoted to developing a biblical worldview. What may surprise those familiar with Nixon’s academic and journalistic work is that he is also an accomplished musician and songwriter whose musical journey spans more than 30 years. In his forthcoming book, A Beautiful Defense: How Aesthetics Points to God , co-written with Dr. Patrick Zukeran and scheduled for release in 2027 , Nixon explores the relationship between beauty, faith, and the creative process. In anticipation of the book’s release, I spoke with Nixon about his musical beginnings, his creative influences, and his unexpected venture into German electronic music. Tell me about your early musical journey. I grew up in a musical family. Music was part of my everyday life. During high school, I formed a band with some friends that eventually signed with an independent record label in the San Francisco Bay Area. We released only one record, but several of the other members went on to successful careers in the music industry. One became involved in founding Stones Throw Records, an influential independent label known for its underground hip-hop and experimental music. It was an exciting time. We were young, creative, and discovering what music could be. What did you do after the band broke up? I continued my college education, eventually transferring to California State University, Stanislaus. There, I met another group of musicians, and we formed a band called Canterbury. We ended up winning a Bay Area battle-of-the-bands competition, which was exciting. But rather than continuing in that direction, we decided to pursue something with a more intentional ministry focus. That led to the formation of Widow’s Mite . Widow’s Mite eventually signed with Rick Wakeman, the legendary keyboardist of Yes. Interestingly, that connection also introduced me to journalist Dan Wooding, who wrote Wakeman’s first biography. That relationship eventually opened the door for me to write for ASSIST News Service . So, in a rather unexpected way, my musical career helped launch my journalism career. Widow’s Mite After college, did you continue writing music? Absolutely. I still write music today. My compositions range from jazz and pop to what I call tone poems —short instrumental works that emphasize mood, atmosphere, and musical expression. Some are experimental, while others are much more accessible. I’ve always enjoyed exploring different musical forms rather than staying within a single genre. Interestingly, some of my recent compositions have been selected for rotation by a German online radio station. And here’s the surprising part: they’re German electronic and techno-influenced songs. I’ve been experimenting with AI-assisted production, including using a synthesized female vocalist to interpret my compositions. Did you say German techno? (Laughs.) I know. It sounds funny, doesn’t it? But there’s a story behind it. Recently, I took a deep dive into the music of Kraftwerk, the pioneering German electronic band. I was familiar with their work during high school in the early 1980s because they had influenced so many of the post-punk bands I was listening to at the time. I decided to revisit their entire catalog, and I was blown away all over again. They were years ahead of their time. Their approach to rhythm, synthesizers, repetition, and technology helped shape entire genres of contemporary music.
content_zh:
由马克·埃利斯(Mark Ellis)——以他的奖学金,新闻学,和声著称,布莱恩·C·尼克松(Brian C. Brian Nixon Nixon或许以他在Veritas国际大学的学术工作、他的书籍、他为《上帝报告》所做的新闻工作、ASSIST新闻服务以及其他媒体而闻名。

他的声音也通过他以前参与的电台节目“每个男人一个答案”(后来被称为“牧师的观点”)以及最近参与的Paratus,

可能令那些熟悉尼克松的学术和新闻工作的人惊讶的是,他还是一位成就卓著的音乐家和作曲家,他的音乐旅程长达30多年. 在他的即将出版的书《美丽的防御:美学如何指向上帝》中,

Patrick Zukeran)并计划于2027年发行,尼克松探讨了美,信仰,以及创作过程之间的关系. 为了期待这本书的发行,我和尼克松谈到了他的音乐开始,他的创作影响,以及他对德国电子音乐的意外冒险. 跟我说说你早期的音乐旅程 我成长在一个音乐家庭。

音乐是我日常生活的一部分。 在高中期间,我与一些朋友组成了一个乐队,最终在旧金山湾区与一个独立的唱片标签签约. 我们只发行了一张唱片,但其他几位成员继续进入音乐行业的成功职业生涯.

1开始参与创办Stones Throw Records,这个有影响力的独立标签以其地下嘻哈和实验音乐而闻名. 这是一个令人兴奋的时代。 我们年轻 富有创造力 并发现了什么是音乐。 乐队解散后你做了什么? 我继续我的大学教育, 最终转到加州州立大学斯坦尼斯劳斯。

在那里,我遇到了另一组音乐家,我们组成了一个乐队,叫坎特伯雷. 我们最终赢得了湾区战役的冠军 令人兴奋 但是,我们不是继续朝这个方向前进,而是决定以更有意的部级重点来追求某些目标。 这导致了寡妇之谜的形成。

寡妇的Mite最终与传说中的Yes键盘手Rick Wakeman签约. 有趣的是,这种联系也让我认识了记者丹·伍德(Dan Wooding),他写了Wakeman的第一份传记。 这段关系最终为我打开了为ASSIST新闻服务撰稿的大门. 因此,以相当出乎意料的方式,我的音乐生涯帮助启动了我的新闻事业.

你继续写音乐吗? 当然 我今天还写音乐 我的构思从爵士乐和流行到我所谓的调子诗——强调情绪、气氛和音乐表现的短器作品。 有些是实验性的,而另一些则更容易获得。

我总是喜欢探索不同的音乐形式, 有趣的是,我最近的一些构件已经被一个德国在线电台选为轮换. 这是令人惊讶的部分:它们是德国的电子和科技影响歌曲。

包括使用合成女性配音师来解释我的配音。 你说德国科技吗? (笑声) 我知道,我记得 这听起来很有趣, 但背后有一个故事。 最近,我深入了德国电子乐队Kraftwerk的音乐。

1980年代初高中期间我熟悉他们的工作,因为他们影响了我当时听的很多后朋克乐队. 我决定重新审视他们的全部目录,我再次被吹走. 他们比以前早好几年 他们对节奏,合成器,重复,技术的方法帮助塑造了整个当代音乐流派.
