summary_zh: 作者：查尔斯·加德纳 (Charles Gardner) — 我的妻子琳达 (Linda) 并不了解 20 世纪 70 年代和 80 年代她的雇主的犹太背景。她只知道自己喜欢为他们工作，只是为了听从上帝的呼召，与孩子们一起工作。因此，我们前往伦敦参加鲑鱼展览，并且 [...] 发现犹太根源，回应反犹太主义的帖子首次出现在《上帝报告》上。
title_zh: 探索犹太血统，应对反犹太主义
content: By Charles Gardner — Charles and Linda on their wedding day My wife Linda had no idea of the Jewish background of her employers during the 1970s and 80s. She just knew that she loved working for them and only left to follow God’s call to work with children. So we travelled down to London for an exhibition of the Salmon and Gluckstein dynasty, and the story of how these resilient Jewish families fled violent persecution in Eastern Europe to build what became the largest catering company in the world known as J Lyons & Co. Linda worked there as a home economist from 1977-1984 but it was only much later that she learnt of the Jewish nature of the firm that once literally fed Britain with its teashops and corner houses on every high street, and its products in every home, Linda playing her part through her cooking and marketing skills. A few years later, after graduating from Bible College in Bournemouth, she worked at a prayer and reconciliation centre in Northern Ireland where she was introduced to the importance of the Christian faith’s Jewish roots, as a result of which she took a study tour of Israel to learn more. And on a second trip to the Holy Land ten years later, she got more than she bargained for. At Cana in Galilee, where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding, Linda was given a vision of her own wedding. And we met on a blind date six months later! Though having Jewish ancestry myself, I grew up knowing nothing about it. But I learnt more later, especially after becoming a Christian in my early twenties, as Linda had done. It helped that I had a Jewish believer as my early mentor, and I became increasingly aware of the significance of our Jewish heritage, about which I now write prolifically. Meanwhile Linda, who has been teaching Christianity in Doncaster area schools for over 30 years, also now teaches about Judaism as it forms the context into which Christ came to us, fulfilling all the laws and promises of the Old Testament. So in both our cases, we were kept in the dark about very important aspects of our lives – until the Lord shone his light on the truth. Which brings me to the Christian Church as a whole, especially in the UK. We have known very little, if anything, of our faith’s Jewish roots or of God’s ongoing purposes for Israel. This needs to change – and fast! For we are surely hurtling towards the Messiah’s Second Coming like a high-speed train, in danger of coming off the rails with the rest of humanity if we fail to get to grips with how we Christians fit into the unfolding picture of global opposition to tiny Israel. What is our role as we watch antisemitism spread across the globe like wildfire? Do we just sit and watch, or write it off as having nothing to do with us, and remain silent? Or do we stand up to be counted as those who refuse to salute the new Nazism that portrays itself as anti-Zionism – a Confessing Church walking the way of the cross for God’s chosen people? My questions come as renewed calls are made for an independent inquiry into antisemitism at the BBC following news that Oscar-winning producer Lucie Kon has won £400,000 in compensation from the broadcaster. Lucie’s career is said to have unravelled after she raised concerns about antisemitism within the BBC, though the latter have not admitted to any fault. This is highly significant as millions of UK Christians are (where Israel is concerned) probably more influenced by what they hear from our national broadcaster than what they read in the Bible. 由查尔斯·加德纳(Charles Gardner)——查尔斯和琳达在他们的婚礼当天 我的妻子琳达对1970年代和80年代雇主的犹太背景一无所知. 她只知道她喜欢为他们工作,只好听从上帝的号召,与孩子们一起工作。

于是我们来到伦敦,为沙门王朝和格勒克斯泰因王朝举办展览, 讲述了这些坚韧的犹太家庭是如何逃离东欧的暴力迫害, 来建造一个被称为J Lyons & Co的世界最大的餐饮公司的故事。

琳达从1977年到1984年作为家庭经济学家在那里工作,但直到很晚,她才得知这家公司的犹太性质,曾经真正地向英国提供每条高街上的茶店和角楼,以及每家每户家中的产品,琳达通过她的烹饪和营销技巧扮演了她的角色.

几年后,她从伯恩茅斯的圣经学院毕业后,在北爱尔兰的一个祈祷与和解中心工作,在那里向她介绍了基督教信仰犹太教根源的重要性,因此她前往以色列学习更多知识. 在十年后的第二次圣地之行中,她得到了比她讨价还价的更多.

在加利利的卡纳,耶稣在婚礼上把水变成了葡萄酒,琳达得到了自己婚礼的愿景. 我们六个月后相识了! 虽然自己有犹太血统,但长大后却一无所知. 但我后来学到更多, 特别是在我20多岁时成为基督徒之后, 就像琳达所做的那样。

这有助于我有一个犹太教信徒作为我的早期导师,我越来越意识到我们的犹太遗产的重要性,我现在以正文写道。

与此同时,琳达在顿卡斯特地区学校教授基督教30多年,现在还教授犹太教,因为它构成了基督来到我们面前的背景,履行了《旧约》的所有法律和承诺。 因此,在我们这两种情况中,我们被蒙在鼓里,谈论着我们生活中非常重要的方面,直到上帝照亮真理。

这让我来到整个基督教会 特别是在英国 我们几乎不知道我们的信仰的犹太根源,或上帝对以色列的持续目的。 这需要改变,

因为如果我们不能把握基督徒如何融入全球反对小以色列的景象, 我们肯定会像高速列车一样, 与人类其他部分一同下火车。 当我们看到像野火一样在全球蔓延的反分裂主义时,我们的作用是什么?

我们只是坐视不理,还是把它写成与我们无关,保持沉默? 或者我们被算作拒绝向将自己描绘成反犹太复国主义的新纳粹主义致敬的人,

我的问题是,在奥斯卡获奖制片人Lucie Kon从广播公司获得40万英镑的赔偿后,英国广播公司再次呼吁独立调查反犹太主义。 Lucie的职业生涯据说在BBC内提出反分裂主义的担忧后破裂,

由于数百万英国基督徒(就以色列而言)受到我们国家广播机构广播的影响,

而今天的查尔斯和琳达(Charles and Linda),上帝的言语告诉我们“安抚”他的古老人民(以赛亚40:1), 有关以色列正在发生的事情的报道经常被传到造成整个国家遭受创伤的恐怖分子身上,

使徒保罗写道,福音应当被宣布为“首先对犹太人,然后对异教徒”。 (罗姆人1:16) 是的,我们必须分享T

summary: By Howard Cooper — Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, says he plans to take his oath of office on a Quran when the new Congress convenes in January. El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers on November 3, becoming the first Muslim American elected to the […]  The post  New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh: 霍华德·库珀 (Howard Cooper) 撰文：密歇根州民主党人阿卜杜勒·赛义德 (Abdul El-Sayed) 成为第一位当选美国参议院的穆斯林，他表示，他计划在一月份新一届国会召开时，在《古兰经》的基础上宣誓就职。 42 岁的埃尔-赛义德于 11 月 3 日击败了共和党人迈克·罗杰斯，成为第一位当选为 […] 的穆斯林美国人。来自密歇根州的新参议员表示，他将在《古兰经》中宣誓。
title_zh: 密歇根州新任参议员表示他将以古兰经宣誓就职
content: By Howard Cooper — Abdul Al-Sayed (wikipedia commons) Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, says he plans to take his oath of office on a Quran when the new Congress convenes in January. El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers on November 3, becoming the first Muslim American elected to the Senate and the first epidemiologist to serve in the chamber, according to WION News. In an interview with NPR’s Leila Fadel, he said, “I will likely swear on a Quran. Which Quran, we’re not sure.” He pointed to a copy once owned by Thomas Jefferson, which Keith Ellison used when he was sworn in to Congress, and to an old Quran at the University of Michigan that he described as the first in the state. The US Constitution does not require a Bible or any religious text. In practice, senators usually take the formal oath together on the Senate floor, and a Bible comes into play in individual ceremonial swearings-in. El-Sayed hasn’t said whether he’ll use the Quran in the formal proceedings, the ceremony, or both, and that his choice would not alter the wording of the oath. He has also stressed that his oath will be to the U.S. Constitution,  according to IBTimes. He will be sworn in by Vice President JD Vance, a fact El-Sayed has noted with humor. The Blaze reported he called it a “delicious irony” that Vance is constitutionally required to do so. Not everyone is comfortable with the news. The Daily Signal reported that former White House press secretary Sean Spicer said this week that given El-Sayed’s connections and statements, he should undergo a formal background check before receiving classified information. Presumably, Spicer was referring to Al-Sayed’s family connections to the Muslim Brotherhood. For many Christians, the moment raises questions about the role of faith in public life, the long American tradition of religious liberty, and the Judeo-Christian roots of the United States. El-Sayed and his colleagues are scheduled to be sworn in at noon on January 3, 2027. The post New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
由霍华德·库珀(英语:Howard Cooper)——阿卜杜勒·赛义德(英语:Abdul Al-Sayed (wikipedia communes)),密歇根州民主党人阿卜杜勒·艾尔·赛义德(英语:Abdul El-Sayed)成为美国参议院首位当选的穆斯林议员,他说他计划在1月份新国会召开时,在《古兰经》上宣誓就职.

42岁的赛义德在11月3日击败共和党人迈克·罗杰斯,成为首位当选参议院议员的美国穆斯林,也是首位在议院任职的流行病学家,据WION News报道. 在NPR的Leila Fadel的采访中,他说:“我很可能在《古兰经》上发誓。

这本《古兰经》, 他指曾由托马斯·杰斐逊拥有的一本副本,基思·埃里森在向国会宣誓就职时曾使用过这份副本,指密歇根大学的一本旧《古兰经》,他称之为该州的第一本。 美国宪法并不要求圣经或任何宗教文本.

在实践中,参议员通常在参议院的地板上共同进行正式宣誓,在个别的仪式宣誓中,圣经开始发挥作用. El-Sayed并未表示他是否会在正式诉讼、典礼或两者中使用《古兰经》, 他还强调,根据IBTimes的说法,他将向美国宪法宣誓。

副总统万斯将宣誓就职, 纵火报称万斯是宪法要求的, 不是每个人都对新闻很满意

《每日信号》报道说,前白宫新闻秘书肖恩·斯皮塞尔(Sean Spicer)本周说,鉴于El-Sayed的联系和声明,他在收到机密信息之前,应当接受正式的背景调查。 Spicer大概指的是Al-Sayed与穆斯林兄弟会的家庭联系。

对许多基督徒来说,此时此刻人们质疑信仰在公共生活中的作用,美国长期的宗教自由传统,以及美国的犹太教-基督教根源. 赛义德和他的同事定于2027年1月3日中午宣誓就职. 密歇根州新参议员表示,

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位勇敢的也门记者讲述了他在访问以色列后，对以色列的看法发生了翻天覆地的变化，这一说法令联合国感到震惊。他得出的结论是，他被教导要相信的关于犹太人的所有事情都是谎言。鲁艾·艾哈迈德应邀 […]  这篇文章《也门记者访问以色列，观点发生巨大转变》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 也门记者访问以色列，观点发生戏剧性变化
content: By Charles Gardner — Luai Ahmed speaking at UN (screenshot YouTube) A brave Yemeni journalist has stunned the United Nations with an account of how his view of Israel has dramatically changed following a visit there. And he was led to the conclusion that everything he has been taught to believe about the Jews is a lie. Luai Ahmed was invited to address the assembly by UN Watch, a non-governmental organisation monitoring the international body’s performance, as the UN Human Rights Council gathered to debate racism. He said: “I grew up in Yemen, where the word that we used for black people is ‘abeed’, which quite literally means ‘slaves’. Racism towards black people in my country is horrifying, but it’s not even the most toxic hatred that I was taught. “The first time I ever heard the word ‘Jew’ was in my local mosque when I was nine years old. At the end of Friday prayers, the Imam said: ‘May Allah kill the Jews and the Zionists’. And I responded alongside thousands of Muslims praying beside me: ‘Ameen’.” Luai then continued: “I was taught that Zionism meant killing Arabs, stealing our land, and destroying Islam. Then October 7th came. Hamas terrorists ‘freed Palestine’ by slaughtering 1,200 Israelis and kidnapping more than 200 people, including a one-year-old child. “Almost everyone in my Arab-Muslim circle celebrated. I didn’t. Instead, as a journalist, I decided to visit the so-called Zionist entity, and I was completely shocked to the core by the lack of apartheid and racism that I experienced. “One day, I got an eye infection. At the hospital, the nurses in reception were Jewish. The doctor treating me was Arab. Is there racism in Israel? Of course. There’s racism everywhere. “But Arabs in Israel aren’t called ‘slaves’. They are doctors, engineers, and party leaders. My experience helped me realise that Zionism really just means the Jewish people’s right to a tiny country. Everything I was taught was a lie.” Quite apart from tipping over the tables of woke left-wing ideology spreading its poisonous antisemitic tentacles across the globe, Luai’s testimony also knocks holes into the escalating pressure on the UK to make reparations for the slave trade, which saw plenty of collaborators in the host countries of those who suffered. And of course, the truth that dare not speak its name – that it was Christians like William Wilberforce who put an end to it! Luai is a great inspiration to fellow journalists like me who long for more of our colleagues to stand up and be counted. Thanks also to David Soakell of Christian Friends of Israel’s Watching Over Zion newsletter, November 5, 2026. The post Yemeni journalist visits Israel, dramatically changes views first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
一位勇敢的也门记者在联合国(YouTube)讲话时, 而他由此得出了这样的结论:他所学的关于犹太人的一切信仰都是谎言.

Luai Ahmed被联合国观察组织邀请在大会上讲话,该组织是监测国际机构业绩的非政府组织,在联合国人权理事会聚集一堂讨论种族主义问题。 他说:“我成长于也门, 我们用来形容黑人的字眼是“有病”的,

对我国黑人的种族主义令人恐惧, “当我九岁时,我第一次听到`犹太人'这个词是在我的地方清真寺。 星期五祷告结束时,教母说:愿真主杀害犹太教徒和犹太复国主义者。

我与数千名穆斯林一同祈祷: 卢艾接着说:“我被告知犹太复国主义意味着杀害阿拉伯人、偷窃我们的土地并摧毁伊斯兰教。 后于十月七日来. 哈马斯恐怖分子屠杀了1 200名以色列人并绑架了200多人,包括一名一岁儿童,从而“解放了巴勒斯坦”。 “我的阿拉伯-穆斯林圈子里几乎每个人都庆祝。

我没有。 相反,作为一名记者,我决定访问所谓的犹太复国主义实体,我对缺乏种族隔离和种族主义感到完全震惊。 “有一天,我眼睛受到感染。 在医院接待的护士是犹太人. 治疗我的医生是阿拉伯人。 以色列是否存在种族主义? 当然 到处都有种族主义。

“但以色列的阿拉伯人并不被称为奴隶。 他们是医生、工程师和党领袖。 我的经验帮助我意识到犹太复国主义只是意味着犹太人民对一个小国的权利。

我所学的一切都是谎言。” 卢艾的证言不仅在醒目的左翼意识形态席上倾出,在全球散布出有毒的反酋长触角,还打入了英国为奴隶贸易提供赔偿的不断升级的压力的洞口,在那些受苦受难者所在的东道国中,有许多合作者。

当然,那个不敢说出自己名字的真理——是威廉·威尔伯福斯这样的基督徒终结了它! 吕艾对像我这样的记者同事来说是一个巨大的灵感,他们渴望有更多的同事站起起来被统计. 也感谢以色列基督教之友的David Soakell,

summary_zh: 文：马克·埃利斯（Mark Ellis）——安珀·斯帕克斯（Amber Sparks）在加利福尼亚州拉古纳海滩长大，对海洋产生了深厚的热爱，这促使她在加州大学伯克利分校学习海洋科学，并在圣地亚哥的斯克里普斯研究所获得了硕士学位。作为蓝纬度基金会的联合创始人，她与业界合作，寻找保护机会，[…]  这篇题为《蝠鲼引导海洋科学家找到失去的鳍》的文章最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 蝠鲼带领海洋科学家找到失去的鳍
content: By Mark Ellis — Amber Sparks (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, especially with the Rigs-to-Reefs program, when oil drilling platforms are decommissioned. “We work with the oil companies to repurpose certain parts of the platform, retrofit it so that it can remain in place and continue to function as an artificial reef,” she told God Reports. Amber’s work has taken her around the world, with many dive experiences and encounters in the ocean with marine life. But there is one story she will never forget. It happened in the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Amber graduated from Scripps Institute and was invited on a research industry cruise with oil company representatives, scientists, and regulators on a liveaboard vessel. At the Flower Garden National Banks, a marine protected area 200 miles offshore, Amber was excited about her first dive, but slightly nervous. “You don’t know what you’re going to see or what this experience is going to be like,” she recalls. Dropping in (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook) Each diver had to jump off the vessel to get in the water. “We’re all geared up with our snorkel, our buoyancy control device, our wetsuit, and fins are the last thing you put on. So, I put on my fins and I jumped off the side of the boat.” “The second that I hit the water, one of my fins fell off, and I looked down and watched as it slowly descended to the bottom.” Amber glanced over at her dive buddy, and said, “I’m gonna go down. I’m going down.” Normally she would wait for her dive partner and they would go down together, but in this case, she thought, “I can’t (wait). I gotta go get my fin.” So Amber slowly began to descend to the bottom, about 60 feet below the ocean surface. “I felt completely lost. I was in a completely new area. I never dove before, and now I only had one fin.” She realized there were major currents that could have moved her fin in any direction. “I realized I can’t really swim with just one fin. So now not only am I at depth, but I’m handicapped with just one fin, and I started to feel pretty nervous.” It would probably take her 10 minutes to get back the surface, with safety stops. At the moment before panic set in, she looked upward and saw an amazing sight. It was a giant manta ray, with wings extending at least 10 feet. “Its wingspan was double mine. Its arms were out, and it was coming up over the side of a reef. “I’ve never seen a manta ray like this before. It totally took my breath away, it was so magnificent.” Another manta ray (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) She noted that manta rays are known in the ocean community to be “majestic, God-connected creatures with an understanding maybe beyond what humans can fully comprehend. They see the world and feel it in another way,” she notes. Mantas have the largest known brain of any fish. Their brains are large in absolute terms and relative to body size, which is also true of elephants, dolphins, and people. Their brains have enlarged areas associated with intelligence, vision, and motor coordination, and some of their brain cells are more like those in birds and mammals than in other fish.(1) As the manta ray drew close to Amber, she had an unusual communication experience. “I felt this sense where it said, ‘I want you to follow me. I’m going to help you find your fin.’ Amber Sparks Amber’s diving partner had just descended next to her, and they both began to swim after the manta. “I was barely making it, following this manta ray across the reef. At this point, I was so excited to see a manta ray. I kind of forgot about being handicapped, and I was just trying to go as fast as I can to keep up with it. Then Amber got the sur
content_zh:
由Mark Ellis——Amber Sparks(蓝色纬度基金会Facebook專頁) 成长于加利福尼亚州拉古纳海滩,Amber Sparks发展了对海洋的深爱,这让她在UC伯克利学习海洋科学,并在圣地亚哥的斯克里普斯研究所获得硕士学位.

作为蓝色纬度基金会的联合创始人,她与业界合作寻找保护机会,特别是在石油钻探平台退役时与Rigs-to-Reefs计划合作. 她告诉God Reports, “我们与石油公司合作,

Amber的作品将她带到世界各地, 但有一个故事 她永远不会忘记。 它在墨西哥湾发生后不久,琥珀从斯克里普斯研究所毕业,并被邀请与石油公司代表,科学家和监管者乘坐一艘活船上进行研究产业巡航.

在离岸200英里的海洋保护区"花园国家银行"(The Flower Garden National Banks),琥珀对她的首次潜水感到兴奋,但略为紧张. “你不知道自己会看到什么, 降入(蓝纬基金会脸书) 每个潜水员必须跳下船才能下水.

title: Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success
summary: By Brian Nixon — While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” […]  The post  Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh:
布莱恩·尼克松(Brian Nixon)——在德克萨斯州休斯敦拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利研究中心等会议时,我转而请图书管理员莎伦·克夫兰(Sharon Cofran)和执行主任Dr.

David Fleming说,“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利对拉尼尔代表他取得的成就将感到非常高兴。” Lanier的第六届年度John Warwick Montgomery讲座系列:大成功首次出现在"上帝的报告"上。
title_zh: 拉尼尔第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利系列讲座：圆满成功
content: John Warwick Montgomery By Brian Nixon — While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. As I reflected on the weekend, I was reminded of the Festschrift Christianity for the Tough-Minded , a collection of scholarly essays honoring Montgomery’s life and ministry. Like that volume, the Lanier lecture series brought together

约翰·沃威克·蒙哥马利·由布赖恩·尼克松(John Warwick Montgomery By Brian Nixon)——在德克萨斯州休斯敦拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃威克·蒙哥马利研究中心等会议时,我转而请图书管理员莎伦·克夫兰(Sharon Cofran)和执行主任Dr.

大卫·弗莱明(David Fleming)说道,“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(John Warwick Montgomery)将非常满意拉尼尔代表他取得的成就。” 蒙哥马利与C.S.的书信

刘易斯和他的大律师礼服为他杰出的个人收藏的上千本书所提供,莱尼尔为基督教世界提供了令人赞叹的敬意,他是20世纪和21世纪伟大的基督教知识分子之一。 1931年生于约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(d.

2024年是一位杰出的基督教道歉学家,神学家,律师和学者,他的非凡生涯跨越了多个学科. 蒙哥马利拥有众多学术学位,包括神学,哲学和法学等博士学位,他通过历史证据,法律推理,和哲学论证,为基督教辩护而获得国际承认.

他的有影响力的著作,包括"历史与基督教"(History and Christian, Faith Founded on Fact),以及"过去的形状"(The Shape of the Past)等,帮助确立了对基督教古典主义的严格处理方法. 无论是在大学里讲道,辩论怀疑论,还是实践法律,蒙哥马利都坚持认为基督教不仅仅是主观信仰的问题,而是建立在历史现实和理性调查基础上的信仰.

在图书馆停留, 第六期年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利讲座系列是一次由杰出的思想家,充满热情的基督徒,以及智力参与演讲的巡回演出.

这次集会不仅是纪念蒙哥马利的生平,还代表着他思想遗产的延续:坚信基督教能够经受住严肃的审视,并为人生最深刻的问题提供令人信服的答案.

马克·拉尼尔,南茜·皮尔西,保罗·古尔德,亚当·弗朗西斯科,和迈克尔·霍顿 从律师和慈善家马克·拉尼尔主持的开场小组讨论到保罗·古尔德博士关于世界观的深思熟虑的介绍,然后是克雷格·帕通律师关于法学学说讲座,一个主题以明确无误的方式出现: 基督教是一种合理的信仰.

这些演讲反映了蒙哥马利自己对道具的跨学科方法:基督教信仰和知识调查不必是对手。 事实上,基督教传统长期以来一直坚持认为,信仰和理性是追求真理的补充途径。 次日继续进行这种丰富的知识探索.

Nancy Pearcey教授谈到了围绕真理的问题,摧毁了各种现代意识形态,而Adam Francisco博士则对伊斯兰历史和信仰提供了翔实的概述,帮助参与者更好地了解了世界上最大的宗教之一。 由Dr.A.先生作主旨发言。

迈克尔·霍顿研究了帮助那些认为是“精神上而非宗教上”的当代社会日益扩大的阶层的挑战。 Horton的演讲强调了在一种对宗教机构越来越有怀疑的文化中传播历史性的基督教真理的重要性,而这种文化往往对精神意义很感兴趣。 医生

迈克尔·霍顿 星期天早上,拉尼尔的创始人马克·拉尼尔(Mark Lanier)在圣经扫盲班期间接待了许多参与者,在那里他继续与迈克尔·霍顿进行对话.

讲座、讨论和访谈共同显示了基督教奖学金的广度,以及深思熟虑的学说在怀疑主义、宗教多元化和文化不确定性的时代的持续相关性。

正如我在周末所回顾的那样,人们提醒我为强硬派而信奉费斯奇里夫基督教,这是一本纪念蒙哥马利生平和部的学术论文集。 和那卷一样,拉尼尔系列讲座也聚集在一起

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——在第二次世界大战南太平洋的一场海战中，一名日本水兵所在的驱逐舰被美国人击沉，他的大多数战友都淹死了。令人惊奇的是，尽管鱼雷官新谷通晴与其他人一起被卷入波涛之下，随着战舰的沉没，但他却奇迹般地在这场1942年的灾难中幸存下来。（只有18名……）  这篇文章《二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”
content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
查尔斯·加德纳编著: 当一艘日本水手的驱逐舰在二战南太平洋战役中被美国人击沉时,大部分同伴溺毙. 令人惊奇的是,尽管随着船只的下沉,他与其他人一起被吸在海浪下,但鱼雷军官Michiharu Shinya却不知何故幸免于1942年的灾难。 (200人的船员中只有18人这样做).

但他宁愿死在那个时候,因为他的族人被灌输相信被俘虏是可耻的. 然而,他受了重伤,但被医护人员喂养。

在时间上,他被接了起来,最终被带到新西兰惠灵顿附近的费瑟斯顿(Featherston)的战俘营,在那里他将度过接下来的三年,正如唐·斯蒂芬斯在他的励志书"战争与格蕾丝"(福音出版社,10Publishing的印记)中记载的那样.

信也和同狱囚犯受到很大程度的善待(与盟军囚犯经常在日本人手中遭受的酷刑形成鲜明对比). 在圣诞节用礼物淋浴 一个他一无所知的宴会 看起来特别奇怪

然而,在一些囚犯要求精神帮助和提供日本圣经后,他决心不再接受基督教教义的 " 接纳 " 。 直到他看到一篇题为“为胜利而悲伤”的文章,作者在文章中引用了一位“赫布鲁先知”的话:“那些希望主复活的人。 他们将像鹰一样飞翔,

他们将奔驰,而不会疲倦,他们将走路,而不会晕倒。 这给他留下了深刻的印象,他下定决心要找出它来自何处. 假设它来自旧约,他开始阅读圣经,从创世纪第一章开始. 最终,在他的喜悦中,他发现深刻的文字来自先知以赛亚的经典(第40章第31节).

在搜索中略微浮出水面后,他发现自己患上了疟疾,一位朋友给他带了一本小册子,名为《原因》,解释救世之路。 难民营的牧师Hessell Troughton牧师曾是日本的传教士, 信也加入了其他人的圣经研究,来到了了解和热爱耶稣作为他的救世主.

这种“完全自由”现在统治了他的生活,监狱变成了他所称的“地球上独一无二的天堂”。 他从此之后再也没有回头看,并且确信他的战后召唤将会为他的主服务. 当他最终回家时,家人震惊地看到他活着,因为他被报道为阵亡.

他还给抓捕者取了一个假名,因为被假定是落入敌人手中的耻辱。 在东京和美国多年的神学研究之后,信也后来成为一名牧师和多产作家和翻译。 他逐渐相信,《旧约》表明了罪恶是“人类的最终问题”,并明确指出基督是答案。

在试图理解为什么如此少的日本人成为基督徒时,他感到部分是由于他们的自豪感,因为他们相信他们是优越的种族。

至于他在新西兰度过的三个圣诞节,作者Don Stephens写道:"在他收到的所有礼物中,他最珍视的一件是`上帝在耶稣基督中无限和深厚的恩惠与和平 ' 。 日本战俘在营地发现「自由」,

title_zh: 在西部明星的阴影下：格罗弗·刘易斯、拉里·麦克默特里和文字的胜利
content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. content_zh:
与《格罗弗·刘易斯读者:短草中的辉煌与西部之星》,拉里·麦克默特里的最新传记, 手持,我装载我的卡车并前往德克萨斯州阿彻城, 由我的妻子梅兰妮和我们的朋友埃利奥特陪同。 阿彻城当然是麦克默特里国家,一个通过美国最著名的小说家之一的文学想象而成名的德克萨斯小镇.

在之前访问Archer城后, 我对McMurtry的信仰(或缺乏信仰)有一番兴趣, 这一次,我转而关注有天赋的记者、评论家和诗人格罗弗·刘易斯,他在大学时代的生活与麦克默特里的生活交织在一起。

然而,刘易斯的故事并非从文学成就开始,而是从几乎难以想象的悲剧开始. 他从小就经历了父母的惨痛损失,当时他的父亲谋杀了他的母亲,随后被他即将死亡的妻子或在场的其他人用同一把枪射杀。 刘易斯才八岁 很难想象一个更可怕的开端。

然而,刘易斯最终没有让这场悲剧成为他的全部故事,而是通过文学找到了声音. 也许他命中注定的卡片 给他写了很多东西 或写作成为他理解世界的方式, 这个世界已经揭示了它的残酷性,还为时过早。

刘易斯在自传诗“Hillbilly Song”中写道 : “ 你曾经问过我,Ann/Over咖啡随着谈话而变得冷淡,在你妈妈的雨滴/住所里,他们是谁,他们在无气息的年代/在野外时如何。 ” 对刘易斯来说,那些早年的确很狂野. 但它们也是他的文学想象最终会成长的土壤.

1934年出生于德克萨斯州的"言语生活"(A Life in Words Born in Texas),格罗弗·刘易斯(Grover Lewis)成为美国新闻业中一个有特色的代言人,特别是通过他对1960年代和1970年代迅速变化的地貌的文化批评和报道.

他以尖锐的观察,文学的才华,以及能够捕捉美国文化的个性和矛盾而闻名,即使他偶尔在讲述中伸张真理. 他的作品出现在包括滚石公司在内的著名出版物中,他的报道帮助他树立了自己作为有见地,有时剪切流行文化观察者的声誉.

然而,刘易斯不只是一名记者。 他是一位诗人和文学家,一个懂得文字可以比传递信息更有用的人. 它们可以揭示人类的状况,暴露其矛盾,甚至可能提供某种治疗方法。

Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) 继续“Hillbilly Song,” 刘易斯思考道:“最后,无气息和干燥的嘴唇/在蓝色的暗处私欲下,我们都躺在一起——/我的母亲、父亲、他们的死亡/梦想,我这个未出生的囚犯儿子......” 这些台词有些困扰。 死者仍然在场。 过去拒绝消失。

而诗人,即使作为一个成年人,似乎也与塑造他进入世界的环境相搏. 然而,写作本身就暗示了另一种情况:拒绝保持沉默。 两德克萨斯州立大学,两条文学道路刘易斯州立大学和拉里·麦克默特里(英语:Larry McMurtry)在1950年代作为北德克萨斯州立学院,即现在的北德克萨斯大学的学生跨过道路.

两人都是年轻的德克萨斯人,被吸引到文学和写字的可能性. 他们的友谊是在共同的知识环境中发展起来的,这种环境鼓励阅读,对话,追求文学野心.

尽管他们的职业生涯最终走的是不同的道路——小说、剧本和文学名人、刘易斯新闻、诗歌和文化批评——但他们对美国生活的复杂性有着共同的兴趣。 麦克默特里和刘易斯在大学期间(ChatGPT)都拥有超越德克萨斯州和美国西部神话的能力,认识到孤独,凝视

title: Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage
summary: By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own […]  The post  Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位犹太籍陆军外科医生对一名年轻士兵的勇气感到惊叹，这名士兵在美国内战（1861-65）的葛底斯堡战役中身受重伤。为了挽救这个男孩的生命，马克斯·罗斯瓦利（Max Rossvally）博士不得不截肢，截掉了他的一条腿和一条胳膊。但这改变了他自己……  这篇题为《犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归向耶稣》的文章  最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归信耶稣
content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. The post Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
牧师彼得·科隆在他的故事电影"查尔斯·加德纳"(By Charles Gardner)中描绘了罗斯瓦利少校——一位犹太军队外科医生对美国内战期间格底斯堡战役(1861-65)中一名年轻士兵严重受伤的勇气感到惊讶. Max Rossvally医生被迫截肢, 但这改变了他自己的生活。

对于17岁的Drummer Boy — — 年龄太小,无法承担前线任务 — — 拒绝氯仿或白兰地来消磨疼痛。 查理·科尔森选择了信任耶稣,他的主和救世主.

这位医生是一名陆军少校和正统犹太人,对男孩的勇敢以及他大胆地宣布对基督的信仰,恳求军官(他知道是犹太人)相信耶稣是可以理解的,因为他也是犹太弥赛亚。 然而,马克思被动摇僵硬,陷入了巨大的困境,因为他一直被教导要憎恨耶稣.

他的宗族曾否认他是一个 " 骗子 " 和假的弥赛亚。 Charlie在几天后就去世了,显然更关心医生的永恒命运,而不是他自己痛苦地离开这一生。 10年后,马克思发现自己在纽约的理发师座椅上再次被敦促信任耶稣.

在解释了福音之后,理发师答应为他祈祷,并说每当他与一个犹太人接触时,他觉得有义务将他介绍给前来寻找“迷失的以色列羊”的人(Matthew 10:6)。

外科医生随后登上火车在华盛顿举行商务会议,报纸的广告将他引向 " 复活 " 服务,传教士重复了他从理发师和男孩士兵那里听到的信息,使他流泪。

他在家里苦苦地祈祷了一段时间,他首先想到,如果他接受基督,他将反对他所知道的所有建议和教导,更不用说整个犹太社区了。 但他最终确信耶稣确实是"旧约预言"的实现(特别是创世纪49:10,米迦5:2和以赛亚7:14).

他就祈祷说:易卜拉欣、易司哈格、叶尔孤白的主啊! 你知道我对这件事很真诚 如果耶稣基督是上帝之子,那么今晚把他告诉我,我将接受他为我的弥赛亚。” 一场漫长的战斗随之而来,但他的疑虑最终被欢乐和幸福所取代,因为他称赞上帝找到了真正的希洛,以色列统治者和埃马纽埃尔.

但他要付出高昂的代价,跟随基督的所有人一样。 他的妻子抛弃了他;他的父母抛弃了他。 但是,他从未放弃过希望,因为他不断祈祷和联系家人。 在54天后,他的妻子作为耶稣的门徒加入了他,在时间上,他的女儿也成为了信徒.

但他的儿子与他断绝关系多年,直到他最终与他的大地父和天父都和解. 在他来到基督的大约18个月之后的一段非凡续集中,马克思在战场上遇见了那些年前他死去的年轻病人的母亲科尔森夫人.

他怀着极大的喜悦,得以分享她儿子如何使他踏上基督辉煌未来的道路,这就是触摸世界各地的生活,包括我的家乡英格兰约克郡. 事实上,他来到利兹居住,向那里的犹太社区伸出援手,并被埋在城内的草坪林墓地.

我的一个爱尔兰朋友科林·内文参观了这个坟墓,其中包括医生颂歌"I am Coming Soon"的节录,并且能够把马克思的故事复制给看守人,因此在1892年去世后一个多世纪的福音派传承下来,享年64岁.

一部54分钟的电影 — — Rossvally: 从Synagogue到救世主 — 已经在DVD上制作,显然可以在网上订购. 在目睹病人的勇气首次出现在上帝的报告之后,

summary_zh: 安德肋·邓乐是天主教会今天（星期二）纪念的圣人，与他在越南因信仰而殉道的另外116位烈士一同受纪念。如果有人问你今天纪念哪位圣人，请看这里。
title_zh: 安德肋·邓·乐，11月24日圣人：这位圣人在十七至十九世纪间因信仰而在越南殉道
content: San Andrés Dung Lac es el santo que la Iglesia católica recuerda hoy, martes, junto a otros 116 mártires que murieron por su fe en Vietnam. Si alguien te pregunta por el santoral de esta jornada, aquí tienes la historia de un sacerdote nacido en la pobreza que no quiso renunciar a lo que creía. Detrás de este nombre hay una persecución que se alargó más de dos siglos, con cifras que impresionan y con protagonistas de tres nacionalidades. Te lo contamos de forma sencilla y con las fechas que conviene tener claras, para que sepas quién fue y por qué su memoria sigue viva en el calendario cada 24 de noviembre. San Andrés Dung Lac, un sacerdote nacido hacia 1795 Trần An Dũng nació hacia 1795 en Bac Ninh, en el norte del país, en el seno de una familia humilde. Su historia empieza como la de tantos niños de su época: con muy pocas posibilidades y un futuro incierto. Una infancia marcada por la pobreza San Andrés Dung Lac vino al mundo en un hogar tan pobre que sus padres lo confiaron a un catequista católico para asegurar su supervivencia. Con él recibió formación cristiana y fue bautizado con el nombre de Andrés. Hoy la Iglesia lo nombra con los dos nombres juntos, Dung y Lac, y ese detalle tiene una explicación que verás enseguida. Es una pista de la vida que llevaban los cristianos de su entorno: con discreción y con miedo a ser descubiertos por las autoridades. De catequizado a sacerdote en 1823 El joven estudió latín y chino y se ordenó sacerdote en 1823. Para proteger su fe y poder seguir ayudando a su comunidad adoptó el nombre de Lac, aunque no consiguió pasar desapercibido para siempre. Fue detenido en varias ocasiones y llegó a ser liberado tras pagar un rescate sus propios feligreses. El martirio de San Andrés el 21 de diciembre de 1839 Durante el reinado del emperador Minh Mạng, que comenzó en 1821, ser cristiano podía costar la vida. A finales de 1839 el sacerdote fue arrestado por tercera vez, junto a Pedro Thi, también sacerdote. Ninguno de los dos aceptó renegar de su fe. La sentencia fue de muerte y se cumplió por decapitación el 21 de diciembre de 1839, a las afueras de Hanói, en la puerta de Cau-Giay. Estos son los datos esenciales sobre San Andrés que te ayudan a situarlo en el tiempo: - San Andrés nació hacia 1795 en Bac Ninh. - Se ordenó sacerdote en 1823 y fue arrestado por tercera vez a finales de 1839. - Murió decapitado en Hanói el 21 de diciembre de 1839. - León XIII lo beatificó el 24 de noviembre de 1900, el mismo día del año en que hoy se le recuerda. San Andrés se convirtió así en la figura más conocida de todo el grupo de mártires vietnamitas, y por eso el conjunto lleva su nombre. Por qué no se celebra el día de su muerte La Iglesia no lo recuerda el 21 de diciembre, sino el 24 de noviembre, una jornada que comparte con todo el grupo de mártires. Así, cada año el santoral reúne en una sola memoria a obispos, sacerdotes, religiosos y laicos que murieron en momentos y lugares diferentes. 117 mártires de tres países y más de 100.000 víctimas El grupo que encabeza San Andrés reúne a 117 mártires canonizados por Juan Pablo II el 19 de junio de 1988. No todos eran vietnamitas: eran 96 vietnamitas, 11 españoles y 10 franceses, entre obispos, sacerdotes, religiosos y laicos. Una persecución de más de dos siglos Los edictos contra los cristianos en Vietnam se sucedieron entre 1645 y 1886, con 53 decretos en total. Se habla de hasta 113.000 creyentes martirizados, y otras estimaciones elevan la cifra a unos 130.000 fallecidos. Del beato al santo, paso a paso El primer grupo de 64 mártires fue beatificado por León XIII en 1900. Hubo cuatro beatificaciones distintas entre 1900 y 1951, y todos los mártires fueron canonizados en tiempos de Juan Pablo II. Por eso los 117 comparten una misma fecha en el santoral. Del siglo XVII al XIX Los 117 mártires murieron en distintos momentos de esa larga persecución, que abarca desde el siglo XVII hasta el XIX.
